w4-800372.blurb: The War of Jenkins' Ear (1739-1748), which merged with the War of Austrian Succession, saw British forces attempt to capture Spanish colonial territories in the Caribbean and Central America. The British attack on Cartagena de Indias in 1741 was repulsed by Spanish forces under Blas de Lezo. The dataset records Spanish to British territorial shifts around coordinates -84, 13.5 (coastal Central America/Nicaragua area) between 1741-1744, consistent with British raiding activities along the Mosquito Coast and temporary gains in the region during this conflict.

citations.label: War of the Austrian Succession - Wikipedia

w4-800374.name: Nader Shah's invasion of India: cession of territories west of the Indus
w4-800374.blurb: Afsharid ruler Nader Shah invaded Mughal India in 1738–1739, sacking Delhi in March 1739. Under the resulting settlement, Emperor Muhammad Shah ceded all territories west of the Indus — including Sindh, Kabul, Ghazni, and Peshawar — to the Afsharid Empire (Nader returned lands east of the Indus). The actual cession occurred in 1739; the dataset's 1741-1744 window reflects continued Afsharid consolidation and mapping lag.

citations.label: Nader Shah's invasion of India – Wikipedia

w4-800375.name: Nader Shah's Offensive in the Ottoman–Persian War – Early Persian Gains
w4-800375.blurb: In 1743 Nader Shah declared war on the Ottomans and launched a major offensive into Ottoman Iraq, capturing Kirkuk and Arbil and besieging Mosul (September–October 1743). Persia made significant inroads into Ottoman Mesopotamia and the Caucasus frontier (~44.7E/37.7N) during 1741–1744 before the stalemate. Window [1741,1744], date 1743; territory from Ottoman Empire to Afsharid Iran.

w4-800380.name: Russo-Swedish War (War of the Hats) - Peace of Turku (1743)
w4-800380.blurb: The Swedish Hat party launched the Russo-Swedish War in 1741 to reclaim territories lost in the Great Northern War. Russia rapidly overwhelmed Swedish forces in Finland ('Lesser Wrath'), occupying the entire country. The Peace of Turku (1743) returned most of Finland to Sweden but required cession of additional southeastern Finnish territory (near lng 28.9, lat 62.1) to Russia. The dataset shows Swedish-to-Russian transfer in 1741-1744, matching this war and settlement.

w4-800383.name: Collapse of Afsharid Iran - emergence of Caucasian Khanates
w4-800383.blurb: The assassination of Nader Shah on 20 June 1747 triggered the rapid disintegration of Afsharid Iran. The Caucasian territories - comprising modern Azerbaijan, Armenia, and parts of Dagestan - broke away into numerous independent or semi-independent khanates (Baku, Shirvan, Karabakh, Ganja, Nakhchivan, Yerevan, etc.). These Khanates of the Caucasus operated autonomously until being reincorporated under the Qajar dynasty or conquered by Russia in the early 19th century.

citations.label: Division of the Afsharid Empire - Wikipedia

w4-800384.name: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748): Lorraine restored
w4-800384.blurb: During the War of the Austrian Succession France again occupied parts of Lorraine. The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (18 October 1748) required France to restore its conquests; Lorraine (coord 6.2E/48.8N) was then governed by ex-king Stanisław I until his death in 1766, when it reverted to France. The dataset's 1744–1748 'France → Duchy of Lorraine' reversion matches the peace terms.

citations.label: War of the Austrian Succession – Wikipedia

w4-800387.name: Khanate of Khiva expansion after Nadir Shah's death
w4-800387.blurb: After Nadir Shah's assassination in 1747, the Khanate of Khiva reasserted independence (it had been occupied 1740–1746) and expanded into the lower Amu Darya/Khwarezm region (64.6,40.9) at the expense of the weakened Khanate of Bukhara, which was in disarray after Nadir Shah's conquest. This matches the from→to (Khanate of Bukhara → Khanate of Khiva) in the 1744–1748 window.

w4-800388.name: Khanate of Khiva independence after Nadir Shah's assassination
w4-800388.blurb: Nadir Shah of Afsharid Iran conquered Khiva in 1740; after his assassination in June 1747 his empire fragmented and the Khanate of Khiva (Khwarezm, lng 59.5, lat 39.8) regained effective independence by 1748 under a new khan. The Afsharid-to-Khiva transfer fits the py1744-y1748 window.

citations.label: Division of the Afsharid Empire — Wikipedia

w4-800391.name: Karim Khan Zand's consolidation of western Iran after Nader Shah's death
w4-800391.blurb: Following Nader Shah's assassination in 1747, Karim Khan Zand emerged as the dominant power in western and southern Iran after defeating rival Afsharid and Zand-aligned claimants in a series of civil conflicts through the late 1740s to early 1750s. By c. 1750–1752 he controlled the heartland of Iran around Fars and Isfahan, displacing Afsharid authority.

w4-800392.name: Sulu Sultanate expansion into NE Borneo / Tidung campaigns
w4-800392.blurb: Between 1746 and 1748, Sultan Azim ud-Din I of Sulu conducted punitive expeditions against the Tidung people of northeastern Borneo (near modern Tarakan, 117.2E, 3.5N), then within the Bulungan sphere. The Sulu campaigns reconsolidated the Tarakan chieftain's allegiance to Sulu at Bulungan's expense, though overlapping claims persisted until Dutch annexation.

w4-800393.name: Rise of Karim Khan Zand – founding of the Zand Dynasty
w4-800393.blurb: After Nader Shah's assassination in 1747, Persia fractured. Karim Khan Zand progressively eliminated rivals, defeating Ali Mardan Khan, and emerged as undisputed regent (vakil) of most of Iran by 1751-52, founding the Zand Dynasty with its capital at Shiraz; the Afsharids were confined to Khorasan. From 'Afsharid Iran' to 'Zand Dynasty' at central-Iran coordinates; window py=1748, y=1752 fits.

w4-800394.name: Foundation of the Durrani Empire by Ahmad Shah Durrani
w4-800394.blurb: Following Nader Shah's assassination on 20 June 1747, his eastern territories rapidly fragmented. Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) convened a loya jirga at Kandahar, was elected Afghan king, and founded the Durrani Empire. He rapidly seized Kandahar, Ghazni, Kabul, and Peshawar, and by 1750-1752 took Herat and Mashhad from Afsharid control. This process transferred the eastern Afsharid territories to the new Durrani state.

w4-800396.name: Elimination of customs border between Hetmanate and Russia (1752)
w4-800396.blurb: In 1750, Empress Elizabeth of Russia revived the Hetmanate for Kyrylo Rozumovsky, but in 1752 eliminated the customs border between the Hetmanate and Russia, a significant step toward full integration. The Zaporozhian Cossack territories were incrementally absorbed into the Russian imperial system during this period. Full abolition of the Hetmanate came in 1764 under Catherine II, and the Zaporozhian Sich was destroyed in 1775.

w4-800397.name: Ayutthaya occupies Tenasserim during the Burmese civil war; Konbaung founded
w4-800397.blurb: During the Burmese civil war of 1740–1752 the Mon Hanthawaddy kingdom overthrew the Toungoo dynasty; Ayutthaya exploited the chaos to occupy the Tenasserim coast (coord 98.3E/15.5N). The Konbaung dynasty was founded in February 1752 by Alaungpaya, who by 1757 reunified Burma and contested Siamese gains. The dataset's 'Konbaung → Ayutthaya' shift in 1748–1752 reflects Siamese territorial control in Tenasserim during this period; event real and correctly dated.

w4-800402.name: Guaraní War and Portuguese Seizure of the Seven Jesuit Missions
w4-800402.blurb: The 1750 Treaty of Madrid transferred seven Jesuit mission settlements east of the Uruguay River from Spain to Portugal. When the Guaraní inhabitants refused to relocate, a combined Spanish-Portuguese force fought the Guaraní War (1754–1757), culminating in the Battle of Caiboaté (10 February 1756) in which over 1,500 Guaraní were killed. Portugal occupied the Misiones Orientales until the 1761 Treaty of El Pardo reversed the transfer.

citations.label: Jesuit missions among the Guaraní – Wikipedia

w4-800407.name: Konbaung conquest of Lower Burma: fall of Pegu (1757)
w4-800407.blurb: The Konbaung dynasty, founded by Alaungpaya in 1752, rapidly conquered Lower Burma: the Irrawaddy delta (May 1755), Thanlyin (July 1756), and the Hanthawaddy capital Pegu (May 1757), ending the Mon kingdom and the Restored Toungoo remnants and reunifying Burma. Matches the First Toungoo Empire (Toungoo-affiliated) → Konbaung transfer in the 1752-1757 window.

w4-800409.name: Ahmad Shah Durrani's subjugation of Badakhshan
w4-800409.blurb: Ahmad Shah Durrani's armies subdued the regions north of the Hindu Kush in the early 1750s, taking Balkh and Badakhshan around 1751. Badakhshan was not absorbed directly but governed by the local ruler Mir Sultan Shah, who acknowledged Durrani suzerainty while retaining real autonomy, even campaigning against neighbouring Chitral. The territory had been under independent local mountain dynasties, not the Dzungar sphere, before this submission.

w4-800410.name: Qing destruction of the Dzungar Khanate; Bukhara claims Badakhshan/Tashkent corridor
w4-800410.blurb: The Qing destruction of the Dzungar Khanate in 1755-1757 removed the dominant steppe power in Central Asia, and the Qing formally annexed most Dzungar lands as Xinjiang by 1759. In the Badakhshan-Pamir borderlands, however, it was Ahmad Shah Durrani's expansion that brought Balkh and Badakhshan under Afghan suzerainty around 1751, governed through local mirs. There was no substantive Bukharan annexation of a Dzungar-held Badakhshan corridor; Bukhara's reach did not extend into these mountain principalities.

w4-800415.name: Battle of Plassey
w4-800415.blurb: On 23 June 1757, Robert Clive's British East India Company force of ~3,000 defeated Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah's army of ~50,000 at Plassey, aided by the defection of Mir Jafar. The Nawab was captured and executed; Mir Jafar was installed as a British puppet. This transferred effective control of Bengal to the East India Company,

w4-800416.name: Karim Khan Zand's Rise and Conquest of Central and Southern Iran
w4-800416.blurb: After Nader Shah's assassination in 1747 the Afsharid Empire fragmented. Karim Khan Zand, chief of the Zand Lur tribe, consolidated power from his base in Fars, defeating rival Afsharid pretenders and warlords through the 1750s. By approximately 1757-1760 he had driven Afsharid authority back to Khorasan and established Zand control over central, southern, and western Iran with Shiraz as his capital. He governed as Vakil (regent) supporting the nominal Safavid figurehead Ismail III.

w4-800424.name: French invasion and occupation of Hanover (1757)
w4-800424.blurb: In July 1757 French forces under d'Estrées defeated the Hanoverian Army of Observation at Hastenbeck and occupied most of the Electorate of Hanover, formalised by the Convention of Klosterzeven (10 September 1757). French forces operated in Hanover until driven back across the Rhine by 1762. The window (1757-1762) and coordinates (8.7, 51.5) match the occupied region.

w4-800427.name: Konbaung Dynasty conquest of Lan Na / Chiang Mai under Naungdawgyi
w4-800427.blurb: After most Lan Na principalities submitted to Alaungpaya in 1757, Chiang Mai remained independent under Ong Chan. King Naungdawgyi of the Konbaung Dynasty sent General Abaya Kamani with 7,000 troops in 1762; after a siege, Chiang Mai fell in 1763 and its population was largely deported to Burma. The territory (lat 19.2, lng 99.1) was thus reincorporated into Burmese control after about 35 years of effective independence.

w4-800429.name: Seven Years' War – Austrian/Allied Occupation of Prussian Territory
w4-800429.blurb: During the Seven Years' War (1756–1763) the Habsburg-led coalition scored early successes against Frederick the Great, with Austrian forces occupying parts of Silesia and adjacent Prussian territory (~15.1E/51N) in 1757–1762 and Russia briefly occupying Berlin (1760). Window [1757,1762] spans the height of allied gains before Frederick's recovery and the 1762 Russian withdrawal. Date 1757.

w4-800432.name: Sikh Misls expand across Punjab after Ahmad Shah Durrani's invasions (1757-1762)
w4-800432.blurb: Ahmad Shah Durrani's repeated invasions of India (1747-1769) progressively dismantled Mughal administration in Punjab. After sacking Delhi in 1757 and installing his son Timur as governor, Afghan control over the province proved tenuous in the face of Sikh Misl resistance. By 1761 the Sikhs had declared Jassa Singh Ahluwalia 'king of Lahore.' Despite the devastating Vadda Ghallughara massacre of c. 25,000 Sikhs in 1762, the Sikhs rebounded quickly, and by the mid-1760s had effectively replaced Mughal authority across much of Punjab. The data entry (Mughal Empire to Sikh Confederacy, py=1757, y=1762) reflects this transition.

citations.label: Indian campaign of Ahmad Shah Durrani - Wikipedia

w4-800437.name: Heraclius II unites Kartli and Kakheti (1762)
w4-800437.blurb: On the death of King Teimuraz II of Kartli on 8 January 1762, his son Heraclius II — king of Kakheti since 1744 — inherited the throne of Kartli, uniting the two eastern Georgian kingdoms for the first time since 1463 to form the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti. Heraclius II ruled the unified kingdom until his death in 1798.

w4-800438.name: Treaty of Paris (1763) – Spain cedes Florida to Britain in exchange for Havana
w4-800438.blurb: The Seven Years' War ended with the Treaty of Paris (10 February 1763), by which Spain ceded all of Florida to Great Britain in exchange for the return of Havana, which Britain had captured in 1762. Britain organised the territory into East Florida and West Florida, marking a major transfer of Spanish colonial territory in North America to the British Colonial Empire.

w4-800439.name: Treaty of Paris (1763) transfers New France to Britain
w4-800439.blurb: The Treaty of Paris signed on 10 February 1763 ended the Seven Years' War. France ceded New France (Canada) and all lands east of the Mississippi River to Britain, and secretly ceded Louisiana west of the Mississippi to Spain. This was the single largest colonial transfer in North American history and ended over 150 years of French presence. The atlas coordinate points to upstate New York, consistent with the former New France–British border zone.

w4-800441.name: Royal Proclamation of 1763 establishes British Indian Reserve
w4-800441.blurb: Following France's cession of New France in the Treaty of Paris (10 February 1763), Britain issued the Royal Proclamation of 7 October 1763, declaring lands west of the Appalachians an Indian Reserve and forbidding colonial settlement there. This transferred administrative claim over Haudenosaunee-held territory near the Great Lakes from the former French sphere to regulated British Crown authority, reflected in the atlas as a 1762–1763 Haudenosaunee-to-British transfer.

w4-800444.name: Treaty of Saint Petersburg (1762) — Russia returns East Prussia to Prussia
w4-800444.blurb: When Empress Elizabeth of Russia died in January 1762, her successor Peter III sought peace, signing the Treaty of Saint Petersburg on 5 May 1762. Russia restored all occupied Prussian territories, including East Prussia, without concessions — the 'Miracle of the House of Brandenburg.' The Treaty of Hubertusburg (1763) confirmed Prussian sovereignty. Matches Russian Empire -> Kingdom of Prussia in [1762,1763].

w4-800445.name: Treaty of Hubertusburg ends the Seven Years War
w4-800445.blurb: The Treaty of Hubertusburg, signed 15 February 1763 between Prussia, the Habsburg Monarchy, and Saxony, ended the Seven Years' War in central Europe. Austria renounced all claims to Silesia, confirming Prussian control, with positions returning to the status quo ante bellum. The data window 1762-1763 captures the confirmation of Prussian control over Silesia.

w4-800446.name: Vadda Ghalughara – Ahmad Shah Durrani's Sixth Invasion (1762)
w4-800446.blurb: In February 1762, Ahmad Shah Durrani led his sixth invasion of India, inflicting the 'Vadda Ghalughara' (Great Massacre) on the Sikh Confederacy at the Battle of Kup (5 February 1762), killing an estimated 10,000–30,000 Sikhs. He then recaptured Lahore, destroyed the Golden Temple at Amritsar, and temporarily re-established Durrani control over most of Punjab before withdrawing in December 1762.

w4-800448.name: Expulsion of the Jesuits from the Spanish Empire (1767) and reversion of Reductions to Crown control
w4-800448.blurb: On 27 February 1767, King Charles III of Spain signed a decree expelling all Jesuits from his dominions. Colonial authorities in the Río de la Plata executed the order in 1767–1768, seizing the Guaraní missions (reducciones) in modern Paraguay, Argentina, and Brazil and transferring them to Crown administration. By 1769 the missions were formally under secular and secular-religious control, marking the complete transfer of their territory to the Spanish Empire.

citations.label: Jesuit missions among the Guaraní – Wikipedia
Suppression of the Society of Jesus – Wikipedia

w4-800450.name: Treaty of Fort Stanwix (1768): Haudenosaunee cede Ohio Valley lands to Britain
w4-800450.blurb: In November 1768, more than 3,000 Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) representatives signed the Treaty of Fort Stanwix, ceding over 27 million acres in the Ohio River Valley to the British Crown in exchange for goods worth roughly £10,000. This formalized a new boundary line south and west of the Proclamation Line of 1763. The atlas entries for 1763–1769 reflect the process from the Proclamation establishing the Indian Reserve through to the formal Stanwix cession.

w4-800451.name: Oyo-Akyem-Dahomey coalition defeats invading Ashanti army (1764)
w4-800451.blurb: In 1764 a joint Akyem-Dahomey-Oyo force defeated an invading Ashanti army in or near Atakpame (in present-day Togo, matching the coordinate lng 0.6, lat 6.5). The Oyo-led coalition's victory halted Ashanti eastward expansion and defined the territorial borders between the neighboring states, within the dataset's 1763–1769 window. This is an attested confrontation, not merely a label artifact.

w4-800461.name: Russian absorption of the Kalmyk/Astrakhan steppe (culminating 1771)
w4-800461.blurb: The Kalmyk Khanate occupied the former Astrakhan Khanate steppe from the 1630s and was abolished by Catherine II in October 1771, its powers transferred to the Governor of Astrakhan. The worklist 'Astrakhan Khanate → Russian Empire' at 41.8E, 49.4N, py=1763 y=1769, brackets the period of intensifying Russian control before the final abolition. The incorporation is real; the 'Astrakhan Khanate' label is the historical territory name. Kept as a genuine, if gradually-dated, absorption.

w4-800462.name: Abolition of Cossack autonomy in Sloboda Ukraine by Catherine II
w4-800462.blurb: From 1763, Catherine II's Shcherbinin Commission investigated the five Sloboda Cossack regiments (Kharkiv, Sumy, Ostrogozhsk, Okhtyrka, Izium) of Sloboda Ukraine. Following a Senate decision of December 1764, the regiments were reorganised in 1765 into regular Russian hussar units, eliminating the Cossacks' self-governance. Sloboda Ukraine became an ordinary Russian province (the Sloboda Ukraine Governorate centred on Kharkiv), and former Cossack officers received hereditary Russian nobility.

citations.label: Abolition of the Cossack system in Sloboda Ukraine – Wikipedia

w4-800463.name: Sikh Reconquest of Punjab after Durrani Withdrawal (1763–1769)
w4-800463.blurb: After Ahmad Shah Durrani's sixth invasion ended in December 1762, the Sikh misls launched a rapid counteroffensive in 1763: they reoccupied Lahore, crushed Jahan Khan's army at Sialkot, killed Zain Khan Sirhindi at Sirhind, and progressively expelled Durrani garrisons from Punjab. Subsequent Durrani invasions (1764–1769) failed to re-establish control, and by the early 1770s the Sikh Confederacy held effective sovereignty over most of Punjab.

citations.label: Indian campaign of Ahmad Shah Durrani – Wikipedia

w4-800464.name: Treaty of Masulipatam (1768) — Nizam cedes Northern Circars to the East India Company
w4-800464.blurb: Following Clive's 1765 Mughal firman granting the Northern Circars to the East India Company, the Nizam of Hyderabad (Asaf Jah II) signed the Treaty of Masulipatam on 23 February 1768, ceding the five Northern Circars to British control. This deprived Hyderabad of its coastline at lng 82.9, lat 18 (coastal Andhra/Orissa), matching Hyderabad State -> British Empire in [1763,1769].

w4-800466.name: Burmese–Siamese War (1765–1767): Fall of Ayutthaya and founding of Thonburi
w4-800466.blurb: King Hsinbyushin of the Konbaung dynasty invaded Siam in 1765; after a 14-month siege Ayutthaya fell and was destroyed on 7 April 1767, ending the 417-year kingdom. General Taksin rallied forces, expelled the Burmese, and founded the Thonburi Kingdom in December 1767. Matches the Ayutthaya → Thonburi transfer in the 1763-1769 window.

w4-800468.name: Abolition of the Kalmyk Khanate by Catherine II
w4-800468.blurb: In January 1771, Ubashi Khan led the majority of the Kalmyk population eastward toward Dzungaria to escape Russian encroachment on their pastoral lands and autonomy. Empress Catherine II responded by formally abolishing the Kalmyk Khanate in October 1771, transferring all governmental powers over the remaining Kalmyks to the governor of Astrakhan and annexing the territory to the Russian Empire.

w4-800469.name: First Partition of Poland
w4-800469.blurb: The First Partition of Poland was agreed by Russia, Prussia, and Austria in 1772 and formally ratified by the Polish Sejm under military duress on 18 September 1773. Russia acquired Livonia and eastern Belorussia, moving its borders westward. The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth lost approximately one-third of its land and half its population across the three partitioning powers, with Russia's share centered on the eastern borderlands.

w4-800470.name: First Partition of Poland
w4-800470.blurb: On 5 August 1772 Russia, Prussia, and Austria signed the treaty partitioning the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, ratified by the Polish Sejm on 30 September 1773. Prussia gained Royal Prussia (excluding Danzig and Thorn) and northern Greater Poland, creating a territorial bridge between Brandenburg and East Prussia. The dataset records 'Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth → Kingdom of Prussia' for this central-Polish corridor, corresponding to Prussia's gains in the First Partition.

w4-800471.name: First Partition of Poland
w4-800471.blurb: On 5 August 1772, Russia, Prussia, and Habsburg Austria signed the First Partition of Poland, ratified by the Polish Sejm in 1773. Austria gained roughly 83,000 km² of southeastern Commonwealth territory, becoming the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria, including Lwów (Lviv). The dataset transfer (Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth -> Habsburg Monarchy, py1769/y1772) at lng22.4/lat49.3 is precisely the Galician region acquired by Austria.

citations.label: Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria – Wikipedia

w4-800474.name: Maratha capture of Delhi (1771) and consolidation in northern India under Mahadji Scindia
w4-800474.blurb: Following the Maratha defeat at the Third Battle of Panipat (1761), Mahadji Scindia (Shinde) led the Maratha revival in northern India, capturing Delhi on 10 February 1771 and restoring Mughal emperor Shah Alam II as a nominal ruler under Maratha protection. By 1772 the Marathas controlled the Delhi–Agra region around lng 77.6, lat 27.7, matching Mughal Empire -> Maratha Empire in [1769,1772].

w4-800475.name: Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (1774) — Russia returns Moldavia to Ottoman suzerainty
w4-800475.blurb: The Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (21 July 1774) ended the Russo-Turkish War of 1768–1774 and required Russia to evacuate the Danubian Principalities, restoring Moldavia to Ottoman suzerainty (a 1775 side-deal then let Austria annex Bukovina). The entry from 'Russian Empire' to 'Principality of Moldavia' at lng 27.3, lat 47 captures Russia's formal withdrawal from Moldavian territory, matching the [1772,1775] window.

w4-800476.name: Second Treaty of Banaras (Treaty of Faizabad, 1775) – Awadh cedes Banaras to the EIC
w4-800476.blurb: By the Second Treaty of Banaras / Treaty of Faizabad (1775), the Nawab of Awadh ceded the Banaras (Varanasi) region to the British East India Company. The coordinates are the Banaras zone, matching the recorded Awadh → British transfer within the 1772–1775 window. (The blurb's earlier framing via the First Treaty of Banaras of 1773 is wrong: that treaty moved Allahabad and Kora FROM the Company TO Awadh, the opposite direction.)

w4-800477.name: Habsburg acquisition of Bukovina from Moldavia (1775)
w4-800477.blurb: Following the First Partition of Poland (1772), the Habsburg Monarchy obtained Bukovina from the Ottoman-vassal Principality of Moldavia in 1775 as compensation for cooperation in the Russo-Turkish War of 1768–1774. The worklist shows Russian Empire→Habsburg Monarchy, reflecting Russia's wartime occupation before ceding it to Austria; Bukovina was incorporated into Galicia and Lodomeria at (24.6°E, 47.1°N).

w4-800480.name: Tây Sơn Rebellion conquers Nguyễn-held central Vietnam
w4-800480.blurb: The Tây Sơn brothers, led by Nguyễn Nhạc, launched their uprising in 1771 in Bình Định and rapidly seized much of central Vietnam from the Nguyễn lords. By 1775, with the Trịnh attacking from the north and capturing Huế, the Tây Sơn swept through the remaining Nguyễn territories in the central coastal region, effectively ending Nguyễn control there. The worklist coordinates correspond to central Vietnam near Bình Định/Phú Yên,

w4-800481.name: Destruction of the Zaporozhian Sich by Catherine II
w4-800481.blurb: Following the 1774 Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca with the Ottomans, which removed the strategic rationale for the Cossack frontier buffer, Catherine II ordered General Peter Tekeli to surround and dismantle the Zaporozhian Sich. On 5 June 1775, Russian troops encircled the fortress and demanded its surrender; the Cossacks capitulated without bloodshed. By manifesto of 3 August 1775, Catherine officially abolished the Zaporozhian Host and annexed its territories to the new Novorossiya Governorate.

citations.label: Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich – Wikipedia

w4-800484.name: Siamese conquest of Lan Na from Konbaung Burma (1774–1775)
w4-800484.blurb: King Taksin of Thonburi (Siam) marched north in December 1774 with Generals Chakri and Surasi to attack Burmese-held Chiang Mai. Local Lanna nobles Kawila of Lampang and Phraya Chaban allied with the Siamese in the 'Fuen Man' liberation movement. Chiang Mai fell on 15 January 1775, ending over 200 years of Burmese Toungoo/Konbaung rule. The dataset records the territory (lat 19.2, lng 99.1) transferring from Konbaung to Chiangmai (local vassal of Siam) around 1772–1775.

citations.label: Siamese conquest of Lan Na (1774–1775) – Wikipedia

w4-800486.name: Trịnh seizure of Phú Xuân (Huế) during Tây Sơn Rebellion
w4-800486.blurb: The Tây Sơn Rebellion (from 1771) devastated the Nguyễn lords' southern domain, and in 1774 the Trịnh lord Trịnh Sâm sent 30,000 troops south. In early 1775 the Trịnh army captured the Nguyễn capital Phú Xuân (modern Huế), driving Lord Nguyễn Phúc Thuần south to Saigon and annexing central Vietnam around lat 16, lng 107.5. Window 1772-1775. The territory stayed under Trịnh control until the Tây Sơn reunified it.

w4-800487.name: First Rohilla War and annexation of Rohilkhand by Awadh (1774)
w4-800487.blurb: The Nawab of Awadh, Shuja-ud-Daula, waged the First Rohilla War in 1774 with British East India Company support, defeating the Rohilla Afghans of Rohilkhand at the Battle of Miranpur Katra (April 1774). Rohilkhand had been a frontier zone exposed to Maratha raids, and after the war the bulk of the territory was annexed to Awadh, with a reduced Rohilla state left at Rampur. Note: the territory was held by the Rohillas (not directly by the Maratha Empire as the dataset 'from' label implies); the dataset reflects loose Maratha frontier overlordship in the region.

w4-800492.name: Tây Sơn Campaigns Against the Trịnh Lords
w4-800492.blurb: The Tây Sơn brothers launched a rebellion in 1771 against the Nguyễn and Trịnh lords who divided Vietnam. By 1776 the southern Nguyễn were overthrown; Nguyễn Nhạc proclaimed the Tây Sơn as an independent state in 1778. Nguyễn Huệ then marched north in 1786 and defeated the Trịnh lord Trịnh Khải, who fled and committed suicide, ending over two centuries of Trịnh rule. The change registered here (1776–1778) reflects the decisive phase when the Tây Sơn consolidated control over former Trịnh-adjacent territory ahead of their full northern campaign.

w4-800493.name: Treaty of Teschen (1779)
w4-800493.blurb: The War of the Bavarian Succession was settled by the Treaty of Teschen (13 May 1779), mediated by France and Russia. Austria renounced its claims on the Bavarian inheritance and returned the bulk of occupied Bavaria to the Wittelsbachs, retaining only the Innviertel — the district between the Inn, Salzach, and Danube. This change marks that Innviertel cession from Bavaria to the Habsburg Monarchy.

w4-800494.name: First Treaty of San Ildefonso and Treaty of El Pardo
w4-800494.blurb: Following the 1776–1777 Spanish-Portuguese War, the First Treaty of San Ildefonso (1 October 1777) settled territorial disputes in South America: Portugal ceded Colonia del Sacramento and the Misiones Orientales while Spain recognised Portuguese sovereignty over southern Brazil. The follow-up Treaty of El Pardo (11 March 1778) further exchanged African territories. Together these redrew the colonial boundary around the Río de la Plata, with territory near modern Uruguay and southern Brazil passing to Spain.

citations.label: First Treaty of San Ildefonso — Wikipedia

w4-800496.name: Treaty of Teschen – End of the War of the Bavarian Succession
w4-800496.blurb: The War of the Bavarian Succession (1778–1779) was triggered by Joseph II's attempt to absorb Bavaria after the extinction of the junior Wittelsbach line. The Treaty of Teschen (13 May 1779) forced Austria to abandon most Bavarian claims, retaining only the Innviertel; the rest reverted to Bavaria under Palatine Wittelsbach rule (~9.7E/49.3N). Window [1778,1780], date 1779.

citations.label: War of the Bavarian Succession – Britannica

w4-800497.name: War of the Bavarian Succession / Treaty of Teschen
w4-800497.blurb: On the extinction of the Bavarian Wittelsbach line (1777), Joseph II arranged to annex Lower Bavaria; Frederick the Great objected and war followed (July 1778). The nearly bloodless War of the Bavarian Succession ended with the Treaty of Teschen (13 May 1779): Austria returned most of Bavaria to the Wittelsbach Elector Palatine but kept the Innviertel. The 1778–1780 window captures this Bavarian consolidation.

citations.label: War of the Bavarian Succession – Wikipedia

w4-800502.name: Treaty of Paris (1783) — Vermont de facto independence recognized
w4-800502.blurb: In the Treaty of Paris (3 September 1783) Britain renounced its claims to its former thirteen colonies, ending the American Revolutionary War. Vermont, which had declared itself an independent republic in 1777 but was denied admission by the Continental Congress, continued to govern itself as the de facto independent Vermont Republic outside both British and U.S. authority until joining the Union in 1791.

w4-800503.name: Bernardo de Gálvez captures Mobile and West Florida for Spain (1780–1781)
w4-800503.blurb: During the American Revolutionary War, Spain's governor of Louisiana, Bernardo de Gálvez, launched a campaign to retake British West Florida. He captured Fort Charlotte at Mobile on 14 March 1780 and completed the conquest with the siege of Pensacola (March–May 1781). The fall of Pensacola on 10 May 1781 transferred all of West Florida from Britain back to Spain.

w4-800505.name: Treaty of Paris (1783) and Vermont Republic
w4-800505.blurb: The Treaty of Paris (3 September 1783) ended the American Revolutionary War; Vermont (coord 72.8W/44.5N) had operated as an independent republic since 1777, unrecognised by Britain and Congress. The 1783 settlement placed Vermont's territory within the US sphere, ending residual British claim. The dataset's 1781–1783 shift from 'British Colonial Empire' to 'Vermont Republic' reflects the war's final phase; Vermont joined the USA in 1791.

w4-800506.name: Vermont Republic distinct from the United States (Treaty of Paris 1783)
w4-800506.blurb: Vermont declared independence from New York in 1777 and operated as the de facto independent Vermont Republic, not recognized by the Continental Congress as one of the states. In August 1781 Congress refused to admit Vermont unless it abandoned its expanded territorial claims, and the 1783 Treaty of Paris folded Vermont's territory within US boundaries (at New York's insistence) even though Vermont itself did not accept US authority. The data window 1781-1783 (from the United States to the Vermont Republic) reflects this contested, de facto separate jurisdictional status.

w4-800507.name: Russian Annexation of Crimea (1783)
w4-800507.blurb: On April 8, 1783, Empress Catherine II issued a manifesto formally annexing the Crimean Khanate to the Russian Empire, following the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (1774). Prince Potemkin administered the territory as Taurida Oblast from 1784, and the Ottoman Empire recognized the loss in the Treaty of Constantinople (December 1783). Coords (36.6E/46N) fall in the northern Crimea/Azov region.

w4-800508.name: Mahadaji Scindia restores Maratha-brokered Mughal authority around Delhi
w4-800508.blurb: After the Treaty of Salbai ended the First Anglo-Maratha War (May 1782), Mahadaji Scindia consolidated Maratha power in north India, reconquering Gwalior (1783) and becoming deputy regent of Mughal affairs (1784), making Shah Alam II a Maratha protégé. The region around Delhi/Mathura (lat 27.8, lng 77.6) reverted to nominal Mughal rule under Maratha protection, matching the Maratha-to-Mughal direction. Window 1781-1783.

w4-800509.name: Treaty of Paris (1783) — Cession of Florida to Spain
w4-800509.blurb: The 1783 Peace of Paris ended the American Revolutionary War with a companion Anglo-Spanish treaty ceding East and West Florida back to Spain, reversing the 1763 transfer. Coordinates (−82.7, 27.9) fall in central Florida. Spain held Florida until the Adams–Onís Treaty of 1821 transferred it to the United States.

w4-800514.name: Chakri coup: founding of the Rattanakosin Kingdom
w4-800514.blurb: In 1782 General Chao Phraya Chakri overthrew and executed King Taksin of the Thonburi Kingdom and ascended as King Rama I on 6 April 1782, founding the Chakri dynasty and Rattanakosin Kingdom, moving the capital to Bangkok. Matches the Thonburi → Rattanakosin transfer in the 1781-1783 window.

w4-800516.name: Konbaung conquest of Arakan (1784–1785)
w4-800516.blurb: King Bodawpaya of the Konbaung dynasty launched an invasion of the Kingdom of Mrauk U (Arakan) in December 1784, led by Crown Prince Thado Minsaw with over 20,000 troops. Burmese forces crossed the Arakan Yoma mountains and captured the capital Mrauk-U on 2 January 1785, ending nearly 360 years of Arakanese independence. The conquest incorporated Arakan (lat 19.5, lng 93.6, modern Rakhine State) into Burma, sparking mass refugee flows into British Bengal and eventually contributing to the First Anglo-Burmese War (1824).

w4-800517.name: Tay Son conquest of Tonkin (1786-1788)
w4-800517.blurb: The Tay Son brothers, having already overthrown the Nguyen lords in the south, launched a northern campaign in 1786 under Nguyen Hue that captured the capital Thang Long (Hanoi) and ended the centuries-long political dominance of the Trinh lords over Tonkin. A Qing Chinese intervention in 1788 briefly restored the last Le emperor, but Nguyen Hue-crowning himself Emperor Quang Trung-drove the Qing out at the Battle of Ngoc Hoi-Dong Da in early 1789, consolidating Tay Son control over the north. The change captured in the data (py=1783, y=1788) reflects this period of Tay Son territorial expansion across Tonkin.

w4-800518.name: Shah Murad founds the Emirate of Bukhara (1785)
w4-800518.blurb: In 1785 Shah Murad of the Manghit clan deposed the last puppet Janid khan and proclaimed himself Emir, adopting the title 'amir al-mu'minin' rather than 'khan' because the Manghits lacked Chinggisid descent. This transformed the Khanate of Bukhara into the Emirate of Bukhara. The from->to (Khanate -> Emirate of Bukhara) at 69, 38.9 in the 1783-1788 window matches this dynastic transformation.

w4-800519.name: Qajar Conquest of Northern Iran from the Zand Dynasty
w4-800519.blurb: After escaping Zand captivity following Karim Khan's death in 1779, Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar spent the early 1780s consolidating tribal power in northern Iran. Between 1783 and 1788 he conducted a series of campaigns that seized Qazvin, Zanjan, Gilan, and the Tehran region, making Tehran his capital in 1786. His repeated defeats of Zand forces gave the Qajars undisputed control of northern Iran by 1788.

w4-800521.name: Gorkha Expansion under Regent Bahadur Shah
w4-800521.blurb: From 1785 to 1794, Regent Bahadur Shah aggressively expanded the Gorkha realm. In 1788 Gorkha forces invaded Tibet over a trade dispute and occupied western Sikkim, while campaigns pushed westward toward Kumaon. These conquests dramatically enlarged the territory of Nepal beyond the Gorkha Kingdom's earlier bounds.

w4-800533.name: Battle of Ngọc Hồi–Đống Đa — Tây Sơn expels Qing
w4-800533.blurb: In January 1789 Emperor Quang Trung (Nguyễn Huệ) of the Tây Sơn routed the Qing invasion army at Ngọc Hồi–Đống Đa and recaptured Thăng Long (Hanoi); a 1789–1791 settlement had Qianlong recognise him as king of Annam. The coordinates (105.9,21.9) are northern Vietnam, matching the from→to (Qing Dynasty → Tây Sơn dynasty) in the 1788–1791 window.

citations.label: Battle of Ngọc Hồi–Đống Đa – Wikipedia

w4-800534.name: Austro-Turkish War (1788–1791) — Habsburg Occupation of Moldavian Territory
w4-800534.blurb: The Austro-Turkish War (1788–1791), fought alongside Russia's concurrent war with the Ottomans, brought Habsburg armies into Wallachia, Moldavia, and Serbia. Austrian forces advanced into Moldavian territories by 1789, occupying areas up to the Prut River. The dataset records 'Principality of Moldavia → Habsburg Monarchy' for the 1788–1791 period (lng 26.8, lat 47.2 — northeastern Romania/Moldova border), consistent with Habsburg military occupation during this war.

w4-800536.name: Qajar conquest of Zand Iran under Agha Mohammad Khan
w4-800536.blurb: Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar systematically dismantled the Zand dynasty through campaigns spanning roughly 1779-1794. By the late 1780s Qajar control had spread across central and northern Iran; he took Shiraz in 1792 and defeated the last Zand ruler Lotf Ali Khan at Kerman in 1794. The dataset window 1788-1791 (Zand Dynasty -> Qajar Dynasty at 55.5, 32.4 in central Iran) corresponds to the middle phase of this conquest.

w4-800539.name: First Saudi State expansion into Eastern Arabia
w4-800539.blurb: The Emirate of Diriyah (First Saudi State) expanded into Eastern Arabia in the late 1780s–1790s, defeating the Bani Khalid and asserting control over the al-Hasa region and influence over Bahrain (49.2,26.6), compelling tribute by 1791–1792. This matches the from→to (Bahrain → Emirate of Diriyah) in the 1788–1791 window.

citations.label: Saud bin Abdulaziz Al Saud – Wikipedia

w4-800540.name: Vermont admitted as the 14th US state
w4-800540.blurb: The Vermont Republic, de facto independent since 1777, was admitted to the United States as the 14th state on 4 March 1791 (Congress voted 18 February 1791), after an October 1790 agreement to pay New York $30,000 to resolve land claims. The from=Vermont Republic / to=United States and 1788-1791 window match.

w4-800543.name: Sino-Nepalese War / Qing intervention in Tibet
w4-800543.blurb: After Nepalese Gorkha forces invaded Tibet (a Qing protectorate) in 1788 and 1791, the Qianlong Emperor dispatched some 70,000 troops under Fuk'anggan, who expelled the Gorkhas and advanced to Nuwakot near Kathmandu in 1792. Nepal signed the Treaty of Betrawati (October 1792), accepting Qing suzerainty over Tibet and quinquennial tribute. The coordinates (87.4E, 28.4N) mark the Nepal-Tibet borderland of these campaigns.

w4-800545.name: Treaty of Sistova — Habsburg Withdrawal from Moldavia
w4-800545.blurb: The Treaty of Sistova (4 August 1791), brokered by Britain, Prussia, and the Netherlands, ended the Austro-Turkish War (1788–1791) and largely restored the pre-war status quo. Austria evacuated its occupied positions including the Moldavian territories it had held since 1789, returning them to Ottoman-suzerain Moldavia. The dataset records 'Habsburg Monarchy → Principality of Moldavia' for 1791–1792, directly matching this restitution.

w4-800547.name: Treaty of Jassy (1792) — Russia returns Wallachia to Ottoman suzerainty
w4-800547.blurb: The Russo-Turkish War of 1787–1792 ended with the Treaty of Jassy (9 January 1792). Russia, which had occupied Wallachia during the war, returned Wallachia and Moldavia to Ottoman suzerainty, keeping only the territory between the Bug and Dniester. This restored Wallachian territory around lng 25.3, lat 44.6 from Russian control to the Principality of Wallachia (Russian Empire -> Principality of Wallachia), in [1791,1792].

w4-800552.name: Proclamation of the French First Republic
w4-800552.blurb: On 21–22 September 1792 the National Convention abolished the French monarchy and proclaimed the First Republic. French Guiana, a French colony (coord 53W/4.9N, Cayenne), was thereby re-categorised under the authority of the new Republic rather than the royal colonial administration. The dataset's 1791–1792 shift from 'French Colony of Guiana' to 'French First Republic' reflects this constitutional transition; the colony would see the 1794 abolition of slavery applied within its borders.

w4-800554.name: Haitian Revolution – slave uprising begins (1791)
w4-800554.blurb: The Haitian Revolution began with the Bois Caïman ceremony (14 Aug 1791) and a mass slave uprising on 22 August 1791 across northern Saint-Domingue; by 1792 rebels controlled roughly a third of the colony. The coordinates are Saint-Domingue, matching the French → Haiti shift recorded for 1791–1792 as France lost de facto control.

w4-800555.name: Sino-Nepalese War (Gurkha War) — Qing reasserts suzerainty over Tibet
w4-800555.blurb: Following two phases of Gurkha invasion of Tibet (1788–1792), the Qing Qianlong Emperor dispatched a large army under Fuk'anggan which repulsed the Gurkhas and advanced near Kathmandu. The Treaty of Betrawati (October 1792) confirmed Tibet firmly under Qing suzerainty, and the 1793 Twenty-Nine Articles Ordinance institutionalised Qing control of Tibetan administration. The dataset records the transfer from 'Tibet' to 'Qing Dynasty' in the 1792–1794 window.

w4-800556.name: Sino-Nepalese War and Treaty of Betrawati
w4-800556.blurb: In the Sino-Nepalese War (1788–1792), a Qing-Tibetan force under Fuk'anggan repelled the Gorkhas from Tibet. The Treaty of Betrawati (1792) restored the pre-war frontier and established Nepalese tributary status to the Qing. Nepalese-occupied territory along the Nepal–Tibet border near lng 87.6 E / lat 28 N reverted to Qing/Tibetan control, matching the [1792,1794] window; the relationship was largely suzerain/tributary.

w4-800558.name: Nawab of Awadh consolidates autonomy from declining Mughal Empire
w4-800558.blurb: Awadh (Oudh) was formally established as an autonomous subah in 1722 under Sa'adat Khan, and the Nawabs progressively reduced their tribute to the Mughal Emperor as Mughal power waned after Aurangzeb's death (1707). Asaf-ud-Daula moved the capital from Faizabad to Lucknow in 1775 and further consolidated independent administration. By the early 1790s Awadh was a de facto independent state though nominally within the Mughal imperial framework, under increasing British pressure following the 1784 Treaty.

w4-800559.name: Qajar Conquest of Zand Iran — Fall of Kerman
w4-800559.blurb: Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar defeated the last Zand ruler, Lotf Ali Khan, at Kerman in 1794, completing the Qajar conquest of Iran. After a prolonged siege Lotf Ali Khan was captured and executed on 20 March 1794, and Kerman's population was brutally punished. This victory ended the Zand dynasty and consolidated Qajar rule over southern and eastern Iran. Agha Mohammad Khan was formally crowned Shah in 1796.

w4-800561.name: Third Partition of Poland — Habsburg acquisition of West Galicia (1795)
w4-800561.blurb: The failed Kościuszko Uprising (1794) precipitated the final dismemberment of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. Austria did not take part in the 1793 Second Partition, but in the Third Partition (signed 24 October 1795) the Habsburg Monarchy received West Galicia and southern Mazovia, including the Lublin–Sandomierz lands around these coordinates. The event is well attested but dated to 1795, just past the worklist window.

w4-800563.name: French Revolutionary conquest of the Austrian Netherlands and Rhineland
w4-800563.blurb: During the War of the First Coalition, French Republican armies broke the Austrian and allied lines at the Battle of Fleurus (26 June 1794) and overran the Austrian Netherlands and the left bank of the Rhine by the end of 1794. These territories — Habsburg and Holy Roman Empire lands, not British — passed under French Republican control, a prelude to their formal annexation.

w4-800565.name: French Republic conquers the Austrian Netherlands and invades Dutch Republic after Battle of Fleurus
w4-800565.blurb: On 26 June 1794 French forces under General Jourdan won the Battle of Fleurus against the Coalition army of Prince Josias of Saxe-Coburg, leading to the swift French conquest of the Austrian Netherlands (modern Belgium). French forces crossed into the Dutch Republic in the winter of 1794–95; Dutch patriots proclaimed the Batavian Republic on 18 January 1795. The Austrian Netherlands were formally annexed by France in October 1795.

citations.label: Battle of Fleurus – World History Encyclopedia

w4-800567.name: French Revolutionary conquest of the Austrian Netherlands and Rhine left bank
w4-800567.blurb: During the War of the First Coalition, French armies under Jourdan and Pichegru won the Battle of Fleurus (26 June 1794) and overran the Austrian Netherlands and the left bank of the Rhine. Coord 6.5E/50.3N is in the Rhineland/Liège region. By late 1794 France held these lands; the Austrian Netherlands were annexed in October 1795 and the Rhineland reorganised into French departments. The dataset's 1792–1794 shift from 'HRE Minor States' to 'French First Republic' reflects this conquest.

citations.label: Left Bank of the Rhine – Wikipedia
War of the First Coalition – Wikipedia

w4-800568.name: French Revolutionary Wars - Savoy and Nice ceded to France
w4-800568.blurb: French forces invaded Piedmont in spring 1796 under Bonaparte, defeating Sardinian forces at Montenotte and Mondovi. The armistice of Cherasco (28 April 1796) and Treaty of Paris (15 May 1796) forced Victor Amadeus III to cede the Duchy of Savoy and County of Nice (around 6.5E, 44.9N) to France. Earlier French annexation of Savoy and Nice had begun in 1792 (matching the worklist window 1792-1794); the 1796 treaty confirmed and extended French control.

w4-800572.name: Third Partition of Poland – Russian annexation of Courland
w4-800572.blurb: In the Third Partition (1795) Russia absorbed the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia after Duke Peter von Biron relinquished his rights to Catherine the Great. Courland near lng 24 E / lat 56.7 N passed from the Duchy of Courland to the Russian Empire; the duchy had sought Russian protectorate status in 1794, matching the [1792,1794] window.

citations.label: Duchy of Courland and Semigallia – Wikipedia

w4-800574.name: Treaty of The Hague (1795) — Batavian Republic established
w4-800574.blurb: After the French invasion of the Dutch Republic in winter 1794–95, the Batavian Republic was proclaimed as a French sister republic. The Treaty of The Hague (16 May 1795) sealed the alliance, ceding Zeelandic Flanders, Maastricht, and Venlo to France outright while the rest of the Dutch lands, including North Brabant, formed the Batavian Republic.

w4-800575.name: British conquest of Dutch Ceylon
w4-800575.blurb: When French Revolutionary forces overran the Dutch Republic in early 1795, the Batavian Republic was proclaimed (19 January 1795) as a French client state, and the Dutch overseas possessions of the Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie nominally passed to it. The trading factories on the Coromandel and Gujarat (Surat) coasts of India thus came under Batavian sovereignty before most were seized by Britain following the Kew Letters.

w4-800576.name: British seizure of Dutch Coromandel under the Kew Letters
w4-800576.blurb: When French forces occupied the Netherlands in January 1795 and stadtholder William V fled to Britain, he issued the Kew Letters ordering Dutch colonial governors to surrender their posts to British protection. Dutch governor Jacob Eilbracht capitulated Dutch Coromandel to Britain on 15 July 1795, transferring the Dutch Indian settlements (lat 14.4, lng 82.4) to British East India Company control. Window 1795-1796.

w4-800578.name: Batavian Republic Created - VOC Colonial Territories Nationalised
w4-800578.blurb: French forces overran the Dutch Republic in 1795, creating the Batavian Republic. The VOC was nationalised on 1 March 1796, transferring its colonial possessions (including West Timor, lng 124, lat -9.2) from company to state control. The dataset's 'from' label of 'Portuguese Colonies' is a Cliopatria mislabel for the VOC/Dutch-held area on Timor; the underlying VOC-to-Batavian Republic nationalisation is well attested for 1795-1796.

w4-800580.name: Kew Letters / British occupation of Dutch Ceylon
w4-800580.blurb: Following the French conquest of the Dutch Republic, the exiled Stadtholder William V issued the Kew Letters (early 1795) ordering Dutch colonial governors to surrender their possessions to Britain for safekeeping. British forces accordingly occupied Dutch Ceylon in 1796; Britain formally retained the island under the 1802 Treaty of Amiens.

w4-800581.name: Persian Expedition of 1796 – Zubov's Russian campaign against the Caucasian khanates
w4-800581.blurb: In response to Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar's sack of Tbilisi (1795), Catherine II launched the Persian Expedition of 1796 under Valerian Zubov. Russian forces stormed Derbent and occupied Baku, Shirvan, and Ganja by mid-1796 before Catherine's death halted the campaign. The worklist transfer Khanates of the Caucasus → Russian Empire at lng 48, lat 40.7 in the 1795–1796 window matches this occupation.

citations.label: Russian conquest of the Caucasus – Wikipedia

w4-800584.name: British invasion of Ceylon (1795–1796)
w4-800584.blurb: When the French revolutionary forces overran the Dutch Republic in 1795 and created the Batavian Republic, Britain seized Dutch colonial possessions to prevent French use. An expedition under Colonel James Stuart took Trincomalee in August 1795 and Colombo in February 1796 after the mercenary De Meuron Regiment switched sides. Dutch governor van Angelbeek surrendered, transferring the island (lat 7.5, lng 80.8) to British control. Ceylon was formally made a British Crown Colony in 1802.

w4-800585.name: British invasion and takeover of Dutch Ceylon
w4-800585.blurb: When France overran the Dutch Republic in 1794–1795, creating the Batavian Republic, Britain treated Dutch colonies as hostile territory. British forces from India launched the invasion of Ceylon in 1795; after capturing Trincomalee (August 1795) and other ports, they accepted the surrender of Colombo on 15 February 1796. Dutch Ceylon was not returned to the Netherlands and was made a British Crown Colony in 1802.

w4-800586.name: Siamese (Rattanakosin) seizure of Cambodian provinces
w4-800586.blurb: In 1795 Siam seized Battambang and Siem Reap from Cambodia; King Ang Eng of Cambodia died in 1796, leaving a succession crisis the Rattanakosin Kingdom exploited to consolidate control over western Khmer territory (104.1,12.6). This matches the from→to (Khmer Empire → Rattanakosin Kingdom) in the 1795–1796 window.

w4-800587.name: Nguyễn campaign against Tây Sơn (central coast)
w4-800587.blurb: Nguyễn Ánh (later Emperor Gia Long) waged a decade-long campaign against the Tây Sơn dynasty, which fractured after Quang Trung's death in 1792. The window (1795-1796) and central-coast coordinates (108.5, 13.1) capture an early phase of the Nguyễn southward/coastal advance that culminated in the capture of Phú Xuân (1801) and Hanoi (1802) and reunification under the Nguyễn dynasty.

w4-800588.name: French conquest of Savoy and Nice / Armistice of Cherasco
w4-800588.blurb: In spring 1796 Napoleon Bonaparte's Army of Italy drove the Austrians and Piedmontese from the southern Alpine foothills, forcing Sardinia out of the war at the Armistice of Cherasco (28 April 1796) and pressing the Habsburgs back through Lombardy. The Alpine and sub-Alpine zone around the Ticino border passed from Habsburg/Austrian into French Republican control during this campaign.

citations.label: Wikipedia: Italian campaigns of the French Revolutionary Wars

w4-800592.name: Treaty of San Ildefonso (1796) — Spain allies with France
w4-800592.blurb: The Second Treaty of San Ildefonso (19 August 1796) bound Spain to France in an offensive and defensive alliance against Great Britain, committing each to supply ships and troops to the other. It was a military pact and made no Italian territorial grant to Spain; northern Tuscany and Liguria remained outside Spanish control.

w4-800593.name: Treaty of Tolentino (1797) / Austrian occupation of central Italy
w4-800593.blurb: During Napoleon's Italian campaign, the Treaty of Tolentino (19 February 1797) stripped the Papal States of the Legations; Habsburg/Austrian forces briefly occupied parts of Umbria and the northern Papal States (centroid lng 12.1, lat 43.3, Perugia region) as the military situation shifted rapidly between French and Austrian control before France consolidated its gains.

citations.label: French Revolutionary Wars in Italy — Wikipedia

w4-800595.name: Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar's invasion of the Caucasus and Battle of Krtsanisi
w4-800595.blurb: In 1795 Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar marched into the South Caucasus to reassert Iranian suzerainty over the Caucasian khanates. After receiving submissions from Karabakh and Ganja, he defeated King Heraclius II of Georgia at Krtsanisi (8-11 September 1795) and sacked Tbilisi. He was crowned Shah in 1796, bringing the Caucasian khanates (lat 39.9, lng 45.6) back under Qajar authority. Window 1795-1796.

w4-800596.name: Wahhabi-Saudi Expansion into Asir / Najd (Emirate of Diriyah)
w4-800596.blurb: The Emirate of Diriyah (First Saudi state) expanded aggressively in the mid-1790s: after defeating the Bani Khalid in al-Hasa (1793-1795), Saudi-Wahhabi forces opened the Asir campaign in 1796 (Ravi ibn Zayda's invasion, sieges of Bisha 1796-1798), with Asir's leadership submitting by c. 1800. The coordinates (~42E 20N) lie in the Asir/southwestern zone, matching the campaign that began in the 1795-1796 window. The 'Ottoman Empire' from-label is loose (local tribal/Sharifian, nominally Ottoman sphere) but the Diriyah expansion is attested.

w4-800601.name: British seizure of Demerara and Essequibo (1796)
w4-800601.blurb: The coordinates (-58, 6.2) correspond to the Dutch colonies of Demerara and Essequibo on the Guiana coast. With Britain at war with the French-controlled Batavian (Dutch) Republic, British forces seized Demerara, Essequibo, and Berbice in 1796 with little resistance. The colonies were briefly returned at the Peace of Amiens (1802) but retaken in 1803 and formally ceded to Britain at the London Convention of 1814. The worklist's from-polity ('New Netherland') is a dataset label for the Dutch Guiana colonies; the Dutch-to-British direction is correct.

w4-800605.name: French withdrawal across the Rhine (1796–1797)
w4-800605.blurb: After advancing into southern Germany in summer 1796, the French armies of Jourdan and Moreau were defeated by Archduke Charles and forced back across the Rhine by October 1796. The Holy Roman Empire minor states of the Rhine Palatinate around Mannheim were restored as the French withdrew from the right bank, an arrangement confirmed by the armistice and the Treaty of Campo Formio (1797).

citations.label: Wikipedia: War of the First Coalition

w4-800607.name: Qajar conquest of Khorasan (Mashhad)
w4-800607.blurb: Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar seized Mashhad and overthrew the last Afsharid ruler Shahrokh Shah in 1796, ending Durrani suzerainty over Khorasan. The territory near Mashhad (59.5,35.9) thus transferred from Durrani to Qajar control in the 1796–1797 window, matching the from→to.

w4-800608.name: Paul I recalls Russian forces from the Caucasus; Qajar Iran regains khanates (1797)
w4-800608.blurb: On Catherine II's death in November 1796, Tsar Paul I recalled all Russian troops from the Caucasus, reversing Zubov's 1796 gains and allowing the Qajars to reassert control over the Azerbaijani khanates. The worklist transfer Russian Empire → Qajar Dynasty at lng 48, lat 40.7 in the 1796–1797 window matches this reversion.

w4-800609.name: French Revolutionary conquest of Piedmont
w4-800609.blurb: Having already forced Sardinia to cede Savoy and Nice in 1796, France moved against the Piedmontese mainland: in December 1798 French troops under Joubert occupied Turin, King Charles Emmanuel IV abdicated his continental possessions, and a provisional government proclaimed Piedmont's union with France. The Subalpine Republic followed in 1800, placing Piedmont under French control.

w4-800610.name: French retreat from southern Germany after Amberg and Würzburg
w4-800610.blurb: In 1796, during the French Revolutionary Wars, a British squadron seized the Dutch colonies of Demerara and Essequibo on the Guiana coast, the Netherlands having become the French-allied Batavian Republic. The colonies surrendered without significant resistance and passed from Dutch (Batavian) to British control.

w4-800611.name: French invasion of Switzerland and creation of the Helvetic Republic
w4-800611.blurb: In early 1798 French Revolutionary armies invaded the Old Swiss Confederacy, defeating Bernese resistance at Grauholz in March 1798. On 12 April 1798 the Helvetic Republic was proclaimed as a French sister republic, dissolving the cantonal sovereign structure. The data window (1797-1799) covers the French conquest and the early Helvetic period at lat 46.8, lng 8.2.

w4-800614.name: French annexation of Piedmont
w4-800614.blurb: After Napoleon forced the Kingdom of Sardinia to cede Piedmont in 1796, the French Directory declared the annexation of Piedmont in early 1799. King Charles Emmanuel IV abdicated and retreated to Sardinia. A brief Austro-Russian restoration in 1799 was reversed by Napoleon's victory at Marengo (1800). The from=Kingdom of Sardinia / to=French Directory and the 1797-1799 window align with the Directory's annexation.

w4-800615.name: British seizure of Demerara and Essequibo (Dutch Guiana)
w4-800615.blurb: The dataset labels the territory 'New Netherland' but the coordinates point to the Demerara-Essequibo region of South America (modern Guyana), the former Dutch colony there. Britain seized Demerara and Essequibo from the Dutch in 1796 during the French Revolutionary Wars when the Batavian Republic (a French client state) was at war with Britain. The colonies were formally ceded to Britain by the Anglo-Dutch Convention of 1814. The 'New Netherland' label in the dataset is likely a misidentification of the Dutch colonial entity.

citations.label: Capture of Demerara and Essequibo - Wikipedia

w4-800616.name: Proclamation of the Roman Republic (1798)
w4-800616.blurb: Following a confrontation in Rome where French General Duphot was killed in December 1797, Napoleon ordered General Berthier to occupy the city. On 15 February 1798 Berthier proclaimed the Roman Republic, deposing Pope Pius VI and incorporating the Papal States into a French client republic governed by a five-man Directory. The Republic was short-lived; Neapolitan forces restored papal authority in October 1799.

w4-800618.name: Durrani decline; Emirate of Bukhara reasserts north of the Hindu Kush
w4-800618.blurb: After Timur Shah Durrani's death (1793) the Durrani Empire fell into dynastic strife, and the Emirate of Bukhara under Shah Murad raided and pressed into Afghan Turkestan, with the Amu Darya as the de facto frontier. By c. 1800 Bukhara had reasserted influence over former Durrani vassal territory in the Merv/Balkh borderland.

w4-800619.name: First Saudi State occupation of the Buraimi oasis
w4-800619.blurb: By around 1800 the Emirate of Diriyah (First Saudi State), under Imam Abd al-Aziz bin Muhammad, had expanded across the Arabian Peninsula and pushed into the eastern Arabian coast that the Sultanate of Oman had influenced. A Saudi campaign led by Salem bin Bilal al-Harq occupied the strategic Buraimi oasis in 1800 (near lat 25, lng 55.8), coercing local tribes into allegiance and displacing Omani authority over the region.

w4-800624.name: Ranjit Singh captures Lahore and consolidates the Sikh Confederacy into the Sikh Empire
w4-800624.blurb: In 1799, Ranjit Singh of the Sukerchakia Misl, allied with Rani Sada Kaur's Kanhaiya Misl, captured Lahore from the Bhangi Misl with an army of 25,000. This act effectively began the transformation of the loose Sikh Confederacy into a centralised state. Ranjit Singh was formally crowned Maharaja in 1801. The dataset records territory around lat 32, lng 74.1 (Punjab heartland) transferring from the Sikh Confederacy to the newly founded Sikh Empire.

w4-800625.name: Serfoji II's 1799 subsidiary treaty ceding Thanjavur to the British East India Company
w4-800625.blurb: In 1799 Thanjavur Maratha king Serfoji II signed a subsidiary alliance ceding administrative control of Thanjavur to the British East India Company for a pension and protection; the Company took over revenue and governance, absorbing it into the Madras Presidency. The worklist shows Thanjavur Maratha→'Carnatic Sultanate', which reflects a data-label issue — the Carnatic (under British administration) was the receiving entity. The underlying 1799 transfer is real.

w4-800627.name: Dissolution of the VOC and nationalization as Dutch East Indies
w4-800627.blurb: The Dutch East India Company (VOC), bankrupt after years of corruption, smuggling losses, and the costs of the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War, allowed its charter to expire on 31 December 1799. The Batavian Republic (the French-backed Dutch revolutionary state) nationalized all VOC debts and territorial possessions in the Indonesian archipelago, transforming company-ruled trading posts into the state-administered colony of the Dutch East Indies effective 1 January 1800.

w4-800628.name: VOC Dissolution and Nationalization as Dutch East Indies
w4-800628.blurb: The VOC was formally dissolved on 31 December 1799 after bankruptcy, and its territorial possessions were nationalised as the Dutch East Indies under direct government administration from 1 January 1800. The Timor region was among the territories transferred. The dataset's 'from' label 'Portuguese Colonies' reflects contested Dutch/Portuguese border zones on Timor; the VOC-to-Dutch-East-Indies succession in 1799-1800 is well attested.

w4-800629.name: Third Treaty of San Ildefonso - Spain cedes Louisiana to France (1800)
w4-800629.blurb: On 1 October 1800, Spain secretly ceded the colony of Louisiana back to France through the Third Treaty of San Ildefonso, in exchange for an Italian duchy (the Kingdom of Etruria) for the Spanish queen's family. Napoleon envisioned Louisiana as the agricultural base for a renewed French Atlantic empire. The dataset records territory at -71.4W, 25.6N (Caribbean area) passing from 'French Directory' to 'French Louisiana' around 1799-1800; the Directory had been replaced by the Consulate in November 1799 just before the treaty was signed.

citations.label: Third Treaty of San Ildefonso - Wikipedia

w4-800630.name: Third Treaty of San Ildefonso - Louisiana retroceded from Spain to France
w4-800630.blurb: Spain secretly retroceded the Louisiana Territory to France under the Third Treaty of San Ildefonso (1 October 1800), in exchange for Napoleon's promise of a Kingdom of Etruria for Spain's Bourbons. Spain had held Louisiana since 1762; France took formal possession on 30 November 1803, weeks before selling it to the US. The from=Spanish Empire / to=French Louisiana and 1799-1800 window match.

citations.label: Third Treaty of San Ildefonso - Wikipedia

w4-800632.name: Coup of 18 Brumaire; French Directory replaced by the French Consulate
w4-800632.blurb: On 9-10 November 1799 (18-19 Brumaire Year VIII), Napoleon Bonaparte and co-conspirators overthrew the Directory in a parliamentary coup, establishing the French Consulate with Napoleon as First Consul. Matches worklist transition French Directory -> French Consulate (1799-1800); coords lng 20.1 lat 15.2 (Lake Chad) reflect French claims inherited by the new government.

w4-800633.name: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War - Fall of Seringapatam
w4-800633.blurb: In the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799), a British East India Company force with Maratha and Hyderabadi allies besieged and stormed Seringapatam on 4 May 1799, killing Tipu Sultan. The Kingdom of Mysore was partitioned: the Mysore heartland was restored to the Wadiyar dynasty as a subsidiary-alliance princely state under British oversight, while coastal and other territories were directly annexed. The dataset reflects British control over the region from 1800.

w4-800635.name: War of the Second Coalition – Habsburg reconquest of the Cisalpine Republic
w4-800635.blurb: In April–May 1799, Austro-Russian forces under Suvorov defeated the French at Cassano (27 April) and entered Milan; the Cisalpine Republic was dissolved and placed under Habsburg provisional administration until Marengo (June 1800) reversed it. The Lombardy region near lng 10.6 E / lat 45.3 N passed from the Cisalpine Republic to the Habsburg Monarchy, matching the [1799,1800] window.

w4-800641.name: Treaty of Lucknow (1801) — Awadh cession to British East India Company
w4-800641.blurb: In November 1801, under the subsidiary-alliance pressure of Governor-General Wellesley, Nawab Saadat Ali Khan II of Awadh ceded about half his dominions — including Rohilkhand, the lower Doab, and the Gorakhpur tract — to the British East India Company in return for Company protection. These districts passed from Awadh to British Company rule.

w4-800642.name: Third Treaty of San Ildefonso – Retrocession of Louisiana from Spain to France
w4-800642.blurb: The Third Treaty of San Ildefonso (1 October 1800) secretly retroceded Louisiana from the Spanish Empire to Napoleonic France in exchange for an Italian duchy for the Spanish queen's family. Spain retained nominal administration until French arrival; the formal transfer occurred on 30 November 1803, just weeks before France sold Louisiana to the United States on 20 December 1803. The data window 1801–1803 captures this Spanish-to-French transition.

citations.label: Third Treaty of San Ildefonso – Wikipedia

w4-800644.name: Treaty of Amiens returns Cape Colony to the Batavian Republic (1803)
w4-800644.blurb: Under the Treaty of Amiens (signed 25 March 1802), Britain returned the Cape Colony to the Batavian Republic; the formal handover occurred on 1 March 1803. The from->to (British Cape Colony -> Napoleonic Batavia Republic) at 22.2, -32.4 in the 1801-1803 window matches this return. The Batavian Republic governed the Cape until Britain re-seized it in January 1806.

w4-800646.name: Subsidiary Alliance Treaty imposed on Awadh
w4-800646.blurb: In November 1801, Governor-General Lord Wellesley compelled Nawab Saadat Ali Khan of Awadh to sign a Subsidiary Alliance, under which Awadh ceded roughly half its territory including the Lower Doab, Gorakhpur, and Rohilkhand to the British East India Company. The Nawab had to disband his own army and accept a British Resident at court; in exchange, the Company assumed responsibility for Awadh's defence. The ceded territories (81 degrees E, 27 degrees N, northern Uttar Pradesh) were absorbed into Company administration by 1803. This agreement made Awadh a de facto British protectorate.

citations.label: British Annexation of Awadh – LotusArise IAS

w4-800647.name: British East India Company Annexation of the Carnatic (1801)
w4-800647.blurb: After Nawab Umdat-ul-Umra's death in July 1801, the Marquis of Wellesley imposed the Carnatic Treaty on 26 July 1801, citing the late Nawab's alleged correspondence with Tipu Sultan, stripping the Nawab of all real territory (North/South Arcot, Tiruchirappalli, Madurai, Tirunelveli) and transferring it to the Madras Presidency. The coordinates (~79E 12N, Coromandel Coast) are the Carnatic heartland. Correctly dated within the 1801-1803 window.

w4-800648.name: French evacuation of Egypt and restoration of Ottoman control (1801–1803)
w4-800648.blurb: After British and Ottoman forces defeated the French Army of the Orient, General Menou capitulated at Alexandria on 2 September 1801. The Peace of Amiens (1802) and Treaty of Paris (1802) returned Egypt to the Ottoman Empire; British troops withdrew in 1803, leaving Egypt under Ottoman provincial administration after the French occupation that began in 1798.

citations.label: French invasion of Egypt and Syria — Wikipedia
Napoleon's Campaign in Egypt and Syria — World History Encyclopedia

w4-800649.name: Russian annexation of the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti (eastern Georgia)
w4-800649.blurb: Tsar Paul I issued a decree on 18 January 1801 unilaterally annexing the eastern Georgian kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti to Russia, abrogating the 1783 Treaty of Georgievsk which had promised Russian protection while preserving Georgian sovereignty. Alexander I confirmed the annexation in September 1801. Russian forces took control of Tbilisi and surrounding territory (lat 41.7, lng 45). By 1803 further western Georgian principalities including Mingrelia also accepted Russian suzerainty, completing the consolidation.

citations.label: Georgia within the Russian Empire – Wikipedia

w4-800652.name: French Occupation of Hanover (Convention of Artlenburg)
w4-800652.blurb: In 1803 French and Prussian forces occupied the Electorate of Hanover following the resumption of hostilities after the Peace of Amiens. The Convention of Artlenburg (5 July 1803) disarmed the Hanoverian army and placed the territory under French control. The Electorate was not formally elevated to the Kingdom of Hanover until the Congress of Vienna in 1814–1815; the 1803 transition thus represents the French occupation replacing the Electorate's independent status.

w4-800653.name: Reichsdeputationshauptschluss – HRE minor ecclesiastical states absorbed by Hesse-Kassel
w4-800653.blurb: The Reichsdeputationshauptschluss of 25 February 1803 reorganized the Holy Roman Empire by secularizing and mediatizing scores of minor ecclesiastical and imperial states to compensate princes for losses west of the Rhine. Hesse-Kassel (Hesse) received former ecclesiastical territories from the Electorate of Mainz and others, and in return was elevated to the Electorate of Hesse, with Landgrave Wilhelm IX becoming Wilhelm I, Elector of Hesse.

w4-800654.name: Louisiana Purchase
w4-800654.blurb: The Louisiana Purchase Treaty was signed on 30 April 1803 between the United States and Napoleon's France, transferring the Louisiana Territory for $15 million; New Orleans was formally transferred on 20 December 1803. France had only recently retroceded the territory from Spain via the Third Treaty of San Ildefonso (1800). The from=French Louisiana / to=United States and 1801-1803 window match.

w4-800655.name: First Saudi State expansion into Hejaz – capture of Mecca and Taif (1803)
w4-800655.blurb: In 1803 Saud bin Abdulaziz led Wahhabi-Saudi forces to capture Taif and then Mecca, seizing the Hejaz from Ottoman suzerainty; this centroid at lng 41.5, lat 19.7 (near Taif/Mecca) corresponds exactly to this dramatic Saudi takeover of the holy cities, the most provocative expansion of the First Saudi State.

w4-800657.name: Nguyễn suzerainty over Cambodia under Emperor Gia Long
w4-800657.blurb: After Emperor Gia Long unified Vietnam in 1802, Cambodia's King Ang Chan II accepted Vietnamese tributary status, paying tribute to Gia Long by around 1803-1807. This followed Cambodian-area Nguyễn support during the civil war and resulted in Vietnamese influence expanding westward into Khmer/Mekong Delta borderlands, consistent with the dataset transfer (Cambodia -> Nguyễn dynasty, py1801/y1803) near lng106.9/lat10.6, though Cambodia simultaneously maintained ties with Siam.

citations.label: Vietnam at the Khmer Frontier (Project MUSE)

w4-800658.name: Nguyen Anh (Emperor Gia Long) defeats the Tay Son dynasty and unifies Vietnam
w4-800658.blurb: After decades of civil war, Nguyen Phuc Anh captured the Tay Son capital Phu Xuan (Hue) in June 1801 and took Hanoi in July 1802, ending the Tay Son dynasty. He proclaimed himself Emperor Gia Long and unified Vietnam for the first time under a single ruler. China officially recognised him in 1803, consolidating the transfer of central and northern Vietnamese territory from Tay Son to Nguyen rule.

w4-800659.name: Wahhabi-Saudi conquest of the Hejaz and southern Arabia (1801–1803)
w4-800659.blurb: The Emirate of Diriyah (First Saudi State), allied with the Wahhabi religious movement, expanded rapidly in the early 19th century. In 1802 Saudi forces sacked the Shia holy city of Karbala in Ottoman Iraq; in 1803 they captured Mecca, bringing the Hejaz under Saudi control. Territories around Yemen and the western Arabian Peninsula previously under Qasimid or Zaydi control were absorbed or displaced by the expanding Saudi-Wahhabi state.

citations.label: Wahhabi conquest of Hijaz – Simple English Wikipedia

w4-800660.name: First Saudi State Captures Mecca and Expands at Ottoman Expense
w4-800660.blurb: The Emirate of Diriyah (First Saudi State), allied with the Wahhabi religious movement, captured Mecca in 1803 (and Medina by 1805), seizing control of the Hejaz from the Ottoman Empire. This expansion came after the Wahhabi forces raided Karbala in 1801 and systematically took control of central and western Arabia. The Ottomans eventually commissioned Muhammad Ali of Egypt to crush the state, culminating in the Siege of Diriyah (1818).

w4-800664.name: Treaty of Lunéville
w4-800664.blurb: The Treaty of Lunéville (9 February 1801) confirmed Campo Formio and pushed the Cisalpine Republic's eastern border to the Adige, transferring the Lake Garda / lower-Adige territory near lng 10.6 E / lat 45.3 N from Habsburg (Venetian-province) control to the French-aligned Cisalpine Republic, which was reorganised as the Italian Republic in January 1802. Matches the [1801,1803] window.

w4-800665.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War — British capture of Delhi and northern India
w4-800665.blurb: During the Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803–1805), General Gerard Lake defeated the Maratha army at the Battle of Delhi on 11 September 1803, capturing the city and securing the person of the blind Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. Daulat Rao Scindia signed the Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon (30 December 1803), ceding Delhi, Agra, the Doab, and surrounding territories (lat 28.6, lng 76.5, the Delhi region) to the British East India Company. The Mughal emperor became a British pensioner.

w4-800666.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War - Treaties of Deogaon and Surji-Anjangaon
w4-800666.blurb: In the Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803-05) Arthur Wellesley defeated Scindia and Bhonsle at Assaye and Argaon. The Treaty of Deogaon (17 December 1803) ceded Cuttack and Orissa; the Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon (30 December 1803) ceded Delhi, Agra, and large central Indian territories. Combined, ~220,683 km2 of Maratha-held territory passed to the British. Transfer Maratha Empire -> British Empire fits the 1803-1805 window.

w4-800668.name: French annexation of Piedmont
w4-800668.blurb: After the brief Subalpine Republic (1800–1802), Napoleon incorporated Piedmont directly into France in September 1802 as a set of French departments; the atlas records this administrative consolidation as complete by the 1805 snapshot. The territory at the centroid (7.8°E, 45.1°N) is the Piedmontese heartland taken from the House of Savoy.

w4-800673.name: Treaty of Pressburg (1805) — Bavarian-French territorial exchange
w4-800673.blurb: Following Austerlitz, the Treaty of Pressburg (26 December 1805) reshaped German borders: Bavaria became a kingdom and received Tyrol from Austria, but simultaneously ceded the Principality of Eichstätt and other enclaves to France's Italian satellites. The centroid (lng 11.5, lat 49.2 — central Franconia/Bavaria) likely reflects the Franconian territories that passed from Bavarian control to French-allied arrangements in 1805.

w4-800676.name: First Saudi State expansion into Kuwait and northern Arabia (c. 1803–1805)
w4-800676.blurb: By 1803–1805 the Emirate of Diriyah under Saud bin Abdulaziz extended its authority northward toward Kuwait (centroid lng 47.8, lat 29.3 is near the Kuwait/Iraq border), as Wahhabi-Saudi tribal networks brought the Banu Khalid and allied clans in northeastern Arabia under Diriyah's sphere, effectively displacing the previously nominal Kuwaiti autonomy in the region.

w4-800678.name: Confederation of the Rhine formation — Nassau accession
w4-800678.blurb: On 12 July 1806 the Confederation of the Rhine was established under French protection; Nassau (formed by union of Nassau-Usingen and Nassau-Weilburg) joined as a founding member, absorbing former HRE minor-state territories along the Rhine and in Westphalia. The Holy Roman Empire was formally dissolved on 6 August 1806.

w4-800682.name: First Saudi State captures Mecca and expands across Arabia (1803-1805)
w4-800682.blurb: The Emirate of Diriyah (First Saudi State) captured Mecca in 1803 and Medina in 1804, seizing the holy cities from Ottoman-aligned Hashimite control, and extended Saudi suzerainty across most of the Arabian Peninsula by 1805. The from->to (Ottoman Empire -> Emirate of Diriyah) at 41.4, 26 in the 1803-1805 window matches this expansion.

w4-800686.name: Francis II proclaims the Austrian Empire; dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire
w4-800686.blurb: Anticipating the collapse of the Holy Roman Empire, Francis II declared himself hereditary Emperor of Austria on 11 August 1804, creating the Austrian Empire as a successor polity for Habsburg possessions; the HRE was formally dissolved on 6 August 1806. Matches worklist transition Habsburg Monarchy -> Austrian Empire (1805-1806); coords lng 18.8 lat 47.5 are the Hungarian/Danubian core.

citations.label: Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire – Wikipedia

w4-800687.name: Peace of Pressburg and the Austrian Empire (1805)
w4-800687.blurb: The Peace of Pressburg (26 December 1805), following Austerlitz, forced Austria to cede Tyrol and Vorarlberg to Bavaria, Venetia/Dalmatia to the Kingdom of Italy, and Further Austria to Baden and Württemberg. The coordinates (15°E, 48.2°N) lie in Lower Austria (Austria proper); the recorded to=Austrian Empire reflects the reorganisation of remaining Habsburg lands into the Austrian Empire (proclaimed 1804) in the 1805-1806 window.
