w4-800691.name: Treaty of Pressburg and elevation of Württemberg to a kingdom
w4-800691.blurb: Under the Treaty of Pressburg (26 December 1805), Napoleon elevated Elector Frederick of Württemberg to King Frederick I, proclaimed 1 January 1806. As part of the formation of the Confederation of the Rhine, Württemberg gained full sovereignty and absorbed numerous mediatized neighboring territories and imperial free cities, becoming the Kingdom of Württemberg.

w4-800692.name: Napoleon Transforms the Batavian Republic into the Kingdom of Holland
w4-800692.blurb: Napoleon presented an ultimatum in April 1806 demanding the Dutch accept his brother Louis Bonaparte as king; the Batavian Republic's government capitulated. On 5 June 1806 the Batavian Republic was formally converted into the Kingdom of Holland, with Louis Bonaparte on the throne. The same territory thus passed from the republican Batavian state to the monarchical Kingdom of Holland — recorded in the dataset as 'Batavian Republic → Kingdom of Holland' for 1805–1806.

w4-800693.name: Peace of Pressburg (1805) – Habsburgs cede Tyrol to Bavaria
w4-800693.blurb: The Peace of Pressburg (26 Dec 1805), after Napoleon's victory at Austerlitz, required the Habsburg Monarchy to cede Tyrol (with Trent and Brixen), Vorarlberg, and adjacent lands to the Kingdom of Bavaria, formally transferred in early 1806. The coordinates are the Inn valley / Innsbruck region of Tyrol.

w4-800694.name: Peace of Pressburg — Bavaria elevated to a Kingdom and gains Tyrol/Vorarlberg
w4-800694.blurb: Following Austria's defeat at Austerlitz, the Peace of Pressburg (26 December 1805) elevated Elector Maximilian IV Joseph of Bavaria to King of Bavaria and transferred Tyrol, Vorarlberg, and other formerly Habsburg territories to the new kingdom, effective 1 January 1806.

w4-800697.name: Russo-Persian War (1804–1813): Russia captures Baku and Caucasian khanates from Qajar Iran
w4-800697.blurb: In the Russo-Persian War (1804–1813), Russian forces captured Derbent, Baku, and other khanates from Persian control in 1806, with Shaki, Shirvan, and Karabakh having already recognised Russian authority in 1805. The war ended with the Treaty of Gulistan (1813). The worklist transfer Qajar Dynasty → Russian Empire at lng 47, lat 40.1 in the 1805–1806 window matches these captures.

w4-800698.name: Formation of the Confederation of the Rhine
w4-800698.blurb: On 12 July 1806, sixteen German states signed the Confederation of the Rhine treaty under French pressure; the Grand Duchy of Berg (under Joachim Murat) absorbed numerous HRE minor states and imperial knights whose territories were mediatized, directly precipitating the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire on 6 August 1806.

w4-800703.name: Creation of the Grand Duchy of Berg and Confederation of the Rhine
w4-800703.blurb: On 15 March 1806, Napoleon created the Grand Duchy of Berg from the Duchy of Cleves, the Duchy of Berg, and surrounding Holy Roman Empire minor-state territories, under Marshal Joachim Murat. On 12 July 1806 Berg joined the newly formed Confederation of the Rhine, and the Holy Roman Empire was dissolved in August 1806. The coordinates (9.1E, 51.7N) lie in the Westphalian/Rhineland region reorganised to form the new grand duchy.

w4-800704.name: Treaty of Fontainebleau – Napoleon annexes the Kingdom of Etruria
w4-800704.blurb: By the Treaty of Fontainebleau (27 October 1807) Napoleon dissolved the Kingdom of Etruria; the regent abdicated in December 1807 and Tuscany was annexed to the French Empire (decree 28 March 1808). Tuscany near lng 11.4 E / lat 43.4 N passed from the Kingdom of Etruria to the First French Empire, matching the [1806,1807] window.

w4-800708.name: Russian invasion and occupation of Moldavia at the outbreak of the Russo-Turkish War
w4-800708.blurb: Following the Ottoman deposition of the pro-Russian hospodars of Moldavia and Wallachia in 1806, a large Russian army crossed into the principalities to safeguard Russia's frontier. Russian troops occupied the Principality of Moldavia by late 1806, beginning six years of Russian military administration there during the Russo-Turkish War of 1806-1812.

w4-800709.name: Russian occupation of Wallachia during the Russo-Turkish War of 1806–1812
w4-800709.blurb: The Russo-Turkish War of 1806–1812 was partly instigated by Napoleon, who encouraged the Ottomans to depose the Phanariot hospodars. Russian forces occupied Wallachia (around lng 25.3, lat 44.6) in late 1806 and held it throughout the war (Principality of Wallachia -> Russian Empire), matching the [1806,1807] window. The conflict ended with the Treaty of Bucharest (1812).

w4-800713.name: Treaty of Tilsit - creation of the Kingdom of Westphalia
w4-800713.blurb: The Treaty of Tilsit (9 July 1807) stripped Prussia of about half its territory; Prussian lands west of the Elbe and former Polish territories were reconstituted as the Kingdom of Westphalia, a French client state under Jerome Bonaparte. Prussia fell from about 9.75 to 4.5 million inhabitants. The from=Kingdom of Prussia / to=Kingdom of Westphalia and 1806-1807 window match.

w4-800714.name: Fulani jihad attacks on Bornu Empire
w4-800714.blurb: Usman dan Fodio's Fulani jihad, which had swept through the Hausa states from 1804, extended its campaigns eastward toward the Kanem–Bornu Empire around 1808. Jihadist forces burned Bornu's capital Ngazargamu and defeated the army of Mai Dunama IX Lefiami, temporarily overrunning western Bornu territories. Cleric Muhammad al-Kanemi rallied local resistance, arguing in correspondence that Bornu was already Muslim, and succeeded in repelling the Fulani, though western districts of Bornu passed under Sokoto influence.

citations.label: Jihad of Usman dan Fodio – Wikipedia

w4-800719.name: Daendels Abolishes the Sultanate of Banten (1808)
w4-800719.blurb: Governor-General Herman Willem Daendels ordered Sultan Aliyuddin II of Banten to relocate his capital and provide forced labour for road construction. When the sultan refused, Daendels ordered a military invasion of Banten, arrested the sultan, destroyed the palace of Surosowan, and on 22 November 1808 proclaimed the Sultanate absorbed into the Dutch East Indies, ending over two centuries of Bantenese sovereignty.

citations.label: French and British interregnum in the Dutch East Indies – Wikipedia

w4-800721.name: Spanish reconquest of Santo Domingo (Siege of Santo Domingo, 1808–1809)
w4-800721.blurb: During Napoleon's invasion of Iberia, French forces held Spanish Santo Domingo (eastern Hispaniola). Dominican loyalists under Juan Sánchez Ramírez defeated the French at Palo Hincado (7 November 1808) and, aided by a British blockade, forced the surrender of Santo Domingo city in July 1809, restoring Spanish rule. The worklist codes this as Portuguese Empire → Spanish Empire, an artifact of the Napoleonic Iberian context; the real transfer was France → Spain at lng -70.3, lat 18.8 in the 1807–1809 window.

citations.label: Spanish reconquest of Santo Domingo – Wikipedia

w4-800723.name: Treaty of Schönbrunn: West Galicia Transferred to Duchy of Warsaw
w4-800723.blurb: The Treaty of Schönbrunn (14 October 1809), signed after Napoleon's victory at Wagram, required Austria to cede West Galicia (the 1795 partition zone, including Kraków) to the Duchy of Warsaw, ruled in personal union by Frederick Augustus I, King of Saxony. This expanded the Duchy from roughly 104,000 km² to 155,000 km². The entry's from-party (Kingdom of Saxony) reflects the personal union, and the coordinates near Leipzig are a data artifact; the actual ceded territory was West Galicia.

w4-800727.name: Napoleon's Annexation of the Papal States (1809)
w4-800727.blurb: On 17 May 1809, Napoleon issued decrees from Schönbrunn Palace annexing the remaining Papal States to the First French Empire, forming the départements of Tibre and Trasimène. Pope Pius VII responded with an excommunication bull, after which French forces arrested him on 6 July 1809. The annexed territory remained under French Imperial control until Napoleon's fall; the Congress of Vienna in 1815 restored the Papal States.

citations.label: Napoleon and the Catholic Church – Wikipedia

w4-800729.name: Venezuelan Declaration of Independence
w4-800729.blurb: On July 5, 1811 the First National Congress of Venezuela, with 40 deputies signing, declared independence from Spain, establishing the American Confederacy of Venezuela across seven of ten provinces of the former Captaincy General. Three provinces (Maracaibo, Coro, Guayana) declined to join and remained under Spanish control.

w4-800731.name: Khanate of Kokand expansion under Alim Khan
w4-800731.blurb: Under Alim Khan (r. 1799-1810), the Khanate of Kokand expanded aggressively northward from the Fergana Valley. Having conquered Tashkent (1800) and Ura-Tepe, Kokand pushed into the Kazakh steppe, subjugating nomadic Kazakh tribes and annexing key cities including areas along the Syr Darya by 1809. This expansion brought Kokand into conflict with the Kazakh Khanate, whose pastures and fortified towns it progressively seized.

w4-800732.name: British East India Company expansion in Punjab borderlands after Treaty of Amritsar
w4-800732.blurb: The Treaty of Amritsar (25 April 1809) between the East India Company and Ranjit Singh fixed the Sutlej River as the boundary between British India and the Sikh Empire, with Ranjit agreeing not to expand south of the Sutlej. The territory around lat 29.8, lng 75.6 (the Cis-Sutlej Sikh states in present-day Haryana/Punjab) passed under British protection as a result. The dataset records this as Mughal Empire territory transferring to British Empire, reflecting that these areas were nominally still part of the collapsing Mughal imperium.

w4-800734.name: Venezuelan Declaration of Independence (First Republic)
w4-800734.blurb: On 5 July 1811 seven provinces of the Captaincy General of Venezuela declared independence from Spain, forming the First Republic of Venezuela. The Spain-to-Venezuela transition (8.8N) is within the window (1809-1811).

w4-800737.name: Russian annexation of the Kingdom of Imereti (1810)
w4-800737.blurb: After Solomon II of Imereti refused Russian vassalage and negotiated with the Ottomans, a Russian decree in February 1810 deposed him; Russian troops captured Kutaisi and formally dissolved the Kingdom of Imereti on 20 February 1810, integrating it into the Russian Empire. From=Kingdom of Imereti, to=Russian Empire matches the 1809-1811 window.

citations.label: Georgia within the Russian Empire – Wikipedia

w4-800739.name: Mexican War of Independence – Hidalgo Revolt
w4-800739.blurb: Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla's Grito de Dolores on 16 September 1810 launched the Mexican War of Independence. His army swept through Guanajuato and Valladolid before being repulsed and Hidalgo executed in 1811, depriving the Spanish Crown of effective control over much of western/central New Spain (~101W 19N, Michoacán/Guerrero region). Formal independence came in 1821. The insurgency's onset falls within the 1809-1811 window.

w4-800740.name: US annexation of West Florida
w4-800740.blurb: On 23 September 1810 settlers in West Florida revolted against Spain and declared the Republic of West Florida; Madison proclaimed annexation on 27 October 1810 and Congress authorized occupation in January 1811. The lower-Mississippi / Baton Rouge area near lng -89.4 W / lat 30.6 N passed from the Spanish Empire to the United States, matching the [1809,1811] window.

w4-800741.name: Treaty of Schönbrunn (1809) — Illyrian Provinces
w4-800741.blurb: The Treaty of Schönbrunn (October 1809) required Austria to cede Carniola, Trieste, Istria, and adjacent Adriatic territories to France, which organized them as the Illyrian Provinces under direct French imperial administration, cutting Austria off from the Adriatic coast.

w4-800742.name: Napoleon annexes Hanseatic cities and northwest Germany (1810–1811)
w4-800742.blurb: In December 1810–January 1811, Napoleon directly annexed the Hanseatic cities (Hamburg, Bremen, Lübeck) and much of the Kingdom of Westphalia's northwestern coast into the First French Empire to enforce the Continental System. The centroid at lng 8.1, lat 52.6 (Weser/Lower Saxony area) reflects territory passing from Kingdom of Westphalia to direct French imperial administration.

citations.label: Wikipedia: French annexation of the Hanseatic cities

w4-800746.name: Transfer of Legations and Marches to the Kingdom of Italy
w4-800746.blurb: After Napoleon annexed the Papal States in 1809, northern Papal territories (the Legations and parts of the Marche, centroid 12.5°E, 44.7°N in Emilia-Romagna) were transferred to the Kingdom of Italy (which Cliopatria labels 'Italian Republic') rather than remaining under direct French imperial administration. This reorganization was formalized in 1809–1810.

w4-800748.name: Treaty of Schönbrunn – Austria cedes West Galicia to the Duchy of Warsaw (1809)
w4-800748.blurb: After Napoleon's victory at Wagram (July 1809), the Treaty of Schönbrunn (14 October 1809) required Austria to cede West Galicia, including Kraków and Lublin, to the French-allied Duchy of Warsaw, expanding it substantially. The worklist transfer Austrian Empire → Duchy of Warsaw at lng 18.4, lat 51.3 (southern Poland) in the 1809–1811 window matches this cession.

citations.label: War of the Fifth Coalition – Wikipedia

w4-800751.name: Paraguayan Revolution / May 1811 insurrection
w4-800751.blurb: On the night of 14–15 May 1811, creole officers under Pedro Juan Caballero staged a coup in Asunción, forcing Governor Bernardo de Velasco to share power in a three-man junta and effectively ending Spanish authority over Paraguay. The province declared full independence from both Spain and the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata, becoming the first de facto independent republic in South America.

w4-800754.name: British Invasion of Java (1811)
w4-800754.blurb: During the Napoleonic Wars, with the Netherlands under French control, a British force of nearly 12,000 under Lord Minto landed on Java on 4 August 1811 and captured Batavia within days; Fort Cornelis fell 26 August and the island capitulated 18 September 1811, with Raffles appointed lieutenant-governor. The coordinates (~118E 4S) reflect broader Dutch East Indies territory transferred to British administration in the 1809-1811 window.

w4-800756.name: Act of Federation of the United Provinces of New Granada
w4-800756.blurb: On July 20, 1810 Bogotá's cabildo abierto deposed the viceroy, and on November 27, 1811 the Act of Federation of the United Provinces of New Granada formally constituted an independent confederation from the former New Kingdom of Granada, covering most of modern Colombia. The federation replaced Spanish imperial authority across roughly 1.1 million km² of the former viceroyalty.

citations.label: Wikipedia: United Provinces of New Granada

w4-800757.name: Paraguayan independence from Spain (prompted by Portuguese threat)
w4-800757.blurb: Paraguay declared de facto independence on 14-15 May 1811, when criollo military officers under Pedro Juan Caballero and Fulgencio Yegros overthrew Spanish Governor Velasco. The immediate catalyst was Velasco's secret negotiations with Portuguese (Brazilian) representatives for military protection - an act Paraguayan patriots regarded as treason. The contested border territory thus passed from the Portuguese/Brazilian sphere to the new Paraguayan Republic.

w4-800758.name: First Saudi State (Emirate of Diriyah) control of Oman's borderlands
w4-800758.blurb: The First Saudi State expanded into Oman's northern interior in stages: bin Ufaisan reached the Buraimi Oasis in 1795, with further campaigns in 1800 and 1803, and Saud bin Abdulaziz formally annexed the Buraimi Oasis and secured recognition from Muscat and the Qawasim in 1805. The core conquest thus predates the 1809-1811 data window, but Saudi/Wahhabi dominance over the northern Omani frontier persisted through this window until Muhammad Ali of Egypt's campaigns (begun 1811) rolled it back.

w4-800760.name: May Revolution and formation of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
w4-800760.blurb: On 25 May 1810, the Primera Junta was established in Buenos Aires, deposing the Spanish viceroy and initiating autonomous self-governance. By 1811 the entity was renamed the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata. Formal independence from Spain was declared in 1816, but the effective territorial transfer from Spanish Empire control began with the May Revolution of 1810 (Cliopatria centroid lat -28.8, lng -62, in northern Argentina), which Cliopatria captures in the Spanish Empire to Río de la Plata 1809-1811 window.

citations.label: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata – Wikipedia

w4-800761.name: Colombian independence — Patria Boba and United Provinces of New Granada
w4-800761.blurb: After Napoleon's invasion of Spain destabilised colonial authority, juntas across New Granada ejected Spanish officials from 1810. On 27 November 1811 five provinces signed the Act of Federation establishing the United Provinces of New Granada, transferring this territory from the Spanish Empire to the patriot confederation during the 'Patria Boba'. The dataset window of 1809–1811 matches.

citations.label: United Provinces of New Granada — Wikipedia
First Republic of New Granada — Wikipedia

w4-800762.name: Treaty of Fredrikshamn (1809) and the end of the Swedish Empire
w4-800762.blurb: The Finnish War (1808–1809) ended with the Treaty of Fredrikshamn on 17 September 1809, by which Sweden ceded the whole of Finland and territories east of the Torne River to Russia. The loss of roughly a third of Sweden's territory and a quarter of its population marked the end of the Swedish Empire era; the rump state, reorganised under a new constitution in 1809 and a new (Bernadotte) dynasty soon after, is captured here as Swedish Empire -> Kingdom of Sweden. The coordinates lie in central Sweden proper, reflecting the relabelling of the reconstituted kingdom in the [1809,1811] window.

w4-800763.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806–1812) — Russian annexation of Bessarabia
w4-800763.blurb: During the Russo-Turkish War of 1806-1812 Russia occupied the Danubian Principalities; the Treaty of Bucharest (28 May 1812) formally ceded Bessarabia (east of the Prut) to Russia. The region passed from Russian wartime occupation to permanent Russian possession as the Bessarabia province within the 1811-1812 window. Well attested.

w4-800766.name: Omani counter-offensive and recovery of eastern coastal territory from Diriyah (1812)
w4-800766.blurb: By 1811–1812, the Sultanate of Oman, aided by a British naval expedition against the Qawasim pirates (a Saudi-allied force) in the Persian Gulf, was able to recover some eastern coastal territories (centroid lng 57.1, lat 24.9, Omani interior near Buraimi) that the First Saudi State had seized in 1809–1811, as Saudi overextension left frontier areas vulnerable.

w4-800767.name: British Invasion of Java
w4-800767.blurb: As part of the Napoleonic Wars, Britain launched a successful amphibious operation against French-controlled Java in August-September 1811. Under Lord Minto and the military command of General Auchmuty, British forces captured Fort Cornelis and compelled Dutch Governor-General Janssens to surrender. Stamford Raffles was appointed Lieutenant-Governor of Java, introducing liberal land tenure reforms. Java remained under British control until returned to the Dutch under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814 (effectively 1816).

citations.label: French and British interregnum in the Dutch East Indies – Wikipedia

w4-800768.name: British Expedition to Palembang
w4-800768.blurb: In April 1812, Colonel Robert Rollo Gillespie led a British expedition up the Musi River against Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II of Palembang. The British occupied the city on 28 April, citing the 1811 massacre of the Dutch garrison as justification, though their real aim was to seize the tin-rich island of Bangka. Badaruddin's brother was installed as a British client sultan, and Bangka was ceded to the British.

w4-800769.name: Spanish royalist reconquest of Venezuela / Capitulation of San Mateo
w4-800769.blurb: After the Caracas earthquake of 26 March 1812, royalist commander Monteverde advanced from Coro; Miranda signed the Capitulation of San Mateo on 25 July 1812, surrendering Venezuela to Spain and ending the First Republic. The Venezuela-to-Spain transition (8.8N) is within the window (1811-1812).

citations.label: Dictatorship of Francisco de Miranda – Wikipedia

w4-800770.name: Mexican War of Independence — insurgency under Morelos
w4-800770.blurb: The Mexican War of Independence (1810-1821) saw insurgent forces under Miguel Hidalgo (1810-1811) and then Jose Maria Morelos (from 1811) seize large areas of New Spain from royalist control. After Hidalgo's execution in 1811, Morelos organised an effective guerrilla campaign in southern Mexico including Oaxaca, Guerrero, and Veracruz, capturing significant territory by 1812-1813. The coordinates (-97 degrees, 17 degrees N) point to Oaxaca/Guerrero, the heartland of Morelos's operations. This insurgent advance transferred effective control of southern Mexico from the Spanish Empire to rebel Mexican forces.

w4-800773.name: Chilean War of Independence (Patria Vieja)
w4-800773.blurb: Following Napoleon's overthrow of the Spanish Bourbon monarchy, Chilean creoles established a series of governing juntas beginning in September 1810. By 1811 Jose Miguel Carrera consolidated patriot control over central Chile, effectively replacing Spanish imperial authority with an autonomous Chilean government - the period historians call the Patria Vieja. Spain reclaimed Chile in the reconquest of 1814 (Disaster of Rancagua), but the change at 1811-1812 reflects the brief patriot administration displacing the Spanish crown.

w4-800774.name: Treaty of Bucharest (1812) — Russia returns Wallachia to Ottoman suzerainty
w4-800774.blurb: The Treaty of Bucharest (28 May 1812) ended the Russo-Turkish War of 1806–1812, freeing Russian forces for Napoleon's invasion. Russia evacuated Wallachia and the Moldavian territory west of the Prut, which reverted to Ottoman suzerainty as the Principality of Wallachia, while Russia retained Bessarabia. This restructured the boundary near lng 25.3, lat 44.6 (Russian Empire -> Principality of Wallachia), in [1811,1812].

w4-800775.name: Zaydi-Saudi War — Egyptian-Ottoman campaign recaptures Yemen for Imamate
w4-800775.blurb: From 1811 onward, Muhammad Ali Pasha of Egypt launched the Ottoman-Egyptian campaign against the Saudi/Wahhabi state (Emirate of Diriyah). By 1812–1813, the Egyptian forces had retaken Medina (1812) and Mecca, and Saudi forces were expelled from Yemen. The Zaydi Imamate of Yemen (Qasimid) re-established control over the Yemeni highlands (centroid lng 44.1, lat 14.9) as the Diriyah state retreated.

w4-800777.name: Said bin Sultan Consolidates Omani Control over East African Coast
w4-800777.blurb: Said bin Sultan acceded as Sultan of Oman in 1806 and began consolidating Omani power over the Swahili coast. By 1812-1814 his forces pressed to reassert authority over the Mazrui clan in Mombasa and other nominally Omani-held ports that had drifted toward autonomy. The coordinates point to the Tanzanian coast. The transfer from 'Sultanate of Oman' to 'Omani Slave Coast' captures the dataset's distinction between metropolitan Oman and its East African commercial empire as Said intensified involvement in Swahili trade.

w4-800779.name: Congress of Vienna — Austrian restoration in northern Italy
w4-800779.blurb: Napoleon's Kingdom of Italy collapsed after his abdication in April 1814. The Treaty of Paris (May 1814) and the Congress of Vienna (1814–1815) gave Austria Lombardy-Venetia. The coordinates point to Venetia/Trentino, which passed from the Napoleonic Italian state directly under Austrian imperial control by 1814, matching the from→to (Italian Republic → Austrian Empire) in the 1812–1814 window.

w4-800780.name: Ottoman-Egyptian reconquest expels Wahhabis from Yemen/Hejaz
w4-800780.blurb: The Emirate of Diriyah (First Saudi State) had expanded into Yemen and the Hejaz by the early 19th century. In 1811-1813, an Ottoman-Egyptian expeditionary force under Muhammad Ali Pasha's sons reconquered Medina, Mecca, Taif and the Hejaz, expelling the Wahhabis. The territory around lng 44.1, lat 14.9 (northern Yemen/Asir highlands) reflects Wahhabi/Diriyah forces being pushed back by the Ottoman campaign, returning control to the Imamate of Yemen.

w4-800781.name: Toribio Montes's Royalist Reconquest of the Quito Region
w4-800781.blurb: The State of Quito declared independence and a constitution in February 1812, but royalist General Toribio Montes arrived via Guayaquil on 21 June 1812, won the Battle of Mocha (3 September) and Battle of Ibarra (1 December 1812), restoring Spanish authority. The coordinates (~78W 1S) lie near Quito/Guayaquil. The dataset's 'Guayaquil Junta' from-label is imprecise (Guayaquil stayed royalist until its own 1820 junta), but the real, well-dated event is the royalist reconquest of the rebel Quito region, transferring it back to Spain within the 1812-1814 window.

w4-800782.name: Congress of Vienna - restoration of Kingdom of Sardinia
w4-800782.blurb: Napoleon's First French Empire had annexed Piedmont and Savoy directly, exiling the House of Savoy to Sardinia. With Napoleon's abdication, the Treaty of Paris (30 May 1814) and the Congress of Vienna (1815) restored the Kingdom of Sardinia its mainland possessions and additionally awarded it the former Republic of Genoa (7.4E, 44.9N covers the Ligurian Alps / Piedmont). Victor Emmanuel I re-established Savoyard rule over the restored kingdom.

w4-800786.name: Artigas and the Formation of the Federal League (Liga Federal)
w4-800786.blurb: José Gervasio Artigas, leader of the Provincia Oriental (modern Uruguay), broke with the centralist government of Buenos Aires and organized the Federal League (Liga de los Pueblos Libres), formally constituted at the Congress of Oriente on June 29, 1815. The League united the Provincia Oriental with Entre Ríos, Santa Fe, Corrientes, Misiones, and Córdoba in a federalist confederation opposing Buenos Aires' hegemony over the Río de la Plata, with Artigas as Protector of the Free Peoples. The dataset records the transition (Río de la Plata → Federal League) beginning 1812, reflecting Artigas's earlier break with Buenos Aires at the Exodus of the Oriental People (1811–1812) and his consolidation in the Banda Oriental and Litoral by 1814.

w4-800788.name: Mexican War of Independence — insurgent campaigns under Morelos (1812–1814)
w4-800788.blurb: After Hidalgo's execution (1811) the Mexican War of Independence entered a critical phase under José María Morelos. Between 1812 and 1814 Morelos captured Orizaba, Oaxaca, and Acapulco, convened the Congress of Chilpancingo (1813), and issued the Constitution of Apatzingán (1814). The coordinates in central Mexico mark the contested royalist core where insurgent and Spanish forces clashed.

w4-800790.name: Restoration of the Duchy of Oldenburg after Napoleon's defeat (1813–1814)
w4-800790.blurb: As Napoleonic power collapsed in 1813–14, the Duchy of Oldenburg (centroid 7.8°E, 53.2°N) was de facto restored to Duke Peter Friedrich Ludwig; the Congress of Vienna (1815) formally recognized Oldenburg's restoration and elevated it to a Grand Duchy, but the effective reversion occurred with the French retreat in 1813–1814.

w4-800792.name: Collapse of the Kingdom of Westphalia after Battle of Leipzig (1813)
w4-800792.blurb: After Napoleon's defeat at the Battle of Leipzig (16–19 October 1813), Allied forces occupied the Kingdom of Westphalia on 26 October 1813, dissolving Jerome Bonaparte's Napoleonic client state. The Confederation of the Rhine, of which Westphalia was a member, was formally dissolved on 4 November 1813, restoring the former territorial order to pre-Napoleonic rulers.

w4-800793.name: Restoration of the Papal States by the Congress of Vienna
w4-800793.blurb: Napoleon's First French Empire had annexed most of the Papal States in 1809, imprisoning Pope Pius VII. Following Napoleon's defeat and Pius VII's return to Rome in May 1814, the Congress of Vienna (1814–1815) formally restored the Papal States to the papacy, largely through the skilled diplomacy of Cardinal Consalvi. The Papal States regained all their pre-Napoleonic Italian territories except Avignon and the Comtat Venaissin.

w4-800794.name: Congress of Vienna / Treaty of Paris (1814) - Papal States restored
w4-800794.blurb: Napoleon's Italian Republic and French Empire had annexed Papal territories (the Marches, Umbria, Lazio) from 1808-1809. With Napoleon's defeat, Pope Pius VII returned to Rome on 24 May 1814, and the Congress of Vienna (1814-15) restored the Papal States (centred 12.4E, 43.9N) to nearly their pre-Napoleonic extent, the exception being Avignon and the Comtat Venaissin, which remained French.

w4-800795.to: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands
w4-800795.name: Collapse of the First French Empire and Restoration of Dutch Sovereignty
w4-800795.blurb: After Napoleon's defeat at Leipzig in October 1813, French occupation troops evacuated the Netherlands. A Dutch triumvirate proclaimed the Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands on 2 December 1813, with William Frederick of Orange as Sovereign Prince. The territory thus passed from direct French imperial administration ('First French Empire') to the newly restored Dutch state. This principality was formalized into the United Kingdom of the Netherlands by 1815 after the Congress of Vienna. The dataset window 1812–1814 matches this restoration.

citations.label: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands – Wikipedia

w4-800796.name: Restoration of the Duchy of Oldenburg after Napoleon's fall (1814, confirmed at the Congress of Vienna)
w4-800796.blurb: Napoleon annexed the Duchy of Oldenburg directly into the French Empire in December 1810, sending Duke Peter into exile in Russia. After Napoleon's defeat, the duke returned in 1814, and the Congress of Vienna (1814-15) formally restored his domain and enlarged it with additional territories (e.g. Birkenfeld), elevating it to a grand duchy.

w4-800799.name: Russian Occupation of the Duchy of Warsaw
w4-800799.blurb: In January-February 1813, Russian armies advancing after Napoleon's Moscow disaster occupied the Duchy of Warsaw and installed a Provisional Highest Council. The Congress of Vienna (1814-1815) then partitioned the duchy, with Russia receiving the largest share as 'Congress Poland.' The coordinates (~20E 52N, central Poland) are the heart of former Warsaw territory. Correctly dated within the 1812-1814 window.

w4-800800.name: Fall of the Kingdom of Westphalia and restoration of the Electorate of Hesse
w4-800800.blurb: The Kingdom of Westphalia, created by Napoleon in 1807 for his brother Jérôme, had absorbed Hesse-Kassel. After the French defeat at Leipzig in October 1813, Jérôme's kingdom collapsed; on 21 November 1813 Elector William I re-entered Kassel and reversed the Westphalian reforms. The Congress of Vienna (1814–1815) confirmed the restoration, returning the territory around lat 51.4, lng 9 to Hessian sovereignty. This matches the worklist transfer from the Kingdom of Westphalia to the Electorate of Hesse within 1812-1814.

w4-800801.name: Second Republic of Venezuela / Bolívar's Admirable Campaign
w4-800801.blurb: After the First Republic fell (1812), Bolívar's Admirable Campaign retook Caracas on 6 August 1813, establishing the Second Republic, which collapsed in 1814 under Boves's royalist offensive. The Spain-to-Venezuela transition (8.8N) is within the window (1812-1814).

w4-800803.name: Treaty of Bucharest (1812) — western Moldavia restored to the Principality
w4-800803.blurb: The Treaty of Bucharest (28 May 1812) ceded Bessarabia (between Prut and Dniester) to Russia and required Russia to return Wallachia and the remainder of Moldavia west of the Prut to Ottoman suzerainty. Western Moldavia reverted from Russian wartime occupation to the Principality of Moldavia within the 1812-1814 window. Well attested.

w4-800805.name: British expedition to Palembang (1812); transfer to the Dutch (1814)
w4-800805.blurb: In 1812 a British expedition under Gillespie deposed Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II of Palembang and ceded Bangka and Belitung to Britain. Under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814, Britain restored Dutch East Indian territories including Palembang to the Netherlands. The window (1812-1814) reflects this period leading to restored Dutch control.

w4-800806.name: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814 - return of Dutch East Indies
w4-800806.blurb: The Anglo-Dutch Convention of 13 August 1814 (Convention of London) obligated Britain to return the Dutch East Indies, which it had occupied after invading Java in 1811 during the Napoleonic Wars. Britain had governed Java and other islands under Stamford Raffles from 1811 to 1816; the treaty restored Dutch sovereignty, confirmed in the transfer of 1816. The dataset records this transition from 'British Colonial Empire' to 'Dutch East Indies' in 1812-1814, which corresponds to the formal agreement period.

citations.label: French and British interregnum in the Dutch East Indies - Wikipedia

w4-800808.name: Ottoman suppression of the First Serbian Uprising
w4-800808.blurb: The First Serbian Uprising (1804-1813) created a de facto autonomous Serbia. After the 1812 Treaty of Bucharest freed Ottoman forces, they launched an offensive; Belgrade fell on 7 October 1813 and Serbia reverted to direct Ottoman rule within the 1812-1814 window, until the Second Uprising of 1815. Well attested.

w4-800810.name: Treaty of Kiel – Norwegian independence from Denmark-Norway
w4-800810.blurb: The Treaty of Kiel (January 1814) ended the Napoleonic Wars for Denmark-Norway, requiring Denmark to cede Norway to Sweden. Norwegians refused the transfer, convened the Eidsvoll Constitutional Assembly, and declared independence on 17 May 1814; after a brief war Sweden accepted Norwegian self-government under the Union of Sweden and Norway (November 1814). This dissolved the Denmark-Norway state and re-established the Kingdom of Norway. Window py=1812, y=1814 fits.

w4-800811.name: Treaty of Kiel / Swedish-Norwegian Union (1814)
w4-800811.blurb: The Treaty of Kiel (14 January 1814) compelled Denmark to cede Norway to Sweden; after Norway's brief independence and the Convention of Moss, Norway entered a personal union with Sweden in November 1814 under the Bernadotte dynasty. The worklist's Swedish Empire→Kingdom of Norway at (14.1°E, 64.2°N) reflects this transfer of Norwegian territory into the new Kingdom of Norway under the union.

citations.label: Union between Sweden and Norway – Wikipedia

w4-800812.name: Treaty of Kiel / Swedish-Norwegian Union (1814)
w4-800812.blurb: The Treaty of Kiel (14 January 1814) and the Convention of Moss (August 1814) transferred Norway from Denmark into a personal union with Sweden under the new Kingdom of Norway. This second entry at (16.1°E, 64.2°N), central Norway, reflects another geographic segment of the same 1812–1814 territorial transfer.

citations.label: Union between Sweden and Norway – Wikipedia

w4-900001.name: Egyptian-Ottoman campaign against Diriyah / Ibrahim Pasha's conquest
w4-900001.blurb: Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptian-Ottoman army besieged and sacked Diriyah in September 1818, destroying the capital of the First Saudi State; the remnant Saudi political entity reconstituted as the Emirate of Nejd under a reduced territorial footprint, explaining the transfer of Diriyah-labelled territory to the Emirate of Nejd by the 1818 snapshot.

w4-900002.name: Congress of Angostura / Battle of Boyacá
w4-900002.blurb: Simón Bolívar's victory at the Battle of Boyacá (August 7, 1819) shattered Spanish military power in New Granada, prompting Viceroy Sámano to flee Bogotá. On December 17, 1819, the Congress of Angostura formally constituted Gran Colombia, incorporating the former Viceroyalty of New Granada.

w4-900003.name: Battle of Tacuarembó
w4-900003.blurb: On 22 January 1820 Luso-Brazilian forces under the Count of Figueira annihilated the Artiguist army at Tacuarembó, killing or capturing over 1,000 of ~2,500 men. This decisive defeat ended Federal League resistance in the Banda Oriental, enabling Portugal to formally annex the territory as the Cisplatina Province later in 1821.

w4-900005.name: Seku Amadu's Jihad — Battle of Noukouma and founding of Massina Empire
w4-900005.blurb: Seku Amadu Lobbo launched a jihad against the animist Bambara (Bamana) Empire, decisively defeating the Bambara coalition at the Battle of Noukouma in 1818 and capturing Djenné that same year. By 1820 he established his capital at Hamdullahi, carving the Massina (Dina) theocratic state out of Bambara-controlled territory in the Inner Niger Delta.

w4-900006.name: Defeat of Artigas and collapse of the Federal League
w4-900006.blurb: Portuguese-Brazilian forces defeated José Gervasio Artigas's Federal League (Liga Federal) in late 1819–1820; Artigas fled to Paraguay in September 1820 after the Battle of Tacuarembó. The Banda Oriental and the Entre Ríos/Corrientes territories reverted to the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata's orbit.

w4-900010.name: General Treaty of Peace (1820)
w4-900010.blurb: Following the Anglo-Wahhabi War of 1819–1820, Britain's naval campaign destroyed First Saudi State authority on the Gulf coast. On 8 January 1820 the maritime sheikhdoms (Qawasim, Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Ajman, Umm al-Quwain) signed the General Treaty of Peace with Britain, establishing the Trucial Coast under British suzerainty and ending Wahhabi/Diriyah pretensions over the lower Gulf littoral.

w4-900013.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War / Rajput Subsidiary Alliances
w4-900013.blurb: In 1818, following the Third Anglo-Maratha War, the East India Company extended its protection treaties to the Rajput states of Rajputana (centroid 73.7°E, 27.4°N), whose nominal Mughal overlordship lapsed; the formerly Mughal-suzerain territories were mapped to the British Empire in Cliopatria as subsidiary alliance agreements replaced Mughal jurisdiction.

w4-900014.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War
w4-900014.blurb: The Third Anglo-Maratha War ended on 9 April 1819 with the fall of Asirgarh Fort; the British East India Company dissolved the Maratha Confederacy, absorbed the Peshwa's territories into the Bombay Presidency, and subordinated the remaining Maratha princes through subsidiary alliances.

w4-900015.name: General Treaty of Peace (1820) / Collapse of First Saudi State
w4-900015.blurb: The Egyptian-Ottoman sack of Diriyah (1818) and the subsequent British General Treaty of Peace (January 1820) destroyed First Saudi authority over the Qatar peninsula; the Al Thani tribe, free of Wahhabi suzerainty, began consolidating authority over the Qatar interior that the Emirate of Diriyah had claimed.

w4-900016.name: Destruction of the Emirate of Diriyah by the Ottoman-Egyptian Expedition
w4-900016.blurb: Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptian army, acting on Ottoman orders, sacked Diriyah in September 1818, executing the Saudi emir Abdullah ibn Saud and demolishing the capital, thereby ending the First Saudi State and restoring Ottoman suzerainty over central Arabia.

w4-900017.name: Chilean War of Independence — Capture of Valdivia
w4-900017.blurb: Following the decisive patriot victory at the Battle of Maipú (5 April 1818), Chilean independence was formally declared, but royalist forces held the southern fortress of Valdivia until Lord Cochrane's surprise assault of February 1820 eliminated the last major royalist stronghold in Chile proper. The prev_year 1819 → 1820 transition reflects this final consolidation of Chilean control.

w4-900018.name: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 — partition of Johor/Riau
w4-900018.blurb: The Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 17 March 1824 divided the former Johor Sultanate's territory between British and Dutch spheres: Britain retained the Malay Peninsula (including Singapore, founded 1819) and the Netherlands took the Riau-Lingga archipelago. The split in the dataset as Johor-to-Riau-Lingga reflects the atlas re-attributing the southern continental/island zone to Riau-Lingga after this 1824 partition.

w4-900019.name: Sikh conquest of Kashmir — Battle of Shopian
w4-900019.blurb: After a failed attempt in 1814, Maharaja Ranjit Singh's Sikh Empire conquered Kashmir from the Durrani (Afghan) Empire in 1819. On 3 July 1819 the Sikh army fought the Battle of Shopian, defeating Afghan commander Jabbar Khan; on 15 July Sikh forces entered Srinagar. The betrayal of Afghan governor Azim Khan's revenue minister, Birbal Dhar, who invited Ranjit Singh to intervene, facilitated the conquest. Kashmir, which had suffered under harsh Durrani rule since 1752, became part of the Sikh Empire and a major source of revenue.

w4-900024.name: Dutch abolition of the Sultanate of Palembang
w4-900024.blurb: The Dutch East Indies colonial government fought a series of expeditions against the Sultanate of Palembang (Sumatra, lat -2.9, lng 104.6) after Sultan Mahmud Badaruddin II resisted Dutch claims. A major Dutch expedition in 1821 under General de Kock defeated and exiled Badaruddin II, installing a puppet sultan. The Dutch formally abolished the Sultanate on 7 October 1823 after the puppet ruler also proved uncooperative, integrating Palembang directly into the colonial administration of the Dutch East Indies.

w4-900026.name: Haitian occupation of Santo Domingo (1822)
w4-900026.blurb: After the brief declaration of 'Spanish Haiti' under José Núñez de Cáceres in November 1821, Haitian President Jean-Pierre Boyer marched troops into the east of Hispaniola. On 9 February 1822 Boyer entered Santo Domingo, ending Spanish colonial rule and uniting the island under Haiti. The occupation lasted until Dominican independence in 1844.

citations.label: Haitian occupation of Santo Domingo — Wikipedia

w4-900028.name: Mexican War of Independence and declaration of the First Mexican Empire
w4-900028.blurb: After eleven years of insurgency, Mexico achieved independence from Spain on 27 September 1821 with the entry of the Army of the Three Guarantees into Mexico City. Agustín de Iturbide, co-author of the Plan of Iguala, was proclaimed Emperor Agustín I on 18 May 1822, inaugurating the First Mexican Empire. The empire covered virtually the entirety of New Spain, including New Mexico, California, and Central America, constituting one of the largest territorial transfers of the era.

w4-900030.name: Khiva–Bukhara warfare and Khivan gains in the Amu Darya basin
w4-900030.blurb: Khiva and Bukhara warred chronically over the Amu Darya basin in the early 19th century; Muhammad Rahim Khan I of Khiva (r.1806–1825), having decisively beaten Bukhara in 1806, kept pressing Bukharan border territory into the early 1820s. No single named battle marks c.1820–1822, but the recorded Emirate of Bukhara→Khanate of Khiva transfer at lng 63.5, lat 37.6 fits this documented era of Khivan expansion.

w4-900033.name: Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan; fall of the Funj Sultanate
w4-900033.blurb: In July 1820 Muhammad Ali sent his son Ismail Pasha south into the Nile Valley; after defeating the Shayqiyya at Korti (Nov 1820), Egyptian forces reached the region by spring 1821, and the last Funj sultan Badi VII surrendered on 14 June 1821, ending Funj rule. Matches worklist transition Funj Sultanate -> Muhammad Ali dynasty (1820-1822); coords lng 32.2 lat 14.5 are the Sennar/Sudan region.

w4-900037.name: Kokand Khanate Expansion into Southern Kazakhstan
w4-900037.blurb: Under Khan Umar (r. 1811–1822) and his successor Muhammad Ali Khan, the Khanate of Kokand expanded northward into Kazakh territories in the early 1820s, capturing Turkistan (1816) and building fortresses across southern Kazakhstan (coords 70E/43.2N). The Great Kazakh Horde, squeezed between Kokand and Russia, accepted Russian protection, leading to the abolition of Kazakh khanate authority in 1822.

w4-900040.name: Talpur dynasty assertion of full independence from the declining Durrani Empire
w4-900040.blurb: The Talpurs ruled Sindh from 1783 under nominal Durrani suzerainty. As the Durrani Empire fragmented amid Sikh expansion in the early 19th century, the Talpurs ceased meaningful tribute and operated as fully independent rulers of Sindh by c. 1820-1822 (annexed by Britain in 1843). The Durrani-to-Talpur transition (28.3N) is within the window (1820-1822).

w4-900042.name: San Martín's liberation of Peru from the Spanish Empire
w4-900042.blurb: General José de San Martín entered Lima in July 1821 after Spanish Viceroy de la Serna evacuated the city, and formally declared Peruvian independence on 28 July 1821. The remaining Spanish forces in the Andes highlands were not defeated until Bolívar's victory at Ayacucho in December 1824. Cliopatria's 1820-1822 window (Spanish Empire to Republic of Peru, centroid lat -12.5, lng -72.5) captures the initial phase of Spanish territorial loss in Peru.

w4-900047.name: Independence of Central America from the First Mexican Empire
w4-900047.blurb: Central America was annexed to Agustin de Iturbide's First Mexican Empire from January 1822 amid resistance (notably in El Salvador). After Iturbide abdicated in March 1823, General Vicente Filisola convoked a constituent assembly which on 1 July 1823 declared Central America independent as the United Provinces of Central America; a federal constitution followed in November 1824 (Chiapas remained with Mexico). The worklist transfer (First Mexican Empire to United Provinces of Central America, 1822-1824) captures this sequence.

citations.label: Federal Republic of Central America – Wikipedia
Central America under Mexican rule – Wikipedia

w4-900048.name: Brazilian independence and reorganization of the Portuguese Empire (1822–1824)
w4-900048.blurb: Prince Regent Dom Pedro declared Brazilian independence on 7 September 1822, but Portuguese garrisons held out until the last surrendered in January 1824. The from/to transition ('Portuguese Empire' to 'Kingdom of Portugal') reflects Brazil's departure and the reorganization of Portugal's remaining holdings as direct metropolitan possessions; the coordinates fall in the Atlantic/African sphere rather than Brazil, but the underlying 1822 independence event is well attested.

w4-900049.name: Wars of South American Independence: liberation of Upper Peru and Bolivia
w4-900049.blurb: Simón Bolívar's campaigns from Gran Colombia liberated Peru with the Battle of Junín (6 August 1824) and the Battle of Ayacucho (9 December 1824), ending Spanish rule in South America. In August 1825 the Congress of Upper Peru created Bolivia. Cliopatria records the 1822-1824 window when Gran Colombia's forces effectively replaced Spanish control over the Andean highlands (centroid lat -17.5, lng -64), matching the Spanish Empire to Gran Colombia transfer.

w4-900050.name: Fall of the First Mexican Empire — Constitution of 1824
w4-900050.blurb: Emperor Agustín de Iturbide, facing army revolts and financial collapse, abdicated on 19 March 1823, ending the First Mexican Empire after less than two years. A Constituent Congress subsequently drafted a federal republican constitution, enacted on 4 October 1824, which established the United Mexican States (Estados Unidos Mexicanos) as a federal republic. Mexico's first president, Guadalupe Victoria, took office under this constitution, formally replacing the imperial government with the Federated Republic of Mexico.

w4-900051.name: Creation of Bolivia from Upper Peru
w4-900051.blurb: Following the patriot victory at Ayacucho (9 December 1824) and Sucre's campaign into Upper Peru in early 1825, an assembly of Upper Peruvian provinces voted for independence and declared Bolivia on 6 August 1825, named after Simón Bolívar. Matches the Republic of Peru → Bolivia transfer in the 1824-1825 window.

w4-900052.name: Declaration of Independence of Bolivia (separation from Peru)
w4-900052.blurb: After the royalist collapse at Ayacucho (Dec 1824), Antonio Jose de Sucre's Bolivarian army—operating under Gran Colombian command—occupied the former Audiencia de Charcas (Upper Peru), defeating the last royalists at Tumusla (2 April 1825). On 6 August 1825 a constituent assembly at Chuquisaca declared independence, creating the Republic of Bolivar (Bolivia) on the ~335,000 km2 Altiplano around Lake Titicaca rather than reverting Charcas to either Peru or Gran Colombia.

citations.label: Wikipedia – Declaration of Independence of Bolivia

w4-900054.name: Ottoman withdrawal and founding of Second Saudi State (1824)
w4-900054.blurb: After Ibrahim Pasha destroyed the First Saudi State and captured Diriyah in 1818, the Ottomans held Najd briefly but withdrew as it proved costly. By 1824 Turki ibn Abdullah al-Saud reestablished the Second Saudi State (Emirate of Nejd) with Riyadh as capital, expelling the remaining garrison. Matches the Ottoman Empire → Emirate of Nejd transfer in the 1824-1825 window.

w4-900055.name: First Anglo-Burmese War
w4-900055.blurb: The First Anglo-Burmese War (1824–1826) broke out after Burmese forces threatened British India's northeastern frontier. British forces under General Archibald Campbell captured Rangoon in May 1824 and advanced up the Irrawaddy. The Treaty of Yandabo (February 24, 1826) compelled Burma to cede Arakan (coords ~93E/22.4N), Tenasserim, Assam, and Manipur to the British East India Company, Britain's first major territorial gain at Burma's expense.

w4-900056.name: Treaty of Yandabo — First Anglo-Burmese War
w4-900056.blurb: Following Britain's victory in the First Anglo-Burmese War (1824–1826), Burma signed the Treaty of Yandabo on 24 February 1826, ceding Arakan (Rakhine) and Tenasserim to the British East India Company. The centroid at 93°E, 22.4°N corresponds to Arakan, the largest territorial block ceded under this treaty.

w4-900060.name: Dost Mohammad Khan seizes Kabul and founds Emirate of Afghanistan (1826)
w4-900060.blurb: The Durrani Empire fragmented after Shah Mahmud had the Barakzai chief Fateh Khan murdered in 1818. Fateh Khan's brother Dost Mohammad Khan captured Kabul in 1826 and assumed the title of Emir, founding the Barakzai dynasty and the Emirate of Afghanistan; the remnant Sadozai Durranis were confined to Herat. The dataset records the Durrani Empire → Emirate of Afghanistan transfer in the 1826–1828 window.

w4-900061.name: Convention of Akkerman (1826)
w4-900061.blurb: The Convention of Akkerman, signed on 7 October 1826, forced the Ottoman Empire to confirm Russian protectorate rights over the Danubian Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia. Turkey agreed to withdraw its forces from the principalities, grant the hospodars seven-year terms removable only with Russian consent, and give Russia veto power over their appointment, placing Moldavia firmly under Russian-supervised governance while Ottoman nominal suzerainty was preserved. The convention was repudiated by Sultan Mahmud II in late 1827, triggering the Russo-Turkish War of 1828-29.

w4-900064.name: Foundation of the Caucasian Imamate — Ghazi Muhammad's uprising
w4-900064.blurb: In 1828 Imam Ghazi Muhammad founded the Caucasian Imamate in Dagestan to resist Russian expansion into the North Caucasus. The Caucasian foothills shifted from Russian Empire control toward the new Imamate's resistance sphere within the 1826-1828 window. Attested.

w4-900069.name: Lao-Siamese War (Chao Anouvong Rebellion) and Siamese conquest of Vientiane
w4-900069.blurb: In 1827 Chao Anouvong of Vientiane, backed by Nguyễn Vietnam, launched a rebellion against Siamese suzerainty. Siamese forces counterattacked, sacked and razed Vientiane in 1828, and drove Nguyễn influence out of the middle Mekong basin. The territory at ~106°E/17.4°N (Vietnamese–Lao border zone) that had been under shared Nguyễn suzerainty fell under direct Siamese control after the war.

w4-900070.name: Congress Poland's autonomous status before the November Uprising (1815–1830)
w4-900070.blurb: The Congress of Vienna (1815) established Congress Poland as a nominally autonomous kingdom in personal union with Russia, with its own constitution, Sejm, and army. The data transition 'Russian Empire' to 'Poles' near Warsaw reflects this distinct autonomous status, which the dataset marks before the November Uprising of 1830, after which Russian control was reasserted.

w4-900071.name: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 - Dutch Consolidation of the Indies
w4-900071.blurb: The Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 partitioned Southeast Asian colonial spheres: the Dutch ceded Malacca to Britain and agreed not to treaty with Malay Peninsula rulers, while Britain withdrew from Sumatra and Riau. The coordinates point to Java/Sumatra borderlands, where polities associated with the former Malacca sphere were formally incorporated into the Dutch East Indies framework. The 1828-1830 window reflects Dutch East Indies consolidation after the treaty.

w4-900072.name: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 — Transfer of British Possessions in Sumatra and Java
w4-900072.blurb: The Surakarta Sunanate (Nagari Kasunanan Surakarta Hadiningrat) was a Dutch protectorate in the interior of Central Java, not a party to the 1824 Anglo-Dutch Treaty, which dealt with British and Dutch coastal settlements in Sumatra and Malacca. Around this period the Dutch colonial state steadily tightened its grip on the Central Javanese courts; Surakarta's major land cessions to the Netherlands came as a penalty after the Java War (1825-1830), when the court was forced to surrender much of its remaining territory.

w4-900074.name: July Revolution of 1830
w4-900074.blurb: The July Revolution (Les Trois Glorieuses, 27-29 July 1830) overthrew the Bourbon King Charles X of France after he issued the Four Ordinances suspending press freedom and dissolving the Chamber of Deputies. Barricade fighting in Paris forced Charles X to abdicate on 2 August 1830, and Louis-Philippe of the Orleans branch was installed as king, inaugurating the July Monarchy. French colonial possessions passed from Bourbon to Orleanist administration at this moment.

w4-900078.name: Second Saudi State (Emirate of Nejd) seizure of al-Hasa
w4-900078.blurb: After the Ottoman destruction of the First Saudi State (1818), Turki bin Abdullah Al Saud founded the Second Saudi State (Emirate of Nejd) and by 1830 reconquered al-Ahsa/Eastern Arabia — the region around Bahrain (49.2,26.6) — reasserting Saudi control over the Gulf coast. This matches the from→to (Bahrain → Emirate of Nejd) in the 1828–1830 window.

citations.label: Turki bin Abdullah Al Saud – Wikipedia

w4-900079.name: Dissolution of Gran Colombia — Venezuela separates (1829–1831)
w4-900079.blurb: Riven by regionalist conflict, José Antonio Páez led Venezuela to formally separate from Gran Colombia on 22 September 1830; Bolívar resigned in May 1830 and died in December, and Gran Colombia was formally dissolved in 1831. The dataset records the Gran Colombia → Venezuela transfer in the 1831–1834 window, slightly lagging the 1830 separation.

w4-900081.name: Dissolution of Gran Colombia / Peru-Gran Colombia border settlement
w4-900081.blurb: When Gran Colombia dissolved in 1830-1831, Ecuador claimed succession to its territorial rights, including Gran Colombia's claim over Maynas (later Loreto) in the upper Amazon won at Tarqui and recognized in the 1829 Treaty of Guayaquil. The Amazonian zone around lat -3.1, lng -74.1 thus became part of Ecuador's inherited claim, even though Peru—disputing Ecuador's right to succeed Gran Colombia—remained in de facto possession, fueling the long Ecuador-Peru border dispute.

w4-900082.name: Dissolution of Gran Colombia and emergence of the Republic of Ecuador (1830-1831)
w4-900082.blurb: Gran Colombia dissolved in 1830-1831; Quito declared independence as the Republic of Ecuador on 13 May 1830 and promulgated its first constitution on 22 September 1830. The from->to (Gran Colombia -> Republic of Ecuador) at -78.2, -1.8 (near Quito) matches this; the dataset window 1831-1834 sits just after the formal separation, consistent with the consolidation of the new republic.

w4-900083.name: Treaty of Adrianople (1829) and Organic Statutes (1831-1832)
w4-900083.blurb: The Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829), ending the Russo-Turkish War of 1828-29, confirmed Russian military occupation and protectorate over Moldavia and Wallachia. The occupying Russian administration under Pavel Kiselyov then imposed the Organic Statutes (Regulamentul Organic), quasi-constitutional documents that modernised the principalities' administrations while embedding Russian influence. Russian forces withdrew by 1834 after the Organic Statutes came into force, formally returning day-to-day governance to Moldavia under its hospodar while Russia retained supervisory rights.

w4-900089.name: End of Russian administration of Wallachia following the Treaty of Adrianople (withdrawal completed 1834)
w4-900089.blurb: After the Treaty of Adrianople (1829), Russia administered Wallachia through General Pavel Kiselyov, who introduced the Organic Statute in 1831. Russian troops withdrew in 1834, returning effective autonomy to the Principality of Wallachia under Ottoman suzerainty and Russian guarantee (Russian Empire -> Principality of Wallachia), matching the [1831,1834] window. The coordinates lng 25.3, lat 44.6 are central Wallachia.

w4-900091.name: Suppression of the November Uprising and abolition of Polish autonomy (1831–1832)
w4-900091.blurb: After the November Uprising (1830–31) was crushed at Warsaw in September 1831, Tsar Nicholas I issued the Organic Statute of 1832, abolishing the Polish constitution, dissolving the Sejm and Polish army, and incorporating Congress Poland as a province of the Russian Empire. The coordinates near Warsaw mark the Congress Poland heartland reverting to direct Russian control.

w4-900092.name: First Egyptian–Ottoman War; Egyptian conquest of Syria and Arabia
w4-900092.blurb: In 1831 Muhammad Ali of Egypt launched a campaign against the Ottoman Empire; his son Ibrahim Pasha defeated Ottoman forces at Homs (July 1832) and advanced into Anatolia. The Convention of Kütahya (May 1833) awarded Muhammad Ali Crete, Aleppo, Damascus, Sidon, Tripoli, and Adana. Matches worklist transition Ottoman Empire -> Muhammad Ali dynasty (1831-1834); coords lng 39.1 lat 27.3 = Hejaz/western Arabia also seized.

w4-900093.name: Sikh Empire capture of Peshawar (1834)
w4-900093.blurb: Maharaja Ranjit Singh of the Sikh Empire dispatched General Hari Singh Nalwa to seize Peshawar from the Peshawar Barakzai Sardars (Afghan rulers aligned with Dost Mohammad Khan's Emirate) on 6 May 1834. Hari Singh Nalwa occupied the city without a pitched battle and was appointed governor. Dost Mohammad Khan subsequently declared a holy war but withdrew in 1835 without retaking it. The region thus shifted from Afghan to Sikh control. (The dataset coordinate lat 33.8, lng 74.8 actually falls in the Kashmir zone rather than Peshawar proper, but the Afghan-to-Sikh transfer at this date is firmly attested.)

w4-900095.name: Foundation of Peru-Bolivian Confederation (residual Spanish territory)
w4-900095.blurb: A small residual zone (~3,900 km², centroid lat -14.1, lng -72.7) in highland Peru still nominally attributed to Spain in the atlas was absorbed into the Peru-Bolivian Confederation when Santa Cruz decreed its formation in October 1836, representing the last formal extinguishing of Spanish claims in this Andean region.

w4-900096.name: Foundation of the Peru-Bolivian Confederation
w4-900096.blurb: When Marshal Andres de Santa Cruz decreed the Peru-Bolivian Confederation at Lima on 28 October 1836, the former Republic of Peru entered the new union as its two Peruvian member states: North Peru (proclaimed at Huaura, 11 August 1836) and South Peru (proclaimed at Sicuani, 17 March 1836). These joined the third constituent state, Bolivia, with Tacna as the federal capital; the union was confirmed by the Pact of Tacna in 1837.

w4-900099.name: Ottoman reincorporation of Tripolitania
w4-900099.blurb: In May 1835 the Ottomans exploited a Karamanli succession crisis, deposed Ali II Karamanli, and ended 124 years of semi-autonomous Karamanli rule, restoring direct Ottoman administration. Tripoli/the Libyan coast near lng 13.5 E / lat 32.4 N passed from the Karamanli dynasty to the Ottoman Empire, matching the [1834,1836] window.

w4-900101.name: Sikh conquest of Jamrud / expansion to Khyber Pass
w4-900101.blurb: Hari Singh Nalwa, commander of the Sikh Khalsa Army, captured the fort of Jamrud at the mouth of the Khyber Pass in late 1836, extending the Sikh Empire's frontier to the border of the Emirate of Afghanistan. The Battle of Jamrud (30 April 1837) repulsed an Afghan counter-attack. The from=Emirate of Afghanistan / to=Sikh Empire and 1834-1836 window match this westernmost Sikh expansion following the 1834 capture of Peshawar.

w4-900104.name: First Anglo-Afghan War; British-backed Shah Shuja displaces Dost Mohammad
w4-900104.blurb: In 1838 Lord Auckland ordered the invasion of Afghanistan to replace Emir Dost Mohammad Khan with the pro-British Durrani pretender Shah Shuja. British forces captured Ghazni and Kabul in 1839, and Shah Shuja was enthroned in August 1839; Dost Mohammad surrendered on 2 November 1840 and was exiled. Matches worklist transition Emirate of Afghanistan -> Durrani Dynasty (1838-1840).

w4-900105.name: Honduras secession from the Federal Republic of Central America
w4-900105.blurb: The Federal Republic of Central America dissolved between 1838 and 1841 amid civil war between Liberal and Conservative factions. Honduras declared independence from the Federation on 26 October 1838 as Conservative opposition to Liberal president Francisco Morazan intensified. Nicaragua, Honduras, and Costa Rica all seceded in 1838, with Guatemala formally dissolving the federation in 1839. Honduras became a sovereign republic under Francisco Ferrera, consolidating its territory independently.

citations.label: Federal Republic of Central America – Wikipedia

w4-900106.name: Declaration of the Republic of the Rio Grande
w4-900106.blurb: On January 17, 1840, Federalist leaders from the northern Mexican states of Coahuila, Nuevo León, and Tamaulipas met near Laredo and declared independence from Centralist Mexico, forming the Republic of the Rio Grande with Laredo as its capital. The rebellion was a direct reaction to Santa Anna's centralist constitution of 1836, which abrogated the federalist Constitution of 1824. The republic never received international recognition and controlled its claimed territory only intermittently during its 283-day existence. It was suppressed by Centralist General Mariano Arista, and rebel leader Antonio Canales surrendered at Camargo on November 6, 1840. The dataset records this secession (Federated Republic of Mexico → Republic of the Rio Grande) over a 1838–1840 window.

citations.label: Republic of the Rio Grande – Wikipedia
Texas State Historical Association – Republic of the Rio Grande

w4-900107.name: War of the Confederation: Battle of Yungay and dissolution of the Peru-Bolivian Confederation
w4-900107.blurb: Chilean forces under General Manuel Bulnes crushed the Peru-Bolivian Confederation's army at the Battle of Yungay on 20 January 1839, forcing Supreme Protector Andrés de Santa Cruz into exile. Peruvian president Gamarra formally declared the Confederation dissolved on 25 August 1839. Bolivia re-emerged as a separate state (Cliopatria centroid lat -16.3, lng -65.6),

w4-900108.name: First Anglo-Afghan War and Afghan loss of frontier territory to Sikh influence (1838–1840)
w4-900108.blurb: The First Anglo-Afghan War (1838–1842) began when British India, allied with Ranjit Singh's Sikh Empire, invaded Afghanistan to replace Dost Mohammed with Shah Shuja. British-Sikh forces marched through Punjab and the Khyber Pass in 1838–1839 and took Kabul by August 1839. The Hazara / upper Indus frontier territory passed under firmer Sikh-British influence during this period before the British withdrew in 1842.

w4-900109.name: Egyptian–Ottoman conquest of the Second Saudi State (Najd)
w4-900109.blurb: Ibrahim Pasha (son of Muhammad Ali of Egypt) campaigned to subdue the revived Second Saudi State in 1837–1838. Khalid ibn Saud, backed by Egyptian military support, defeated Faisal bin Turki at Riyadh in 1838 and was installed as a pro-Egyptian ruler. Egyptian forces held Nejd until the Convention of London (1840) compelled Muhammad Ali to withdraw. Matches the Nejd → Muhammad Ali dynasty transfer in the 1838-1840 window.

w4-900110.name: Egyptian-Ottoman Conquest of Najd
w4-900110.blurb: As Egyptian forces under Muhammad Ali extended into eastern Arabia during the 1838-1839 campaigns against the Second Saudi State, Egyptian occupation of Al-Hasa pulled Bahrain into Egypt's orbit. In 1839 the Bahraini ruler Abdullah bin Ahmad Al Khalifa signed a treaty acknowledging Egyptian supremacy and redirecting the zakat formerly paid to the Emirate of Nejd, with a Turkish agent stationed on the island; this brief submission lapsed after the Convention of London (1840) forced Egypt's withdrawal from Arabia.

w4-900112.name: Costa Rica secedes from the Federal Republic of Central America
w4-900112.blurb: The Federal Republic of Central America (formerly the United Provinces of Central America) disintegrated under internal civil war. On 30 May 1838 the Federal Congress allowed member states to organise as they wished, and Costa Rica (lat 9.6, lng -84.3) withdrew and proclaimed itself sovereign in 1838, becoming the 'Free State of Costa Rica.' By 1840 the federation had effectively ceased to exist. The dataset records Costa Rican territory transferring from the United Provinces to the independent Costa Rica.

citations.label: Federal Republic of Central America – Wikipedia
Free State of Costa Rica – Wikipedia

w4-900113.name: British Conquest of Sindh
w4-900113.blurb: The British East India Company under General Charles Napier defeated the Talpur Amirs of Sindh at the Battle of Miani (17 February 1843) and the Battle of Hyderabad (24 March 1843), annexing Sindh to British India. The data window (py=1838) reflects earlier British pressure: the British seized Karachi in February 1839 and used the pretext of the First Anglo-Afghan War to impose subsidiary treaties. Full annexation was completed in 1843.

w4-900118.name: Ottoman reassertion of direct rule over Tripolitania / Tanzimat consolidation
w4-900118.blurb: In May 1835 Ottoman forces overthrew the last Karamanli ruler (Ali II) and reimposed direct administration over Tripolitania, after which a prolonged tribal revolt persisted into the 1840s. The 1838–1840 worklist window captures the consolidation of direct Ottoman authority over the interior (lng 28.3, lat 21.6, toward Fezzan) in the wake of the 1835 takeover and early Tanzimat reorganisation. The named event proper is 1835; the window reflects ongoing consolidation rather than a single sharp transition.

w4-900119.name: Ottoman reconquest of Tripoli ends Karamanli rule
w4-900119.blurb: Ottoman forces under Necib Pasha landed at Tripoli in May 1835, deposed Ali II Karamanli, and ended the 124-year semi-autonomous Karamanli dynasty, restoring direct Ottoman rule over Tripolitania. Direct administration was extended eastward over Benghazi and Cyrenaica — the region of this parcel — and into the interior over the following years, which is why the atlas records the change only between its 1838 and 1840 snapshots, a few years after the decisive 1835 reconquest.

w4-900120.name: Dissolution of the Federal Republic of Central America — Nicaraguan Secession
w4-900120.blurb: Nicaragua seceded from the Federal Republic of Central America (United Provinces of Central America) on November 5, 1838, one of the first states to break away as the federation unraveled under civil war and Rafael Carrera's conservative uprising. The federation was effectively dissolved by 1840. Coords (-85.4, 12.8) fall in Nicaragua.

citations.label: Federal Republic of Central America – Wikipedia

w4-900121.name: Dissolution of the United Provinces of Central America — Nicaragua
w4-900121.blurb: El Salvador remained one of the last states committed to the federal union as the United Provinces of Central America disintegrated amid civil war in 1838-1840. After Nicaragua, Honduras, and Costa Rica seceded in 1838 and the federal congress authorized the states to constitute themselves freely (decree of 30 May 1838), El Salvador continued to host the federal government and only emerged as a fully separate Republic of El Salvador with the lapse of the federation by 1841.

citations.label: Wikipedia: United Provinces of Central America

w4-900123.name: Rafael Carrera annexes Los Altos into Guatemala
w4-900123.blurb: General Rafael Carrera forcibly reannexed the secessionist State of Los Altos into Guatemala on 2 April 1840, marching into Quetzaltenango; later revival attempts were suppressed through 1849. The coordinates are the western Guatemala / Quetzaltenango highlands, matching the recorded Los Altos → Guatemala transfer for 1840–1842.

w4-900127.name: Rashidi expansion at expense of Second Saudi State (Battle of Baqaa)
w4-900127.blurb: After Egyptian forces withdrew from Arabia in 1840, the Second Saudi State (Emirate of Nejd) was weakened by succession disputes. Abdullah ibn Rashid of Jabal Shammar exploited this to extend Rashidi authority over northern Qasim and adjoining areas; the Battle of Baqaa (1842), about 100 km north of Ha'il, cemented Rashidi dominance against a Qasim coalition. Matches the Nejd → Jabal Shammar transfer in the 1840-1842 window.

w4-900128.name: Egyptian Withdrawal from Arabia (London Convention 1840)
w4-900128.blurb: After the Convention of London (1840) forced the withdrawal of Egyptian forces from Arabia, the weakened Second Saudi State (Emirate of Nejd) could not hold its northern districts. Around Jabal Shammar, Abdullah ibn Rashid consolidated an autonomous emirate centered on Ha'il, founding the Rashidi dynasty that increasingly governed northern Najd in the early 1840s as Saudi authority contracted toward Riyadh.

w4-900131.name: Convention of London (1840); Egyptian withdrawal from Syria
w4-900131.blurb: Under the Convention of London (15 July 1840), Britain, Austria, Prussia, Russia, and the Ottomans required Muhammad Ali to withdraw from Syria, Arabia, Crete, and Adana. After Anglo-Austrian naval bombardment, he capitulated on 27 November 1840, returning these territories to the Ottoman Empire. Matches worklist transition Muhammad Ali dynasty -> Ottoman Empire (1840-1842); coords lng 39.3 lat 27.3 in western Arabia.

w4-900132.name: Suppression of the Republic of the Rio Grande by Centralist Mexico
w4-900132.blurb: The Republic of the Rio Grande was militarily suppressed by the Centralist Mexican government under General Mariano Arista during 1840. After defeats at the Battle of Santa Rita de Morelos (March 1840) and the loss of Laredo, rebel commander Antonio Canales capitulated at Camargo on November 6, 1840, ending the short-lived republic. The northern states of Coahuila, Nuevo León, and Tamaulipas returned to Centralist Mexican control. The dataset records this transition (Republic of the Rio Grande → Centralist Mexico) as completing between 1840 and 1842, likely reflecting the time needed to fully consolidate Centralist authority in the region.

citations.label: Republic of the Rio Grande – Wikipedia
Texas State Historical Association – Republic of the Rio Grande

w4-900133.name: Surrender of Canales and reincorporation into Centralist Mexico
w4-900133.blurb: After military reverses against General Mariano Arista's centralist forces, Antonio Canales surrendered at Camargo on 6 November 1840, dissolving the Republic of the Rio Grande and reintegrating the northeastern territory into the Centralist Republic of Mexico.

citations.label: Wikipedia: Republic of the Rio Grande

w4-900134.name: Mexico's annexation of Soconusco (former Los Altos territory)
w4-900134.blurb: The Siete Leyes (Seven Laws), promulgated on 30 December 1836, abolished Mexico's 1824 federal constitution and reorganized the country as a centralized republic, converting the federal states into departments under appointed governors. The highland region of Los Altos in Guatemala (the future Sexto Estado) was a Central American territory wholly outside Mexico and unaffected by this constitutional change.

w4-900135.name: Restoration of Dost Mohammad Khan; end of British-backed Durrani interlude
w4-900135.blurb: After the catastrophic British retreat from Kabul in January 1842 and the Army of Retribution's withdrawal by the end of 1842, the British-installed Durrani ruler Shah Shuja was assassinated. Dost Mohammad Khan, released from Indian captivity, returned and resumed power in Kabul, restoring the Barakzai emirate. Matches worklist transition Durrani Dynasty -> Emirate of Afghanistan (1842-1846).

w4-900136.name: Treaty of Ponche Verde – End of the Farroupilha (Ragamuffin) War
w4-900136.blurb: The Riograndense Republic (República Rio-Grandense / Piratini Republic) was a secessionist state proclaimed in Rio Grande do Sul in 1836 during the Ragamuffin War (Farroupilha). After a decade of conflict, negotiations led by the Marquis of Caxias concluded with the Treaty of Ponche Verde, signed on March 1, 1845, at Dom Pedrito. The treaty granted full amnesty to rebels, incorporated them into the imperial army, and reintegrated Rio Grande do Sul into the Empire of Brazil. The dataset records the transition (Riograndense Republic → Empire of Brazil) completing by 1846, consistent with the time needed to implement the treaty's terms.

w4-900137.name: Treaty of Amritsar (1846) – Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh after First Anglo-Sikh War
w4-900137.blurb: The First Anglo-Sikh War (1845–46) ended with the defeat of the Sikh Empire, which was forced to pay a heavy indemnity it could not afford. In lieu of payment, the Sikh Empire ceded Kashmir to the British East India Company, which then sold the territory to Gulab Singh of Jammu on 16 March 1846 via the Treaty of Amritsar for 7.5 million rupees. Gulab Singh thus became the first Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir under British suzerainty.

w4-900138.name: Treaty of Amritsar (1846) — sale of Kashmir to Gulab Singh
w4-900138.blurb: By the Treaty of Amritsar of 16 March 1846, the British East India Company transferred to the Dogra chief Gulab Singh the hill country between the Indus and the Ravi - including Kashmir - for 75 lakh rupees, creating the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir under Dogra rule. The Company had itself just acquired these lands from the defeated Sikh Empire under the Treaty of Lahore (9 March 1846); the Maratha Empire, dismantled in 1818, had no connection to this territory.

w4-900140.name: British Conquest of Sindh
w4-900140.blurb: General Charles Napier of the British East India Company defeated the Talpur amirs of Sindh at the Battle of Miani (17 February 1843) and the Battle of Hyderabad (24 March 1843), annexing Sindh to British India and exiling the Talpur rulers. Sindh was held by the Baloch Talpur dynasty, not by the Sikh Empire, whose domains lay to the north in the Punjab.

w4-900141.name: Dominican War of Independence from Haiti (1844)
w4-900141.blurb: On 27 February 1844, Dominican nationalists of La Trinitaria declared independence from the Haitian occupation (1822–1844), seizing Puerta del Conde in Santo Domingo. The Dominican Republic emerged as an independent state, and Haiti's subsequent counter-invasions (1844–1856) failed to reincorporate it. The worklist transfer Empire of Haiti → Dominican Republic at lng -70.3, lat 18.8 (Hispaniola) in the 1842–1846 window matches this independence.

citations.label: Haitian occupation of Santo Domingo – Wikipedia

w4-900145.name: British formalisation of Mosquito Coast protectorate
w4-900145.blurb: After the death of the Miskito king Robert Charles Frederick in 1842, Britain appointed an agent (Patrick Walker) to govern the Mosquito Coast behind the facade of an underage Miskito king, deepening its hold on the Caribbean coast of Nicaragua (-83.7, 13). By 1848 Miskito-British forces seized San Juan del Norte from Nicaragua. The worklist window (1842-1846) captures this intensified British control before the Clayton-Bulwer Treaty (1850).

w4-900146.name: British reassertion of Mosquito Protectorate
w4-900146.blurb: Following the death of the Mosquito king Robert Charles Frederic, Britain in 1844 reasserted its protectorate over the Mosquito Kingdom on the Caribbean coast of Central America, appointing Patrick Walker as consul-general at Bluefields and claiming suzerainty over coastal territory also claimed by Nicaragua. This Mosquito Coast arrangement had no connection to the Sikh Empire of the Punjab.

w4-900147.name: Restoration of the Mexican federalist constitution of 1824 amid the Mexican-American War
w4-900147.blurb: The Centralist Republic of Mexico (established 1835 under the Seven Laws) was toppled in 1846 when the outbreak of the Mexican–American War triggered a federalist revolt that forced Santa Anna's government to restore the Constitution of 1824, re-establishing the Federal Republic of Mexico. The transition occurred in August 1846, within the dataset window [1842,1846] which ends the second centralist phase (Bases Orgánicas, 1843–1846).

citations.label: Wikipedia: Second Federal Republic of Mexico

w4-900148.name: French military consolidation of Algeria, 1842–1847
w4-900148.blurb: After the French expelled resistance leader Abd al-Qadir to Morocco in 1842, his continued guerrilla campaign prompted France to defeat the Sultan of Morocco at the Battle of Isly (1844), forcing Morocco to expel Abd al-Qadir. Large swathes of the northern Saharan hinterland previously under nominal Ottoman or tribal control were progressively brought under French military administration between 1842 and 1846 as the conquest of Algeria neared completion.

w4-900150.name: Annexation of the Republic of Texas by the United States
w4-900150.blurb: Texas was annexed by the United States through a joint resolution signed by President Tyler on 1 March 1845, becoming the 28th state on 29 December 1845 with formal transfer of authority on 19 February 1846. The annexation triggered the Mexican–American War. Matches the Republic of Texas → United States transfer in the 1842-1846 window.

w4-900151.name: Declaration of Liberian independence from the American Colonization Society
w4-900151.blurb: The Colony of Liberia, managed by the American Colonization Society (ACS) since 1822 as a settlement for freed American Black people, declared independence on 26 July 1847 under governor Joseph Jenkins Roberts, becoming the first Black republic in Africa. The declaration was prompted partly by British refusal to recognise ACS authority to levy customs duties and by the colony's growing economic and political needs. Britain recognised Liberian sovereignty in 1848, France in 1852; the United States withheld recognition until 1862.

citations.label: Founding of Liberia, 1847 – U.S. Office of the Historian

w4-900154.name: Sardinian annexation of Parma during Revolutions of 1848
w4-900154.blurb: During the revolutions of 1848, Duke Charles II of Parma fled as a provisional government took power, and in May 1848 the population voted by plebiscite to unite the Duchy of Parma with the Kingdom of Sardinia, which absorbed it during the First Italian War of Independence.
