Parma was a distinct duchy from neighboring Modena and Reggio; its fusion with Piedmont-Sardinia lasted only until Austria's victory at Novara in 1849.

citations.label: Wikipedia: Revolutions of 1848 in the Italian states

w4-900155.name: Sardinian annexation of Modena during Revolutions of 1848
w4-900155.blurb: In March 1848, as revolution spread through the Italian states, Duke Francis V of Modena fled his capital, and a popular assembly voted in a June 1848 plebiscite to unite the Duchy of Modena and Reggio with the Kingdom of Sardinia during the First Italian War of Independence. The Habsburg-Este duke was restored after Austria's decisive victory at Novara in March 1849.

citations.label: Wikipedia: Duchy of Modena and Reggio
Wikipedia: Revolutions of 1848 in the Italian states

w4-900156.name: Algeria Made Integral Departments of France (Constitution of 1848)
w4-900156.blurb: The French Constitution of 4 November 1848 (Second Republic) declared the northern Mediterranean territories of Algeria to be integral departments of France. The coordinates (3.3E, 35.3N) point to northern Algeria; the dataset's 'French Equatorial Africa' loser label is a misclassification, but the administrative status change of French Algeria (~211,924 km2 in the northern zone) in 1848 is well attested and fits the 1846-1848 window.

w4-900158.name: Sicilian Revolution of 1848
w4-900158.blurb: On 12 January 1848 the Sicilian revolution erupted in Palermo; the Sicilian parliament declared independence and deposed Ferdinand II in April 1848, holding autonomous/nationalist control until the Bourbon reconquest of May 1849. Sicily near lng 14 E / lat 37.5 N briefly left Bourbon Two Sicilies control to Italian nationalists, matching the [1846,1848] window.

w4-900160.name: French Revolution of 1848 (February Revolution)
w4-900160.blurb: The February Revolution of 1848 toppled the July Monarchy when street barricades and popular uprising in Paris forced King Louis-Philippe to abdicate on 24 February 1848 and flee to England. A provisional government proclaimed the French Second Republic, instituting universal male suffrage. French overseas territories passed from July Monarchy to Second Republic control.

w4-900162.name: First Schleswig War — Holstein uprising against Denmark
w4-900162.blurb: In March 1848 the duchies of Holstein and Schleswig rebelled against Denmark, proclaiming a provisional government in Kiel and seeking German Confederation membership; Prussia intervened, driving Danish forces out. Coord 9.7E/54.5N is in Holstein. The dataset's 1846–1848 'Denmark-Norway → Duchy of Holstein' shift reflects Holstein escaping Danish control at the outbreak of the First Schleswig War (1848–1851), which ultimately ended in Danish victory (London Protocol, 1852). Event real and correctly dated.

w4-900163.name: First Schleswig-Holstein Uprising (1848) — Holstein breaks from Danish Crown
w4-900163.blurb: The Schleswig-Holstein uprising of March 1848, backed by German nationalist sentiment and later by Prussian military intervention, expelled Danish authority from the Duchy of Holstein in the opening phase of the First Schleswig War (1848-1851). Holstein was a German Confederation duchy in the Danish crown's personal union, not a Russian territory; the rebellion's provisional government aligned with Prussia and the German cause, not Russia.

w4-900165.name: Death of Kenesary Khan and final Russian absorption of the Kazakh Khanate
w4-900165.blurb: Kenesary Kasymov, the last khan of the Kazakh Khanate and leader of a decade-long resistance against Russian colonization, was killed in 1847 in Kyrgyz territory. His death ended the last organized armed resistance to Russian rule in the Kazakh steppe. Russia had already abolished the Middle Jüz khanate administratively in 1822; Kenesary's defeat in 1847 completed Russia's de facto control over all Kazakh territories (Cliopatria centroid lat 48.4, lng 67.4),

citations.label: Kazakhstan in the Russian Empire – Wikipedia

w4-900167.name: Baden Revolution of 1848–49 (Establishment of Republic of Baden)
w4-900167.blurb: In May 1849 the Baden revolution drove Grand Duke Leopold into exile, and a revolutionary provisional government briefly controlled the entire Grand Duchy of Baden, the only German state to fall wholly under republican rule during the 1848-49 upheavals. The rising was crushed by Prussian troops by July 1849; Baden was a separate state from the Kingdom of Bavaria, which had no part in this transition.

w4-900168.name: First Italian War of Independence - Battle of Novara (1849)
w4-900168.blurb: Austria decisively defeated the Kingdom of Sardinia at the Battle of Novara on 23 March 1849, forcing King Charles Albert to abdicate. The subsequent Peace of Milan (6 August 1849) restored Austrian control over Lombardy-Venetia with no territorial changes from the pre-war status quo, reversing the temporary Sardinian and revolutionary gains of 1848. The territory near Verona (lat 45.3, lng 11) corresponds to the Austrian Lombard-Venetian Kingdom whose restoration at Sardinia's expense is what the data entry records.

citations.label: First Italian War of Independence - Wikipedia

w4-900169.name: Battle of Novara — Austria defeats Sardinia, recovering Lombardy
w4-900169.blurb: Field Marshal Radetzky's Austrian army crushed the Sardinian forces at the Battle of Novara on 23 March 1849, forcing King Charles Albert to abdicate and ending the First Italian War of Independence. The ensuing armistice restored Austrian control over Lombardy, the Habsburg crown land lost during the 1848 revolts; this transition concerned Lombardy, not the Grand Duchy of Tuscany.

citations.label: Wikipedia: First Italian War of Independence

w4-900172.name: Russo-Ottoman occupation of Wallachia suppressing the 1848 Revolution
w4-900172.blurb: The Wallachian Revolution of 1848 toppled Prince Gheorghe Bibescu and proclaimed liberal reforms. Russia and the Ottomans jointly intervened: Russian troops entered Wallachia in 1848 and, with Ottoman forces, suppressed the revolutionary government, placing Wallachia under joint supervision via the Convention of Balta Liman (1849). Matches Principality of Wallachia -> Russian Empire in [1848,1849].

w4-900173.name: Russian military occupation of Wallachia during the Revolutions of 1848
w4-900173.blurb: When the Wallachian Revolution broke out in June 1848, Russia - acting as guarantor power under the Treaty of Adrianople (1829) - intervened militarily; Russian and Ottoman forces jointly suppressed the revolution by September 1848, and Russia occupied the Principality of Wallachia until 1851. This concerned Wallachia, the principality south of the Carpathians, not neighboring Moldavia.

w4-900174.name: Second Anglo-Sikh War and British annexation of the Punjab
w4-900174.blurb: The Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848–1849) ended with Lord Dalhousie's proclamation of the annexation of the Punjab on 2 April 1849, bringing the trans-Indus and north-western frontier region (atlas coords lng 72.9, lat 35) under British control. The 'from' label of Talpur Dynasty is a Cliopatria polygon artifact (the Talpurs of Sindh were conquered separately in 1843), but the genuine 1849 British consolidation of this Punjab/Kashmir-border territory falls within the recorded window.

w4-900175.name: Annexation of Sindh / Second Anglo-Sikh War
w4-900175.blurb: After the Second Anglo-Sikh War ended in British victory at the Battle of Gujrat (February 1849), the Punjab — including territories previously held by the Talpur-linked northwest frontier chiefs — was annexed to British India by proclamation on 29 March 1849. The Talpur Dynasty had already lost Sindh proper in 1843 (Battle of Miani), but the centroid at lng 72.9, lat 35 points to the northwestern frontier zone that came under British control with the 1849 Punjab annexation.

w4-900176.name: Annexation of Punjab — Second Anglo-Sikh War
w4-900176.blurb: After the Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49), the British East India Company issued the Punjab Annexation Proclamation on 29 March 1849 under Governor-General Dalhousie, transferring all Sikh territories — including the hill states around lng 76.2, lat 31.7 (Kangra/Himachal region) — from British Colonial Empire (East India Company) to direct Crown/Imperial control.

w4-900178.name: Restoration of Parma after First Italian War of Independence
w4-900178.blurb: Parma had been temporarily annexed by Piedmont-Sardinia during the First Italian War of Independence (1848-49); after Austria's victory at Novara on 23 March 1849, Austrian pressure compelled Sardinia to relinquish the Duchy, restoring the Bourbon-Parma ducal house. The Duchy of Parma was an independent restored state, not part of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

citations.label: Wikipedia: First Italian War of Independence

w4-900179.name: Dutch consolidation over the Sultanate of Sambaliung
w4-900179.blurb: The Dutch steadily extended control over northeastern Borneo through the 1840s, exploiting divisions between the Sultanates of Sambaliung and Gunung Tabur (split from Berau by Dutch divide-and-rule in 1810). Sultan Alimuddin of Sambaliung resisted and had been exiled to Makassar; by around 1849 (the year Sambaliung took its definitive name) Dutch authority and the rival Gunung Tabur were tightening their grip over the region near 118.1E, 1.7N. The nearby Dutch annexation of Kutai (1844) confirms the broader timeline.

w4-900181.name: Brazil–New Granada Treaty of 1853
w4-900181.blurb: Brazil and Peru signed the Treaty of Friendship, Commerce, and Navigation on 23 October 1851, the first agreement to fix part of the Brazil-Peru Amazon frontier on the principle of uti possidetis de facto and to regulate navigation of the Amazon. No ratified Brazil-New Granada boundary treaty existed in this period; the western Amazon boundary with New Granada (Colombia) remained disputed for decades.

w4-900182.name: Second Anglo-Burmese War
w4-900182.blurb: The Second Anglo-Burmese War (April 1852 - January 1853) was launched by Governor-General Lord Dalhousie following a manufactured naval confrontation by Commodore Lambert at Rangoon. British and Indian forces under Lieutenant-General Godwin swiftly captured Rangoon (May 1852), Prome (October 1852), and surrounding Lower Burma. In December 1852, Dalhousie unilaterally proclaimed the annexation of the Province of Pegu without any formal treaty. Lower Burma's annexation gave Britain direct control of the Irrawaddy Delta, its teak forests, and a continuous coastline from Calcutta to Singapore.

w4-900185.name: Pahang declares independence from Johor Sultanate (1853)
w4-900185.blurb: The fourth Bendahara (Chief Minister) of Pahang, Tun Ali, renounced his allegiance to the Sultan of Johor in 1853 and declared Pahang an independent state, exploiting the erosion of Johor's authority that had accelerated after the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 confined the Johor Sultan to Riau-Lingga under Dutch oversight. Tun Ali governed autonomously from Pekan, effectively dissolving the centuries-old bond between Pahang and the Johor empire. The data entry (Sultanate of Johor to Pahang Sultanate, py=1849, y=1853) reflects this declaration.

w4-900187.name: London Protocol of 1852
w4-900187.blurb: After Denmark's victory in the First Schleswig War (1848–1851), the London Protocol of 8 May 1852 was signed by the five great powers, Austria, Prussia, France, Russia, and Britain, along with Denmark and Sweden. It confirmed the Danish king as duke of Holstein (lat 54.4, lng 9.7) while requiring the duchy to remain constitutionally distinct from Denmark. Holstein was thereby returned to Danish sovereignty following the failed German uprising.

w4-900188.name: William Walker's Republic of Baja California (initial declaration)
w4-900188.blurb: This records the seizure phase of the Walker filibuster: Walker's forces detached Baja California from Mexican federal control, beginning with the capture of La Paz on 3 November 1853. The coordinates match the southern Baja peninsula. The dataset's py=1849 reflects a prior data state; the actual event is Walker's November 1853 takeover, which falls within the 1849-1853 window's terminal year.

citations.label: Expedition of William Walker to Baja California and Sonora – Wikipedia

w4-900189.name: Saudi (Nejdi/Wahhabi) occupation of the Buraimi oasis and Abu Dhabi interior
w4-900189.blurb: CORRECTED: The junior researcher anchored this on the 1853 Perpetual Maritime Truce, a Britain-Trucial maritime agreement that did not transfer territory to Nejd. The actual event matching the transfer Trucial States -> Emirate of Nejd (py1849/y1853) at lng54.1/lat24.4 (Abu Dhabi interior) is the renewed Second Saudi State (Emirate of Nejd) expansion into the Buraimi oasis under Emir Faisal bin Turki: Saudi-Wahhabi forces pressed the interior 1845-1850, and in 1853 Abdullah ibn Faisal occupied Buraimi (extracting tribute from Muscat), beginning a hold that lasted until 1869. This Wahhabi push into the Abu Dhabi hinterland matches the dataset window and location.

citations.label: Faisal bin Turki Al Saud (1785–1865) – Wikipedia

w4-900192.name: Taiping Rebellion (Heavenly Kingdom Expansion)
w4-900192.blurb: The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom under Hong Xiuquan rose in Guangxi in 1850 and expanded north, capturing Nanjing (renamed Tianjing) in March 1853 and controlling a large swath of central China along the Yangtze (~224,570 km2). The coordinates (115.1E, 31.3N) lie in Hubei/Anhui, the heart of Taiping expansion by 1853. Transfer Qing Dynasty -> Taiping Heavenly Kingdom fits the 1849-1853 window.

w4-900194.name: British protectorate consolidation on Mosquito Coast
w4-900194.blurb: Britain seized San Juan del Norte (Greytown) for the Mosquito Kingdom in January 1848, compelling Nicaragua to sign a peace treaty ceding the town. In the ensuing years (1849–1853), intensified by the California Gold Rush transit traffic, Britain strengthened the Mosquito protectorate against Nicaraguan sovereignty claims. The Clayton-Bulwer Treaty (1850) between Britain and the United States froze the status quo, effectively leaving the Mosquito Kingdom in control of Nicaragua's Caribbean coast.

w4-900195.name: Treaty of Managua (1860) — British withdrawal from the Mosquito Coast
w4-900195.blurb: The Treaty of Managua, signed on 28 January 1860 between Britain and Nicaragua, formally ended the British protectorate over the Mosquito (Miskito) Kingdom on the Caribbean coast of Central America. Britain ceded sovereignty over the Mosquito Coast to Nicaragua, implementing the Clayton-Bulwer Treaty (1850). Note: the dataset records this as British Colonial Empire to Mosquito Kingdom; the treaty actually restored the Mosquito reserve under nominal autonomy while transferring sovereignty to Nicaragua.

w4-900198.type: military suppression / restoration of imperial control
w4-900198.name: Austrian and Russian suppression of the Hungarian Revolution of 1848-1849
w4-900198.blurb: Hungary declared independence from Habsburg rule on 14 April 1849, but combined Austro-Russian forces (Russia sending a ~200,000-strong army) defeated the Hungarian army; General Gorgey surrendered at Vilagos on 13 August 1849. Austrian absolutism over Hungary followed until the Ausgleich of 1867. The from->to (Hungarian Nationalists -> Austrian Empire) at 21.3, 47 (eastern Hungary) and the 1849-1853 window match this reconquest.

w4-900199.name: Prussian suppression of the Baden Revolution and restoration of the Grand Duchy
w4-900199.blurb: The Baden Revolution of 1848-1849 briefly established a republic under Lorenz Brentano after Grand Duke Leopold fled in May 1849. Prussian forces under Prince Wilhelm invaded Baden in June 1849, defeating the revolutionary army at Waghäusel on 20 June and entering Karlsruhe on 25 June. The Grand Duchy of Baden was restored. The data window 1849-1853 reflects the restoration and consolidation.

w4-900200.name: Proclamation of the Second French Empire under Napoleon III
w4-900200.blurb: Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte seized power in a coup d'etat on 2 December 1851, dissolving the Legislative Assembly of the French Second Republic. On 2 December 1852 he proclaimed himself Emperor Napoleon III, converting the Second Republic into the Second French Empire. French colonial and claimed territories passed from Second Republic to Second Empire administration at this moment. The date 1852 falls within the [1849,1853] window.

w4-900202.name: Austrian occupation of the Danubian Principalities (Crimean War)
w4-900202.blurb: During the Crimean War (1853-1856), Russia occupied the Ottoman Danubian Principalities (Moldavia and Wallachia) in July 1853 as a pretext for war. Austria, though neutral, pressured Russia to withdraw and in August 1854 occupied the principalities itself to prevent Russian expansion toward the Balkans. The Treaty of Paris (1856) stripped Russia of its protectorate and placed the principalities under joint European guarantee, effectively transferring suzerainty from Russia's orbit to Austrian and Ottoman management.

w4-900203.name: Collapse of William Walker's Republic of Baja California
w4-900203.blurb: American filibuster William Walker captured La Paz in November 1853 and declared an independent 'Republic of Lower California,' but Mexican resistance and logistical failure forced his retreat; by May 1854 he surrendered to US authorities and Mexico reasserted control. The coordinates (~113W 28N, southern Baja) match the area Walker claimed. The 1853-1856 window captures the reversion of the territory to Mexico.

w4-900204.name: Division of the Omani Empire after death of Said bin Sultan (1856)
w4-900204.blurb: After Sayyid Said bin Sultan died in October 1856, the Omani Empire was split between his sons (African Zanzibar under Majid; Asian Muscat and Oman under Thuwaini), fragmenting Omani authority in the western Indian Ocean. The Majeerteen Sultanate in NE Somalia asserted greater independence as Omani coastal control weakened in the mid-1850s.

w4-900207.name: Partition of the Omani Empire - Creation of Sultanate of Zanzibar
w4-900207.blurb: Sultan Said bin Sultan of Oman died on 19 October 1856 and his maritime empire was partitioned: the East African domains including Zanzibar and the Swahili coast went to his son Majid bin Said as the Sultanate of Zanzibar, while Oman went to Thuwaini bin Said. British arbitration (the Canning Award, 1861) formalised the split. The coordinates point to the Tanzanian coast, where territory formerly labelled 'Omani Slave Coast' became the Sultanate of Zanzibar's core domain. The death (1856) falls at the end of the 1853-1856 window.

w4-900208.name: William Walker's filibuster control of Nicaragua (mislabelled Republic of Baja California)
w4-900208.blurb: The worklist records 'Republic of Nicaragua → Republic of Baja California' at -85.4E, 13N (Nicaragua), py=1853 y=1856. The Baja California name belongs to Walker's earlier 1853–54 expedition; the location and window correspond to Walker's seizure of Nicaragua (he controlled the country 1856–57, becoming president July 1856). The underlying territorial-control event — Walker's filibuster regime in Nicaragua — is real and falls in the window, though the dataset mislabels it with his Baja California republic name.

w4-900209.name: William Walker's seizure of Nicaragua
w4-900209.blurb: William Walker, whose earlier filibuster created the 'Republic of Baja California' label, arrived in Nicaragua in 1855 with 57 men, won the Battle of Rivas, and seized Granada; he was inaugurated president on 12 July 1856 after a fraudulent election — the Cliopatria geometry reflects Walker's Nicaragua polity inheriting the 'Republic of Baja California' label before a relabeling.

w4-900211.name: Second Saudi State's withdrawal from the Trucial Coast hinterland (c. 1853-1856)
w4-900211.blurb: Amid internal Saudi succession struggles in the 1850s and following the 1853 British Perpetual Maritime Truce, Saudi authority over the Trucial Coast hinterland weakened, allowing coastal confederations to reassert control. The worklist transition is 'Emirate of Nejd' -> 'Trucial States' [1853,1856] at lng 54, lat 24.4 (UAE interior), with the withdrawal inside the window. This is the reciprocal of 900189; the paired oscillation reflects the contested zone, but the underlying receding-Saudi-influence dynamic is attested.

w4-900212.name: Panthay Rebellion: Muslim uprising in Yunnan
w4-900212.blurb: The Panthay Rebellion (1856–1873) was an uprising of Hui Muslims against Qing rule in Yunnan. In 1856 Du Wenxiu (Sultan Sulayman) seized Dali and established an independent Muslim sultanate in western Yunnan, controlling large areas for nearly two decades. Matches the Qing → Panthay Rebellion transfer in the 1853-1856 window.

w4-900215.name: Defeat of William Walker and restoration of Nicaraguan sovereignty
w4-900215.blurb: By May 1857 the Central American allied coalition had crushed William Walker's filibuster regime in Nicaragua; Walker capitulated to the U.S. Navy on 1 May 1857 and was repatriated. The territory captured under his short-lived government reverted to the restored Republic of Nicaragua, ending the foreign occupation and re-establishing legitimate Nicaraguan authority over the country.

w4-900216.name: Dutch deposition of Sultan Mahmud IV and tightening control over Riau-Lingga
w4-900216.blurb: On 7 October 1857 Sultan Mahmud Muzaffar Shah (IV) of the Riau-Lingga Sultanate was deposed by the Dutch East Indies colonial government after he sailed to Singapore without naming a viceroy, defying a Dutch travel prohibition. The Dutch installed his uncle Sultan Badrul Alam Syah II in his place and formalised further restrictions through the contract of 1 December 1857. This marked a decisive tightening of Dutch control over Riau-Lingga's administrative core (full Dutch takeover followed in 1911).

w4-900217.name: Treaty of Paris (1856) - cession of southern Bessarabia to Moldavia
w4-900217.blurb: The Treaty of Paris, signed 30 March 1856 to end the Crimean War, required Russia to cede the southern districts of Bessarabia (near the Danube delta) to the Danubian Principality of Moldavia, depriving Russia of direct access to the Danube. Austria, which had occupied Moldavia and Wallachia during the war, was obliged to withdraw. The territory around lat 46.8, lng 26.6 accordingly passed from Austrian to Moldavian administration in 1856-1857.

w4-900218.name: Treaty of Paris (1856) — Austria evacuates Danubian Principalities
w4-900218.blurb: The Treaty of Paris of 30 March 1856, which ended the Crimean War, restored the autonomy and traditional administration of the Danubian Principality of Moldavia under nominal Ottoman suzerainty and the collective guarantee of the Great Powers, ending wartime Russian and subsequent Austrian occupation. Russian forces withdrew from Moldavian soil (centred near lng 26.6, lat 46.8), and Moldavia was placed under an internationally guaranteed regime that paved the way for the 1859 union with Wallachia.

w4-900219.name: End of the Austrian occupation of Wallachia
w4-900219.blurb: Under the Treaty of Paris of 30 March 1856 ending the Crimean War, Russia ceded southern Bessarabia (the districts later organised as Cahul, Bolgrad and Ismail) to the Principality of Moldavia, restoring to it Danube-mouth territory annexed by Russia in 1812. The cession removed Russia from direct access to the lower Danube and added roughly 9,000–10,000 km² to Moldavia, which carried the districts into the United Principalities (Romania) after 1859.

w4-900220.name: Anglo-Persian War and Treaty of Paris (1857)
w4-900220.blurb: The Anglo-Persian War (1856–1857) was triggered by the Qajar dynasty's capture of Herat in October 1856. British forces defeated Persia, and the Treaty of Paris (4 March 1857) required Persia to withdraw from Herat and renounce all claims over Herat and Afghanistan, ceding contested western Afghan territory from Qajar influence to the Emirate of Afghanistan.

w4-900222.name: Panthay Rebellion — Muslim insurgency seizes Yunnan territory
w4-900222.blurb: The Panthay Rebellion (1856–1873) was a Hui Muslim uprising in Yunnan triggered by the 1856 Kunming Massacre; rebels under Du Wenxiu captured Dali and held large parts of Yunnan, including the Yunnan/Sichuan border zone (103.5,28.9). The Qing lost effective control of rebel-held areas, matching the from→to (Qing Dynasty → Panthay Rebellion) in the 1857–1859 window.

w4-900223.to: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia
w4-900223.name: Double election of Alexandru Ioan Cuza and unification of Moldavia and Wallachia
w4-900223.blurb: Alexandru Ioan Cuza was elected prince of Moldavia on 5 January 1859 and then of Wallachia on 24 January 1859, creating a personal union of the two principalities as the United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia. This was a nationalist fait accompli that the Great Powers ultimately accepted. Moldavian territory (lat 46.5, lng 27.7) formally joined the new united state, the predecessor of modern Romania, which achieved full administrative union and adopted the name Romania in 1862.

citations.label: Unification of Moldavia and Wallachia – Wikipedia

w4-900224.to: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia
w4-900224.name: Election of Alexandru Ioan Cuza — Union of Moldavia and Wallachia (1859)
w4-900224.blurb: Alexandru Ioan Cuza was elected prince of Moldavia on 5 January 1859, then of Wallachia on 24 January 1859, creating a personal union of both principalities. This unified entity became the United Principalities (later Romania), absorbing Moldavia's territory (centred around lng 27.7, lat 46.5) under a single administration, recognised by the Great Powers in 1861.

citations.label: Wikipedia: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia

w4-900225.name: Government of India Act 1858 — dissolution of East India Company, creation of British Raj
w4-900225.blurb: The Indian Rebellion of 1857 (Sepoy Mutiny), which lasted until 1859, exposed the inadequacy of East India Company rule and prompted Parliament to pass the Government of India Act on 2 August 1858. The Act transferred all powers, territories, and assets of the Company to the British Crown, abolished the Board of Control, and created the office of Secretary of State for India. The Governor-General was redesignated Viceroy, and India became a direct Crown possession — the British Raj — a status it retained until independence in 1947.

w4-900226.name: Colombian Constitution of 1858 — Republic of New Granada becomes Granadine Confederation
w4-900226.blurb: On 22 May 1858 the Colombian Congress adopted a new federal constitution that dissolved the centralist Republic of New Granada and replaced it with the Granadine Confederation of eight sovereign states. This was Colombia's first federal constitution. The dataset window of 1857–1859 brackets the transition.

w4-900227.name: Second Italian War of Independence — cession of Lombardy to Sardinia (1859)
w4-900227.blurb: France and Sardinia went to war with Austria in April 1859. After Franco-Sardinian victories at Magenta (4 June) and Solferino (24 June), Napoleon III and Franz Joseph I agreed the Armistice of Villafranca (July 1859). Austria ceded Lombardy (excluding Mantua and Peschiera) to France, which transferred it to Sardinia via the Treaty of Zürich (November 1859), advancing Italian unification.

citations.label: Second Italian War of Independence — Wikipedia

w4-900228.name: French Cochinchina Campaign – Capture of Saigon
w4-900228.blurb: In September 1858, a Franco-Spanish naval expedition under Admiral Rigault de Genouilly attacked Da Nang, then moved south and captured Saigon on 17 February 1859. This Cochinchina Campaign was the opening act of France's conquest of Vietnam. The Treaty of Saigon (1862) formalised French possession of three southern provinces of the Nguyễn empire, and the territory around Saigon passed to French control during 1858–1859. (The worklist's 'to' label 'New Caledonia' is a Cliopatria stand-in for French colonial possession; the underlying event is the French seizure of Saigon.)

w4-900229.name: Banjarmasin War (Banjar War) and Abolition of the Sultanate of Banjar
w4-900229.blurb: The Banjarmasin War (1859–1863) was triggered by a disputed succession following the death of Sultan Adam in 1857 and Dutch interference in installing Tamjidillah II. Anti-colonial resistance coalesced under Prince Antasari and was framed as a religious war. The Dutch declared the Sultanate abolished in 1860, placing southern Borneo under direct colonial rule from Batavia. The dataset records 'Sultanate of Banjar → Dutch East Indies' for 1859–1860, consistent with the formal abolition.

w4-900233.name: Wyke-Cruz Treaty (1859) — Mosquito Coast cession to Honduras
w4-900233.blurb: By the Wyke–Cruz (Anglo-Honduran) Treaty of 28 November 1859, Britain agreed to relinquish the Bay Islands—Roatán, Guanaja, Utila, Barbareta, Helene and Morat—which it had constituted a Crown Colony in 1852, recognising them as Honduran territory. The transfer took full effect in 1861, ending direct British rule over the islands; it was a separate settlement from the Mosquito Coast question, the bulk of which passed to Nicaragua under the 1860 Treaty of Managua.

w4-900234.name: Taiping Heavenly Kingdom Expansion into Jiangsu and Zhejiang (1860)
w4-900234.blurb: In May 1860, the Taiping forces broke the Qing siege of their capital Nanjing and launched an offensive into the wealthy Yangtze delta. They captured Hangzhou and Suzhou later in 1860, briefly controlling much of southern Jiangsu and Zhejiang. Their attempt to take Shanghai in August 1860 was repelled by Western-led forces, marking the peak of Taiping expansion.

w4-900236.name: Treaty of Turin (1860): cession of Savoy and Nice to France
w4-900236.blurb: Under the Treaty of Turin (24 March 1860) the Kingdom of Sardinia ceded the Duchy of Savoy and County of Nice to Napoleon III's Second French Empire in exchange for French support of Italian unification, confirmed by April 1860 plebiscites and promulgated 14 June 1860. Coord 6.6E/45N is in the Savoy Alps, matching the ceded territory.

w4-900241.name: Battle of Pavon and reunification of Buenos Aires with Argentina (1861)
w4-900241.blurb: The State of Buenos Aires, which had seceded from the Argentine Confederation in 1852, rejoined a unified Argentina following the Battle of Pavon on 17 September 1861. The from->to (State of Buenos Aires -> Argentine Confederation) at -60.3, -37.3 in the 1860-1861 window matches this reunification, which led to a unified Argentine Republic under Mitre in 1862.

w4-900243.name: Spanish annexation of the Dominican Republic (1861)
w4-900243.blurb: On 18 March 1861, Dominican president Pedro Santana obtained the annexation of the Dominican Republic into the Spanish Empire, motivated by fears of Haitian invasion. Spain made Santo Domingo a province under Santana as governor-general, triggering the Dominican Restoration War (1863–1865). The worklist transfer Dominican Republic → Spanish Empire at lng -70.3, lat 18.8 in the 1860–1861 window matches this annexation.

citations.label: Annexation of the Dominican Republic to Spain – Wikipedia

w4-900244.name: Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand and Proclamation of the Kingdom of Italy
w4-900244.blurb: In May–October 1860, Giuseppe Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand conquered the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, and plebiscites (October 1860) voted overwhelmingly for annexation to the Kingdom of Sardinia. After the Siege of Gaeta (February 1861), the last Bourbon resistance ended. The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed on 17 March 1861, formally merging the Two Sicilies into the Savoyard/Sardinian monarchy.

citations.label: Kingdom of the Two Sicilies – Wikipedia

w4-900245.name: Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand and unification of Italy (1860–1861)
w4-900245.blurb: The Papal-States territory that passed to the Kingdom of Sardinia in 1860 was the Marche and Umbria, invaded by 35,000 Piedmontese troops in September 1860 and won at the Battle of Castelfidardo (18 September 1860). After plebiscites, these provinces were annexed to Sardinia, reducing papal rule to Lazio and Rome; the gains were folded into the Kingdom of Italy proclaimed on 17 March 1861.

w4-900246.name: Siege of Anqing — Qing reconquest of Taiping territory
w4-900246.blurb: The Battle of Anqing (September 1860 – 5 September 1861) was a prolonged siege of the key Taiping Heavenly Kingdom stronghold on the Yangtze River in Anhui province, conducted by the Hunan Army under Zeng Guoquan. Anqing had been the westernmost Taiping bastion defending Nanjing; its fall on 5 September 1861 opened the Yangtze route to the Taiping capital and marked the turning of the tide in the Taiping Rebellion, leading to the eventual recapture of Nanjing in 1864.

w4-900247.name: Qing recovery of northern Anhui during Taiping Eastern Offensive, 1861
w4-900247.blurb: During the Taiping eastern offensive of 1860–1861, rebel armies broke the Qing siege of Nanjing and drove into the lower Yangzi, seizing wealthy prefectures of Jiangsu and Zhejiang—including Suzhou (June 1860) and, after this period, Hangzhou—wresting large territories from Qing control. The campaign extended the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom's reach toward Shanghai and marked the rebellion's greatest territorial extent before the Qing counteroffensive of 1862–1864.

w4-900249.name: Qing recapture of Anqing and containment of Taiping Rebellion
w4-900249.blurb: By 1861-1862 the Qing dynasty, aided by Zeng Guofan's Xiang Army and the foreign-officered Ever Victorious Army under Frederick Townsend Ward (later Charles Gordon), began systematically recapturing territory from the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. Zeng Guofan took the strategic city of Anqing in 1861, and by May 1862 his forces besieged Nanjing. The Ever Victorious Army repulsed Taiping assaults on Shanghai (January 1862) and recaptured towns in the Yangtze delta. The coordinates (117 degrees E, 30 degrees N) point to the Anhui/Jiangxi border — Anqing region — where the Qing counteroffensive gained critical momentum.

citations.label: Ever Victorious Army – Warfare History Network

w4-900251.name: Creation of the Stikine Territory by Britain during Stikine Gold Rush
w4-900251.blurb: On 19 July 1862, Britain detached the Stikine Territory from the Hudson's Bay Company's North-Western Territory in response to the Stikine River gold rush, appointing the Governor of British Columbia as Administrator. The new territory was bounded to the west by the Alaska panhandle of Russian America, formalizing British sovereignty over a region bordering Russian imperial territory. The territory was dissolved in 1863, most of it absorbed into British Columbia.

citations.label: Russian colonization of North America – Wikipedia

w4-900252.name: Dutch protectorate over the Sultanate of Siak, eastern Sumatra (c. 1858–1862)
w4-900252.blurb: The Dutch made the Sultanate of Siak a protectorate of the Dutch East Indies on 1 February 1858, with a follow-on treaty c. 1862 confirming Dutch sovereignty over Siak and adjacent eastern Sumatran territories. The coordinates are the Siak River region. The recorded transferor 'Sultanate of Malacca' is an atlas label for the Malay/Johor-Malaccan sultanate tradition to which Siak belonged; the underlying Dutch annexation of this Malay sultanate is well attested.

citations.label: Sultanate of Siak Sri Indrapura – Wikipedia

w4-900253.name: Kingdom of Sardinia proclaimed Kingdom of Italy (1861)
w4-900253.blurb: On 17 March 1861 the Parliament of the Kingdom of Sardinia proclaimed Victor Emmanuel II King of Italy, creating the Kingdom of Italy through the Risorgimento. The from->to (Kingdom of Sardinia -> Kingdom of Italy) at 12.6, 41.6 (central Italy) in the 1861-1862 window matches this unification; Rome and Venetia were incorporated later (1870, 1866).

w4-900254.name: Battle of Pavón and unification of Argentina under Buenos Aires
w4-900254.blurb: On 17 September 1861, Buenos Aires forces under Bartolomé Mitre defeated the Argentine Confederation's army at the Battle of Pavón, causing Confederation president Derqui to resign and the national government to dissolve. Mitre became provisional president of a unified Argentine Republic (Cliopatria centroid lat -31.5, lng -62.3), formalized by 1862,

w4-900255.name: Second French intervention in Mexico; occupation of Mexico City (1863)
w4-900255.blurb: After being repulsed at Puebla in 1862, reinforced French forces captured Puebla in May 1863 and entered Mexico City on 10 June 1863, establishing a pro-French government. The window (1862-1863) and coordinates (-97.6, 19.4, the Puebla-Mexico City corridor) match the French occupation.

citations.label: Second French intervention in Mexico - Wikipedia

w4-900257.name: Rionegro Constitution of 1863 — Granadine Confederation becomes United States of Colombia
w4-900257.blurb: After the Colombian Civil War of 1860–1862, in which Liberal general Tomás Cipriano de Mosquera defeated the conservative government, a convention at Rionegro signed a radically federalist constitution on 8 May 1863 that renamed the country the United States of Colombia, granting the nine sovereign states near-complete autonomy. The dataset window of 1862–1863 matches.

w4-900258.name: Fall of Nanjing and collapse of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom (1864)
w4-900258.blurb: The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom held its capital Tianjing (Nanjing) from 1853. By early 1864 Qing forces under Zeng Guofan, aided by the Ever Victorious Army, had besieged the city. Hong Xiuquan died on 1 June 1864; Qing forces stormed Nanjing in July 1864, ending the Taiping state and returning the territory around Nanjing to Qing control.

w4-900260.name: Second French intervention in Mexico — establishment of Second Mexican Empire (1863–1864)
w4-900260.blurb: Napoleon III intervened militarily in Mexico from 1862. After capturing Mexico City in June 1863, French forces established a regency and offered the crown to Archduke Maximilian of Austria, who accepted at the Treaty of Miramar (April 1864) and arrived in Mexico in May 1864. This transferred control of much of Mexico to the Mexican Monarchist Empire.

citations.label: Second French intervention in Mexico – Wikipedia

w4-900261.name: French handover of occupied territory to Mexican Monarchist junta
w4-900261.blurb: After French forces under General Forey occupied Mexico City in June 1863, Napoleon III directed that administration pass to a conservative Mexican Regency (Monarchist junta) pending Maximilian's arrival; French military advances in late 1863 – early 1864 systematically transferred control of newly seized regions to the Monarchist government.

citations.label: Wikipedia: Second French intervention in Mexico

w4-900268.name: Fall of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom
w4-900268.blurb: The Taiping Rebellion (1850-1864), one of the deadliest conflicts in history, was suppressed by Qing imperial forces under Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang. The Taiping capital of Nanjing fell on 19 July 1864 when Zeng's Xiang Army breached the walls; Hong Xiuquan had already died in June. The remaining Taiping forces were mopped up through 1865, restoring Qing control over the Yangtze valley and Jiangnan region (coordinates ~119.6E, 29.8N = Zhejiang/lower Yangtze).

w4-900270.name: Second Mexican Empire - Imperial Consolidation (1864-65)
w4-900270.blurb: French forces under Marshal Bazaine captured Mexico City in 1863; Maximilian I landed at Veracruz in May 1864 and 1864-65 marked the peak of imperial territorial control, holding the central states, major cities, and about two-thirds of the population. The dataset records the change from 'Mexican Monarchists' to 'Second Mexican Empire' between 1864 and 1865, reflecting the formal establishment of the empire. Coordinates (lat 20.5) lie in central Mexico.

citations.label: Second French intervention in Mexico - Wikipedia

w4-900271.name: Consolidation of the Second Mexican Empire under Maximilian
w4-900271.blurb: With Maximilian von Habsburg's arrival and assumption of the throne in mid-1864, territory taken from the Mexican Republic by French and conservative forces was consolidated under the Second Mexican Empire's administration. The provisional conservative regency gave way to an institutionalised imperial government, extending nominal imperial authority over the regions then under French military occupation, though republican resistance under Benito Juárez persisted in the north.

w4-900272.name: Dominican Restoration War ends Spanish rule (1863–1865)
w4-900272.blurb: The Dominican Restoration War (16 August 1863 – 15 March 1865) was a successful guerrilla campaign against Spanish colonial forces following the 1861 annexation. Unable to contain the insurgency, Spain repealed the annexation on 3 March 1865 and evacuated, restoring the Dominican Republic. The worklist transfer Spanish Empire → Dominican Republic at lng -70.3, lat 18.8 in the 1864–1865 window captures the final phase of Spanish withdrawal.

citations.label: Annexation of the Dominican Republic to Spain – Wikipedia

w4-900273.name: War of the Triple Alliance – Allied Invasion of Paraguay
w4-900273.blurb: The War of the Triple Alliance (1864–1870) pitted Paraguay against Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay. After Paraguayan forces invaded Brazilian and Argentine territory in 1864–1865, the Triple Alliance drove Paraguay back. On 16 April 1866, an Allied army crossed the Paraná River into Paraguay proper, and the Battle of Tuiutí (20 May 1866) was the largest land battle in South American history. Brazilian forces occupied extensive Paraguayan border territory during 1865–1866.

citations.label: War of the Triple Alliance – Britannica

w4-900275.name: Ottoman firman of 1866: succession reform and near-Khedival status for Egypt
w4-900275.blurb: In 1866, Ottoman Sultan Abdülaziz granted Ismail Pasha a firman transforming Egypt's succession from agnatic seniority to male-line primogeniture, cementing Ismail's dynastic position. A follow-up firman in June 1867 formally recognized Ismail with the title 'Khedive,' elevating Egypt to near-sovereign status within the empire. Cliopatria records this administrative transition (Muhammad Ali dynasty to Khedivate of Egypt at lat 21.3, lng 32.6) in the 1865-1866 window.

citations.label: History of Egypt under the Muhammad Ali dynasty – Wikipedia

w4-900276.name: Colombian Constitution of 1886 — United States of Colombia becomes Republic of Colombia
w4-900276.blurb: Under President Rafael Núñez's 'Regeneration' programme, a new centralist constitution adopted on 5 August 1886 abolished the federalist United States of Colombia and established the unitary Republic of Colombia, converting the sovereign states into centrally governed departments. The transition (US of Colombia → Republic of Colombia) is genuine and the parties are correct, but the dataset window of 1865–1866 is a data error: the actual date is 1886.

w4-900277.name: End of the American Civil War — Confederate States surrender (1865)
w4-900277.blurb: Robert E. Lee surrendered to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House on 9 April 1865, effectively ending the American Civil War; remaining Confederate armies surrendered within weeks and the Confederate government collapsed. The former Confederate states were reunited under the United States and placed under Reconstruction. The dataset records the CSA → USA transfer in the 1865–1866 window.

w4-900278.name: Austro-Hungarian Compromise (Ausgleich) of 1867
w4-900278.blurb: The Ausgleich of 8 February 1867 transformed the Austrian Empire into the Dual Monarchy of Austria-Hungary, granting Hungary full internal autonomy under its own parliament and prime minister while maintaining a common monarch (Franz Joseph I) and shared ministries for foreign affairs, defence, and common finances. The compromise was driven by Hungary's nationalist pressure and Austria's military defeats (1859, 1866). The date 1867 falls within the [1866,1868] window.

w4-900279.name: Brunei Cessions to Sarawak under James and Charles Brooke
w4-900279.blurb: James Brooke, first White Rajah of Sarawak, died in 1868 and was succeeded by his nephew Charles Brooke, who continued to press the weakening Sultanate of Brunei for territorial cessions throughout his reign (1868-1917). The coordinates correspond to the interior of Borneo where Sarawak progressively absorbed Brunei's hinterland. The 1866-1868 window marks the James-to-Charles transition and ongoing Sarawak territorial consolidation at Brunei's expense.

w4-900280.name: Franco-Siamese Treaty of Bangkok and consolidation of French protectorate over Cambodia
w4-900280.blurb: The Franco-Siamese Treaty of Bangkok (1867) confirmed France's protectorate over Cambodia (initially established in 1863) while Siam renounced suzerainty in exchange for formal recognition of Siamese control over Battambang and Siem Reap. France subsequently integrated Cambodia more firmly into its Indochina administration, and King Norodom was crowned in 1868 with French backing. The coordinates (105 degrees E, 12 degrees N) point to central Cambodia. This transferred effective authority over the Khmer heartland from traditional Siamese-Khmer dual suzerainty to the French colonial sphere.

citations.label: Franco-Siamese Treaty of Bangkok (1867) – Wonders of Cambodia

w4-900281.name: Qing reconquest of Yunnan from Panthay rebels
w4-900281.blurb: Qing imperial forces systematically reconquered rebel-held Yunnan districts from the mid-1860s, culminating in the recapture of Dali in January 1873 and Du Wenxiu's death. The window py=1866/y=1868 at (103.5,28.9) marks an earlier reconquest phase, matching the from→to (Panthay Rebellion → Qing Dynasty).

w4-900284.name: Meiji Restoration – Overthrow of the Tokugawa Shogunate
w4-900284.blurb: On 9 November 1867, the last Tokugawa shogun Yoshinobu formally returned political authority to Emperor Meiji (taisei hōkan). On 3 January 1868, a coup by Satsuma and Chōshū seized the Imperial Palace and issued the edict of imperial restoration (ōsei fukko). The Boshin War (1868–1869) eliminated the remaining shogunal forces, and the domains were replaced by a prefecture system in 1871, transferring Tokugawa-administered territory to the imperial government.

w4-900286.name: Fall of the Second Mexican Empire and execution of Maximilian I
w4-900286.blurb: After France withdrew its troops in 1866, the Second Mexican Empire quickly collapsed. Emperor Maximilian I was captured at Querétaro in May 1867 and executed by firing squad on 19 June 1867. The restored Mexican Republic under Benito Juárez then reasserted control over all national territory (Cliopatria centroid lat 23.7, lng -101.9), ending the foreign-backed imperial experiment and reunifying the country under republican governance in the 1866-1868 window.

w4-900294.name: Meiji Restoration: abolition of the Tokugawa Shogunate
w4-900294.blurb: On 3 January 1868 pro-imperial forces proclaimed the restoration of imperial rule; the last shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu had resigned in November 1867. The Boshin War (1868–1869) crushed Tokugawa loyalists, and the han system was abolished in 1871, consolidating territory under the Meiji Emperor. Matches the Tokugawa Shogunate → Empire of Japan transfer in the 1868-1870 window.

w4-900295.name: Franco-Prussian War and Proclamation of the French Third Republic
w4-900295.blurb: Napoleon III declared war on Prussia on 15 July 1870; the French were swiftly defeated and Napoleon III was captured at the Battle of Sedan on 1 September 1870. On 4 September 1870 republican deputies in Paris proclaimed the French Third Republic, and a Government of National Defence was formed. The Treaty of Frankfurt (May 1871) ceded Alsace-Lorraine to Germany. French colonial territories passed from Second Empire to Third Republic administration.

w4-900296.name: Capture of Rome (Breach of Porta Pia) — end of Papal temporal power
w4-900296.blurb: On 20 September 1870 the Royal Italian Army under General Raffaele Cadorna breached the Aurelian Walls at Porta Pia and took Rome, ending more than a millennium of papal temporal rule once the protecting French garrison withdrew during the Franco-Prussian War. A plebiscite on 2 October 1870 ratified annexation to the Kingdom of Italy, extinguishing the Papal States; Rome became Italy's capital in 1871.

w4-900299.name: Franco-Prussian War - annexation of Alsace-Lorraine by the German Empire (1871)
w4-900299.blurb: The Franco-Prussian War (19 July 1870-28 January 1871) ended with the Treaty of Frankfurt (10 May 1871), under which France ceded Alsace (excluding Belfort) and much of Lorraine to the newly proclaimed German Empire. The territory-designated the Reichsland Elsass-Lothringen-encompassed key industrial assets and strategic fortresses. The data entry (Second French Empire to German Empire, py=1870, y=1871) corresponds to this annexation, which fundamentally altered the balance of power in western Europe for half a century.

w4-900301.name: Foundation of the German Empire / Unification of Germany
w4-900301.blurb: Wurttemberg joined the war against France in July 1870 and signed a treaty of alliance with Prussia on 25 November 1870. The German Empire was proclaimed at Versailles on 18 January 1871, with the Kingdom of Wurttemberg absorbed as a constituent state. Wurttemberg retained special privileges (its own postal service, railways, and army administration), but its territory and sovereignty were subsumed under the Empire.

w4-900302.name: Unification of Germany / Proclamation of the German Empire
w4-900302.blurb: The Grand Duchy of Mecklenburg-Schwerin, which had sided with Prussia in 1866 and joined the North German Confederation in 1867, became a constituent federated state of the German Empire proclaimed at Versailles on 18 January 1871. Grand Duke Frederick Francis II had contributed troops and high command to the Franco-Prussian War; the duchy retained internal autonomy as a member state until the monarchy's fall in 1918.

w4-900305.name: Ottoman incorporation of Kuwait into Basra Vilayet (1871)
w4-900305.blurb: In 1871 the Ottoman governor of Iraq, Midhat Pasha, reasserted Ottoman suzerainty over Kuwait, incorporating it into the Basra Vilayet (formalised by 1875); the Al-Sabah ruler accepted the title of Ottoman qaimaqam under pressure, placing Kuwait nominally within the Ottoman administrative sphere.

w4-900309.name: French repayment of Frankfurt indemnity and German evacuation of occupied France
w4-900309.blurb: The Treaty of Frankfurt (10 May 1871) ending the Franco-Prussian War required France to pay a 5-billion-franc indemnity and tolerate German occupation of northern France until payment was complete. Under Finance Minister Léon Say, France mobilised patriotic loans and discharged the entire sum by September 1873, nearly two years ahead of schedule. The last German occupation forces evacuated French territory in mid-September 1873, restoring full French sovereignty over the occupied zones.

w4-900310.name: Qing suppression of the Panthay Rebellion
w4-900310.blurb: Qing imperial forces recaptured Dali in January 1873, ending the Panthay Rebellion. Du Wenxiu was captured and executed, and massacres of Yunnan's Hui population followed. The rebellion's collapse restored Qing authority over all of Yunnan. Matches the Panthay Rebellion → Qing transfer in the 1871-1873 window.

w4-900311.name: Post-War of Triple Alliance territorial settlement – Hayes arbitration returns territory to Paraguay (1878)
w4-900311.blurb: The War of the Triple Alliance (1864–70) left Paraguay devastated and occupied by Brazilian and Argentine forces until 1876. A dispute between Brazil and Argentina over the Chaco was arbitrated in 1878 by U.S. President Rutherford B. Hayes, who awarded the contested northern Chaco territory to Paraguay rather than Argentina. The dataset window (1873–1877) captures the period of continued Brazilian occupation and the peace-treaty negotiations that ultimately restored much of this territory to Paraguay.

citations.label: War of the Triple Alliance – Britannica
Treaty of the Triple Alliance – Wikipedia

w4-900312.name: Pangkor Treaty and British Residency in Perak
w4-900312.blurb: The Pangkor Treaty of 20 January 1874 was signed between Governor Andrew Clarke and Sultan Abdullah of Perak, installing a British Resident whose advice had to be followed on all matters except Malay religion and custom. The assassination of the first Resident J.W.W. Birch in 1875 prompted a British punitive campaign; by 1877 British authority was firmly established. This is the transfer of effective sovereignty from the Sultanate of Perak to British Colonial control.

w4-900313.name: Pangkor Treaty 1874 — British Residency in Perak
w4-900313.blurb: On 10 October 1874 the Vunivalu Ratu Seru Epenisa Cakobau and other leading chiefs signed the Deed of Cession before Sir Hercules Robinson, transferring sovereignty over the Fijian islands to Queen Victoria. The act established the Crown Colony of Fiji under British administration, bringing the formerly independent Fijian kingdom into the British Empire.

w4-900314.name: Deed of Cession of Fiji
w4-900314.blurb: Exploiting the Selangor Civil War, the British extended the Pangkor residency model to Selangor in 1874, with James Guthrie Davidson installed as the first British Resident in October 1874 (Frank Swettenham serving as assistant). The sultan was thereafter expected to follow the Resident's advice on all matters save Malay religion and custom, drawing the tin-rich state into Britain's sphere of indirect rule.

w4-900315.name: Rashidi expansion: Emirate of Jabal Shammar captures territory from Emirate of Nejd
w4-900315.blurb: Under Emir Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Rashid (r. 1869–1897), the Rashidi Emirate of Jabal Shammar steadily expanded at the expense of the weakened Second Saudi State (Emirate of Nejd) through military pressure and tribal alliances during the 1870s, with significant shifts in the Najd region by the mid-1870s. This culminated in the Battle of Mulayda (1891). The worklist transfer Nejd → Jabal Shammar in central Arabia in the 1873–1877 window matches this consolidation.

w4-900319.name: Russian annexation of the Khanate of Kokand — Kokand Campaign (1875–1876)
w4-900319.blurb: Internal rebellion in the Khanate of Kokand in 1875 prompted Russian intervention under Kaufmann and Skobelev. After capturing Andizhan in January 1876 and crushing resistance at Uch-Kurgan, Tsar Alexander II annexed Kokand on 19 February 1876; the Fergana Valley was renamed Fergana Province of Russian Turkestan (Khanate of Kokand -> Russian Empire), matching the [1873,1877] window.

w4-900322.name: British Annexation of the Transvaal (South African Republic)
w4-900322.blurb: On April 12, 1877, Sir Theophilus Shepstone proclaimed the annexation of the South African Republic (Transvaal) in Church Square, Pretoria, on behalf of the British Crown. The annexation was ordered by Colonial Secretary Lord Carnarvon as part of his scheme to confederate South Africa, and was facilitated by the Transvaal's bankruptcy and its ongoing war with the Pedi kingdom under Sekhukhune. The Boers, led by Paul Kruger, initially protested politically before launching the First Anglo-Boer War (1880–1881) to regain independence. The dataset records the transition (South African Republic → British Cape Colony) over a 1873–1877 window, with the British Cape administration governing the annexed Transvaal until the Pretoria Convention of 1881.

citations.label: First Anglo-Boer War – South African History Online
Annexation of the Transvaal – The British Empire

w4-900325.name: Treaty of Berlin — Principality of Bulgaria established
w4-900325.blurb: The Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878) ended with the Treaty of San Stefano and the revising Congress of Berlin (June–July 1878), creating the autonomous Principality of Bulgaria from Ottoman territory; Russian forces administered it until the principality was organised (1879–1880). The coordinates (25.5,43.1) are Bulgaria, matching the from→to (Russian Empire → Principality of Bulgaria) in the 1877–1880 window.

w4-900326.from: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia
w4-900326.name: Treaty of Berlin (1878) — Russian annexation of Southern Bessarabia from Romania
w4-900326.blurb: Under the Treaty of Berlin of 13 July 1878, Romania (the United Principalities) was compelled to retrocede southern Bessarabia—the Cahul, Bolgrad and Ismail districts it had held since 1856—to the Russian Empire, receiving Northern Dobruja in compensation. The cession, resented in Bucharest as the betrayal of a wartime ally, restored Russia's foothold on the lower Danube.

w4-900332.to: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia
w4-900332.name: Treaty of Berlin (1878): Romania cedes southern Bessarabia to Russia
w4-900332.blurb: After fighting alongside Russia in the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–1878, Romania gained independence at the Treaty of Berlin (1878) but was compelled to cede southern Bessarabia (≈27–28°E, 45–46°N) to Russia in exchange for northern Dobruja. The transfer was formalised 1878–1880, matching the Russian Empire→United Principalities (Romania) entry's 1877–1880 window.

w4-900333.name: Treaty of Berlin (1878) - Serbia's full independence and territorial expansion
w4-900333.blurb: The Treaty of Berlin (13 July 1878), revising the Treaty of San Stefano after the Russo-Turkish War of 1877-78, formally recognised Serbia as a fully sovereign and independent state, ending nominal Ottoman suzerainty. Serbia also received new territories to the south including the districts of Nis, Pirot, Toplica, and Vranje. Prince Milan subsequently proclaimed Serbia a kingdom in 1882. The data entry (Serbs to Kingdom of Serbia, py=1877, y=1880) captures the transition from semi-autonomous principality to recognised sovereign state with expanded territory.

w4-900335.name: Third Anglo-Burmese War and British annexation of Upper Burma
w4-900335.blurb: The Third Anglo-Burmese War lasted about two weeks in November 1885. Britain launched the campaign after King Thibaw Min refused an ultimatum; General Prendergast's force advanced up the Irrawaddy, and Thibaw surrendered on 28 November 1885 and was exiled. Upper Burma was formally annexed on 1 January 1886, ending the Konbaung dynasty and incorporating the country into British India. The worklist transfer (Burma to British Raj, 1884-1885) matches.

citations.label: History of Myanmar – The British in Burma – Britannica

w4-900337.name: Convention of Constantinople (1881): Greece receives Thessaly
w4-900337.blurb: Following Article 24 of the 1878 Treaty of Berlin, the Convention of Constantinople (2 July 1881) had the Ottoman Empire cede most of Thessaly and the Arta district of Epirus to Greece; Greek troops crossed the old border on 6 July 1881. Coord 21.9E/39.5N is in Thessaly, matching the ceded territory and the 'Ottoman → Greece' direction. The dataset's py=1884/y=1885 window is off by ~3–4 years (a Cliopatria periodisation quirk); the true event date is 1881.

w4-900339.name: Siamese administrative integration of Chiang Mai (Lanna)
w4-900339.blurb: Following the Anglo-Siamese Treaty of Chiangmai (1883), King Chulalongkorn sent a royal commissioner to Chiang Mai in 1883–1885 to impose Siamese administration, eroding the autonomous Kingdom of Chiang Mai (Lanna) at (99.7,19.7). This Bangkok centralisation matches the from→to (Chiangmai → Rattanakosin Kingdom) in the 1884–1885 window.

w4-900340.name: Expansion of Jabal Shammar under Muhammad ibn Rashid at the expense of the Emirate of Nejd
w4-900340.blurb: Muhammad ibn Rashid (r. 1869–1897) of the Rashidi dynasty steadily expanded the Emirate of Jabal Shammar into Nejd at the expense of the Second Saudi State. By 1884 he had become the single dominant figure in Najd, pushing into the Qassim region (around lat 26.1, lng 44, the buffer between Medina and Riyadh). This expansion culminated in his annexation of Najd (1887) and the decisive Battle of Mulayda (1891) with the fall of Riyadh, but the mid-1880s ascendancy is the period captured here.

citations.label: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al Rashid – Wikipedia

w4-900342.name: Patenôtre Treaty (1884) — French protectorate over Annam and Tonkin
w4-900342.blurb: The Patenôtre Treaty (Treaty of Huế), signed 6 June 1884, established the French protectorate over Annam and Tonkin, transferring Nguyễn-dynasty sovereignty to French Indochina; China's rival claim to suzerainty was extinguished by the Treaty of Tientsin (9 June 1885) ending the Sino-French War. There is no historical basis for the previous claim that Siam held suzerainty over the Quảng Trị/Thừa Thiên area — that assertion should be dropped.

w4-900343.name: Treaty of Saint Petersburg (1881) — Ili / Central Asian Border Implementation
w4-900343.blurb: The Treaty of Saint Petersburg (24 February 1881), also called the Treaty of Ili, resolved the Ili Crisis between Russia and Qing China. Russia returned most of the Ili valley (occupied since 1871) to the Qing in exchange for territory west of the Khorgos River, an indemnity of 9 million rubles, and trade privileges. Implementation of the border demarcation extended into 1882–1885, and Xinjiang was formally organized as a Chinese province in 1884. The dataset records 'Russian Empire → Qing Dynasty' for 1884–1885 near Ili, capturing the final demarcation phases of this treaty.

w4-900344.name: London Convention (1884) – Restoration of South African Republic Independence
w4-900344.blurb: Following the First Anglo-Boer War (1880–1881) and the Boer victory at Majuba Hill, the Pretoria Convention (August 1881) restored limited Boer self-rule; the subsequent London Convention (February 27, 1884) superseded it and granted the South African Republic (Transvaal) full independence, with Paul Kruger representing the ZAR. The British relinquished administration of the Transvaal, returning territory from British Cape Colony control to the South African Republic. The dataset records this as a 1884–1885 transition, consistent with the ratification and implementation of the London Convention and the British withdrawal.

citations.label: First Anglo-Boer War – World History Encyclopedia

w4-900347.name: Treaty of Ancón — Chilean Occupation and Peruvian Civil War aftermath
w4-900347.blurb: The Treaty of Ancón (20 October 1883, ratified 1884) ended the War of the Pacific between Chile and Peru. Chile permanently acquired Tarapacá and administered Tacna and Arica for ten years pending a plebiscite. Dissatisfaction with the terms sparked the Peruvian Civil War of 1884–1885, after which Andrés Cáceres' government took power. The dataset records 'Republic of Chile → Republic of Peru' in 1884–1885 near the Andean interior, reflecting areas where Chilean occupation lines were withdrawn and Peruvian administration restored after the civil war.

w4-900351.name: Egyptian evacuation of Sudan / British assumption of Sudanese administration
w4-900351.blurb: Following the Mahdist uprising, the British-backed Egyptian government decided in early 1884 to abandon the Sudan. General Charles Gordon, sent to evacuate the garrisons, was instead besieged at Khartoum, which fell to the Mahdists in January 1885. Effective control of the Sudan thus passed directly from the Khedivate of Egypt to the Mahdist State; there was no intervening period of British administration, despite Britain's role in directing the evacuation.

w4-900352.name: Berlin Conference recognizes Leopold II's Congo Free State (26 February 1885)
w4-900352.blurb: On 31 March 1885 Britain proclaimed the Bechuanaland Protectorate over the territory north of the Molopo River, following the Warren Expedition mounted to forestall Boer and German encroachment along the 'Missionary Road' to the interior. The protectorate covered the lands of Tswana chiefdoms in what is now Botswana; the southern portion was constituted as the separate crown colony of British Bechuanaland (later annexed to the Cape Colony in 1895).

w4-900355.name: Italian colonization of Eritrea and founding of Colonia Eritrea
w4-900355.blurb: Italy established the Colony of Eritrea on January 1, 1890, consolidating its Red Sea coastal possessions (acquired from 1885 at Massawa) into a formal colony; this incorporated territory that had formerly been under Ethiopian imperial suzerainty or direct control, particularly the Tigrayan highlands and Red Sea littoral.

w4-900356.name: Italian protectorate treaty with Sultanate of Hobyo (1889)
w4-900356.blurb: In 1889 Sultan Yusuf Ali Kenadid of Hobyo signed a protectorate treaty with Italy, ceding nominal sovereignty to Italy's Benadir Company in exchange for backing against rival Somali powers; Italian chartered companies extended paper control over the Hobyo coast and hinterland by 1890.

w4-900357.name: Italian Protectorate over Majeerteen Sultanate
w4-900357.blurb: On 7 April 1889, Boqor Osman Mahmud of the Majeerteen Sultanate signed a protectorate treaty with Italy at Alula, following a conference of notables at Bargal; Italy agreed to provide arms and subsidies while pledging non-interference in internal administration in exchange for economic concessions.

w4-900359.to: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
w4-900359.name: Establishment of the Aden Protectorate
w4-900359.blurb: Between 1886 and 1888, Britain concluded a series of protection treaties with tribal rulers of the hinterland around Aden, formally establishing the Aden Protectorate; these agreements brought the territory under the Crown's direct jurisdiction, superseding earlier informal arrangements administered through the East India Company.

w4-900360.name: Proclamation of the Republic of Brazil
w4-900360.blurb: On 15 November 1889 Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca overthrew Emperor Pedro II in a bloodless military coup, abolishing the Empire of Brazil and proclaiming the republic. Brazil's entire territory (~8.4 million km²) transferred from the 'Empire of Brazil' to the 'Brazilian Republic' under the provisional government.

w4-900361.name: Limbang annexation by Sarawak (Charles Brooke, 1890)
w4-900361.blurb: In 1890 Rajah Charles Brooke of Sarawak annexed the Limbang district (~114.9°E/4.4°N) from Brunei without compensation, splitting Brunei into its two present non-contiguous parts. Britain, as Brunei's protecting power under the 1888 Protectorate Agreement, took no action because Sarawak was not considered a 'foreign power' under that treaty.

w4-900363.name: Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty (1890)
w4-900363.blurb: The Anglo-German Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty of 1 July 1890 formalised the division of East African spheres of influence: Germany's control over the Zanzibar Sultanate's mainland coast (future German East Africa/Tanganyika) was recognised, while Britain gained Zanzibar as a protectorate. This confirmed German East Africa Company control over coastal strips previously under Zanzibar suzerainty.

w4-900364.name: British Protectorate Agreement over Brunei (1888)
w4-900364.blurb: The Protectorate Agreement signed on 17 September 1888, negotiated by Sir Hugh Low, placed Brunei under British protection: the sultan could not cede or lease territory to foreign powers without British consent, and Britain controlled external affairs. The atlas shows Brunei territory (~114.6°E/4.6°N) transferring to the British colonial sphere as a result of this agreement.

w4-900365.name: Pahang Treaty / British Residency Established
w4-900365.blurb: The Pahang Treaty of 8 October 1887 (supplemented by a further agreement in 1888) compelled Sultan Ahmad of Pahang to accept a British Resident, formalising the extension of British protectorate authority over the ~40,000 km² sultanate. Britain applied sustained diplomatic and naval pressure following concerns about Pahang's instability and Siamese encroachment.

w4-900366.name: Rashidi Expansion under Muhammad ibn Rashid
w4-900366.blurb: Under Muhammad ibn Rashid, the Emirate of Jabal Shammar expanded aggressively in the 1880s, defeating Saudi forces and driving the Al Saud into exile in Kuwait by 1891; the territorial gains in this window (~1887) reflect the Rashidi military dominance over central Najd at the height of their power.

w4-900367.name: Fall of Khartoum and Mahdist conquest of Sudan
w4-900367.blurb: In January 1885 Mahdist forces under Muhammad Ahmad stormed Khartoum, killing General Gordon and completing their expulsion of Egyptian and British forces from Sudan. The Mahdist State then governed most of present-day Sudan until 1898, ending Egyptian/British control that had nominally held the territory.

w4-900368.name: French Protectorate over Luang Phrabang established
w4-900368.blurb: Following the devastating Black Flag / Haw raids of 1887, King Oun Kham of Luang Phrabang requested French protection, which was formalised in a protectorate treaty accepted in March 1889. The 1893 Franco-Siamese Treaty then confirmed French control over all Lao territories east of the Mekong; the atlas registers the Luang Phrabang polygon passing to French Indochina between 1885 and 1890.

w4-900369.name: Incorporation of Nieuwe Republiek into Transvaal (1888)
w4-900369.blurb: On 20 July 1888, the Nieuwe Republiek (New Republic), a small Boer state in northern Natal founded in 1884, voluntarily incorporated into the South African Republic (Transvaal). Facing British pressure — including annexation of its coastline in 1887 and Dinuzulu's revolt — President Lucas Meyer sought merger with Transvaal to avoid British absorption.

w4-900370.name: Franco-Siamese Treaty of 1893 – Siamese gains on west bank
w4-900370.blurb: The 1893 Franco-Siamese Treaty, while forcing Siam to cede territories east of the Mekong, also recognised Siamese administration over the right (west) bank territories opposite Luang Phrabang (centroid 101°E/18.8°N = Nan/Phrae region of northern Siam). The atlas records a ~16,500 km² block passing from 'Kingdom of Luang Phrabang' to 'Rattanakosin Kingdom' in the 1890–1895 window, reflecting demarcation of the Mekong as the new border which left west-bank Lao-speaking areas under Siamese control.

w4-900372.name: Franco-Siamese Treaty of 1893 and subsequent Mekong agreements
w4-900372.blurb: The Franco-Siamese Crisis of 1893 forced Siam to cede all territory east of the Mekong (Laos, including Luang Phrabang's eastern dependencies) to France; subsequent conventions in 1896 and 1904 further delimited French Indochina's borders. The centroid at 102.6°E, 20.2°N reflects the Luang Phrabang region incorporated into French Laos by these agreements.

w4-900373.name: Franco-Siamese Treaty of 1893 / French annexation of Champasak
w4-900373.blurb: The Franco-Siamese Treaty of October 1893, imposed after France's Paknam gunboat incident in July 1893, forced Siam to relinquish all territories east of the Mekong including Champasak. The Kingdom of Champasak was incorporated into French Indochina as a tributary vassal; the atlas records this consolidation in the 1890–1895 window.

w4-900374.name: Franco-Siamese Treaty of 1893 and 1896 conventions — French Laos
w4-900374.blurb: Under the Franco-Siamese Treaty of 1893, Siam ceded all territory east of the Mekong River to France. The centroid at 104.4°E, 16.5°N corresponds to the lower Mekong area (present-day central Laos/northeastern Thailand border), territory France incorporated into French Indochina (Laos) under this and the 1896 supplemental convention.

w4-900375.name: Convention of 1894 (Swaziland Convention)
w4-900375.blurb: The Swaziland Convention of 1894 transferred Swaziland to the South African Republic (Transvaal) as a protectorate, ending the tripartite British-Boer-Swazi administration established after King Mbandzeni's death in 1889. Swaziland came under Transvaal administration until the outbreak of the Second Boer War in 1899.

w4-900376.name: Anglo-German Declarations on the Western Pacific / British Protectorate over the Southern Solomons
w4-900376.blurb: In 1886 Germany and Britain delimited spheres of influence in the Pacific, with Germany relinquishing claims to the southern Solomon Islands; Britain declared a protectorate over the southern Solomons in June 1893, and the 1899 Samoa Treaty (Treaty of Berlin) formalised German cession of Choiseul, Santa Isabel, Shortlands, and Ontong Java to the British Solomon Islands Protectorate.

citations.label: Wikipedia: History of the Solomon Islands

w4-900377.name: Sarawak cessions to British North Borneo / British Colonial Empire (1890s)
w4-900377.blurb: In a series of agreements between the White Rajahs of Sarawak and the British government during the late 19th century, Sarawak's northern borderlands were demarcated and some areas transferred to direct British colonial administration (British North Borneo). The 1890 agreement fixed boundaries, and the Cliopatria dataset registers this boundary revision as a net transfer to the British Colonial Empire.

citations.label: Wikipedia: Sarawak under the Brooke family

w4-900378.name: British Uganda Protectorate expansion to Nile-Congo watershed
w4-900378.blurb: Between 1890 and 1895, Britain extended its control in the Uganda region to the Nile-Congo watershed (centroid ~31°E, 2.8°N, south-western Sudan/northern Uganda), displacing the Mahdist State's nominal authority over the upper Nile headwaters region; the Uganda Protectorate was formally declared in 1894 and the West Nile region incorporated.

w4-900379.name: Franco-British Convention on West African Boundaries (1889) and French advance into Ashanti hinterland
w4-900379.blurb: Following the Anglo-French Convention of 1889 that delimited spheres of influence in West Africa, French forces advanced northward from the Ivory Coast hinterland into territory the Ashanti Empire claimed. French treaties with local chiefs in the Gyaman/Brong area in the early 1890s brought these territories under French suzerainty before the 1895 British protectorate formalized the Ashanti's remaining core territory.

w4-900380.name: Cuban War of Independence (Grito de Baire)
w4-900380.blurb: The Grito de Baire on February 24, 1895 launched the Cuban War of Independence, with José Martí and generals Máximo Gómez and Antonio Maceo leading forces against Spanish colonial rule. Cuban nationalist insurgents seized substantial territory in eastern Cuba over the following years, representing territory effectively under rebel rather than Spanish control.

w4-900383.to: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
w4-900383.name: Exclusive Agreement of 1892 (Trucial States)
w4-900383.blurb: The Exclusive Agreement of March 1892 bound the rulers of the Trucial sheikhdoms (Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Umm Al Quwain) not to cede territory to, or enter relations with, any power other than Britain, cementing a de facto British protectorate over the Trucial Oman coast. The centroid near 25.7N, 56.1E lies on the Musandam/Trucial coast covered by this agreement. Qatar was not a party to the 1892 agreement; it came under a separate British treaty only in 1916, so the transfer here reflects British paramountcy over the Trucial sheikhdoms rather than over Qatar.

w4-900384.to: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
w4-900384.name: Exclusive Agreements with Trucial States
w4-900384.blurb: Between 6–8 March 1892, the rulers of Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, and Umm Al Quwain signed Exclusive Agreements with Britain pledging not to transfer territory or enter foreign relations without British consent, in return for British protection against external threats; this formalised British paramountcy.

w4-900385.name: Chitral Campaign and British Establishment of Gilgit Agency
w4-900385.blurb: In 1895 a British relief force broke the siege of Chitral and installed a compliant Mehtar (Shuja-ul-Mulk), while the Gilgit Agency was consolidated under British Indian political control through agents superintending the Jammu and Kashmir frontier states of Chitral and Hunza. These highland regions had previously lain under the loose suzerainty of the Dogra Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir, not the Talpurs of Sindh; the campaign brought them firmly within the British Raj's strategic sphere on the Hindu Kush frontier.

w4-900386.name: British Gilgit Agency and Northern Frontier Consolidation
w4-900386.blurb: The Gilgit Agency was reorganized and expanded by the British Indian government in 1889, consolidating control over the northern frontier territories of Kashmir (Gilgit, Hunza, Nagar, Yasin, Punial, Chitral) as part of the 'Great Game' against Russian expansion. The British leased and militarized these territories from the Maharaja of Kashmir; the 1895 period saw active British delimitation of the Pamir boundary and the Chitral campaign.

w4-900387.name: Overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom and proclamation of Republic of Hawaii (1893-1894)
w4-900387.blurb: On 17 January 1893, a Committee of Safety supported by U.S. Marines from the USS Boston overthrew Queen Liliʻuokalani. After President Cleveland refused to restore the monarchy, the Provisional Government proclaimed the Republic of Hawaiʻi on 4 July 1894 under President Sanford Dole. A royalist counter-coup in January 1895 failed, and Liliʻuokalani abdicated on 24 January 1895, formally ending the Hawaiian monarchy. Hawaii was annexed by the United States in 1898.

citations.label: Overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom - Wikipedia

w4-900391.name: Italian Protectorate over Sultanate of Hobyo
w4-900391.blurb: Sultan Yusuf Ali Kenadid of Hobyo signed a protectorate treaty with Italy on 8 February 1889, bringing the Sultanate of Hobyo (Obbia) under Italian suzerainty within Italian Africa. The atlas window (py=1890/y=1895) at (47.5,5.5) in central Somalia reflects this Italian control being consolidated and mapped, matching the from→to (Sultanate of Hobyo → Italian Africa).

w4-900392.name: Rise of the Darawiish (Dervish) State Against Italian Somaliland
w4-900392.blurb: Mohammed Abdullah Hassan (the 'Mad Mullah') returned to Somalia in 1895 after religious studies in Mecca and began organizing resistance to European colonialism. By 1899–1900 he had established the Dervish (Darawiish) state, which actively resisted Italian expansion in northeastern Somalia. The Italians controlled the Benadir coast and protectorates from the early 1890s but the interior territory around Nugaal fell under Dervish influence through a combination of raids and the 1905 Illig Treaty.

w4-900393.name: Mohammed Abdullah Hassan founds the Dervish movement in Somalia
w4-900393.blurb: Mohammed Abdullah Hassan began building his religious-military following from 1895 after preaching in Berbera, founding the Darawiish (Dervish) movement that resisted British, Italian, and Ethiopian forces until 1920. The from=Sultanate of Hobyo / to=Darawiish and the 1890-1895 window reflect the movement's founding and expansion into the central-Somali hinterland, though firm Dervish statehood centred at Taleh consolidated later (from 1899).

w4-900399.name: Second Madagascar Expedition and French conquest of the Merina Kingdom
w4-900399.blurb: France launched the Second Madagascar Expedition in 1895; General Duchesne's column occupied Antananarivo on 30 September 1895, and Queen Ranavalona III signed a protectorate treaty on 1 October 1895. The French parliament voted annexation on 6 August 1896, and Gallieni suppressed the Menalamba resistance, exiling the queen in 1897, with pacification largely complete by 1898. The worklist transfer (Merina Kingdom to French Africa, 1895-1898) matches conquest through pacification.

w4-900401.name: Proclamation of the Korean Empire
