w4-900656.blurb: After the Northern Expedition unified much of China under the Kuomintang in 1928, Liu Wenhui's Sichuan-based army strengthened control over eastern Kham (later Xikang province). This borderland between Tibet proper and Republican China (~99E 31N) was contested between Lhasa and Chinese warlords through the 1920s-1930s. Tibet kept de facto independence over its core, but the dataset records the nominal shift of eastern Kham toward Chinese Nationalist-aligned authority c. 1927-1928.

w4-900659.name: Northern Expedition — KMT unification of China (1926–1928)
w4-900659.blurb: The Northern Expedition (9 July 1926 – 29 December 1928), led by Chiang Kai-shek and the National Revolutionary Army, defeated the Beiyang warlord government and most regional militarists, achieving nominal unification of China under the Kuomintang's Nationalist Government at Nanjing by late 1928. Zhang Xueliang's allegiance declaration from Manchuria on 29 December 1928 completed the formal unification. The Cliopatria dataset records this transition (from the Kuomintang faction to the Republic of China) as fully reflected by the [1929,1930] window, consistent with the KMT's consolidation through the Central Plains War against residual warlords.

w4-900660.name: Allied evacuation of the Rhineland (Young Plan, 1930)
w4-900660.blurb: Under the Versailles Treaty the Rhineland was to be occupied until 1935, but the Young Plan (1929) led France and Britain to withdraw early. The last French troops left the Mainz zone on 30 June 1930, returning the Rhineland to full Weimar German sovereignty. The window (1929-1930) and coordinates (7.2, 49.2) fit this transfer.

w4-900662.name: Central Plains War
w4-900662.blurb: The Central Plains War (1929-1930) was a large-scale armed conflict between Chiang Kai-shek's Nanjing-based Kuomintang government and a coalition of warlord-generals including Feng Yuxiang, Yan Xishan, and the Guangxi clique, who rejected Nanjing's attempt to centralize military power. The coalition temporarily controlled large areas of Henan, Shanxi, and central China during 1930. Chiang ultimately prevailed when Zhang Xueliang's Manchurian forces entered the war on Nanjing's side in September 1930.

w4-900665.name: Kuwait-Iraq Border Formalised; Kuwait Confirmed as British Protectorate
w4-900665.blurb: In Iraq's 1932 application to the League of Nations, the Iraqi government formally acknowledged its border with Kuwait as defined in 1923 under British mediation. Kuwait remained a British protectorate (1899-1961). The dataset entry transferring from 'Kuwait' to 'United Kingdom' in 1930-1932 near lng 47.5, lat 29.5 reflects a model reclassification as British protectorate boundaries were formalised following Iraq's independence; it captures a real administrative-status event rather than an outright conquest.

w4-900666.name: League of Nations Class C Mandate for South West Africa administered by South Africa
w4-900666.blurb: After German South West Africa was conquered by South African forces in 1915, the League of Nations on 17 December 1920 granted South Africa a Class C Mandate to administer the territory. In Cliopatria this transfer (British Africa to South Africa at lat -25.9, lng 22.2, the SWA/Namibia region) registers in the 1930-1932 window, reflecting consolidation of direct South African administrative control rather than the initial mandate grant. South Africa treated the territory as a de facto fifth province, defying League and later UN oversight until Namibian independence in 1990.

w4-900669.name: Statute of Westminster 1931
w4-900669.blurb: The Statute of Westminster, passed by the British Parliament on 11 December 1931, granted full legislative independence to the Dominions of Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Ireland, and Newfoundland, formally ending British parliamentary supremacy over them. For Canada, this meant recognition as a fully sovereign state free from Westminster's legislative override, making the territorial extent previously administered as part of the British Colonial Empire into juridically Canadian territory. Canada had lobbied for this outcome since the Balfour Report of 1926 and the Imperial Conference of 1930.

citations.label: Statute of Westminster – The Canadian Encyclopedia

w4-900671.name: Siamese Revolution of 1932
w4-900671.blurb: On 24 June 1932 the Khana Ratsadon (People's Party), a group of European-educated military and civilian officers, staged a bloodless coup that ended Siam's absolute monarchy under the Chakri dynasty. King Prajadhipok accepted constitutional monarchy, and the country was renamed the Kingdom of Thailand in 1939. The coup transformed the Rattanakosin Kingdom into a constitutional monarchy without significant territorial change; the event marks the end of the Rattanakosin polity label.

w4-900673.name: Proclamation of the Second Spanish Republic
w4-900673.blurb: On 14 April 1931, following a landslide republican victory in municipal elections, King Alfonso XIII went into exile and the Second Spanish Republic was proclaimed. Spain's possessions, including the Spanish Sahara (coords near lng -3.4, lat 22.3), passed from the Kingdom of Spain to the new Republic. Matches worklist transition Kingdom of Spain -> Second Spanish Republic (1930-1932).

w4-900675.name: Brazilian Revolution of 1930 — Vargas provisional government
w4-900675.blurb: The Revolution of 1930 overthrew President Washington Luís and brought Getúlio Vargas to power as head of a provisional government, abrogating the 1891 Constitution and dissolving the National Congress. Vargas ruled by decree and strongly centralised federal authority over the states, effectively converting Brazil from the federated First Republic into a more unitary authoritarian state. The centralisation deepened after the Constitutionalist Revolution of 1932 in São Paulo was militarily defeated, giving Vargas even firmer control until a new constitution was enacted in 1934.

w4-900676.name: Sino-Tibetan War of 1930–1932
w4-900676.blurb: The Sino-Tibetan War began in 1930 when Tibetan forces entered eastern Kham (Xikang). ROC warlords Liu Wenhui (Sichuan) and Ma Bufang (Qinghai) counterattacked, pushing Tibetan forces back across the Jinsha River by 1932. The ceasefire left Kham territories east of the upper Yangtze under ROC authority. From 'Tibet' to 'Republic of China' at eastern-Kham coordinates; window py=1930, y=1932 fits.

w4-900677.name: CPC Long March ends — Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia base area established, 1935
w4-900677.blurb: The Long March (October 1934 – October 1935) brought the Chinese Communist Party's main Red Army forces to northern Shaanxi, where they established and consolidated the Shaanxi-Gansu base area later centered on Yan'an (centroid ~109.8°E, 37.9°N, roughly 42,000 km²). This transition reattributes that territory to CPC (Chinese Soviet) control, taken from the preceding Republican/warlord patchwork — the opposite direction from the original 'to: Republic of China' label, which is inverted.

w4-900679.name: CCP establishes the Jiangxi Soviet (Chinese Soviet Republic, 1931)
w4-900679.blurb: The Chinese Communist Party established the Chinese Soviet Republic (Jiangxi Soviet) on 7 November 1931 at Ruijin, carving substantial territory from Nationalist control in central China. Coordinates (113.1, 29.0, Hubei/Hunan region) fall within the Soviet's zone of expansion. The from->to (Republic of China -> Communist Party of China) in the 1930-1932 window matches this.

w4-900681.name: PCIJ Eastern Greenland Case (Denmark v. Norway)
w4-900681.blurb: In 1931 Norway occupied and claimed sovereignty over eastern Greenland ('Erik the Red's Land'). Denmark brought the case to the Permanent Court of International Justice, which ruled on 5 April 1933 that Denmark held sovereignty over the entire island of Greenland, rejecting Norway's claims. Norway accepted the ruling, and the territory reverted to unambiguous Danish/Greenlandic control by 1933–1936.

citations.label: Legal Status of Eastern Greenland (PCIJ, 1933) — Justia

w4-900683.name: Chinese Civil War - Long March and CCP consolidation in Shaanxi (1934-1936)
w4-900683.blurb: Under pressure from Chiang Kai-shek's Fifth Encirclement Campaign, the Chinese Communist Party abandoned its Jiangxi Soviet in October 1934 and completed the Long March, arriving in Shaanxi province by October 1935 with some 8,000 survivors. By October 1936 all three Red Army columns had united in northern Shaanxi, establishing the Yan'an base area. This shift represents Communist territory passing from Republic of China control in the central provinces to CCP-controlled Shaanxi, around the coordinates given.

w4-900686.name: Nationalist Fifth Encirclement Campaign and the Long March
w4-900686.blurb: Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist (Republic of China) Fifth Encirclement Campaign, launched in 1933, employed blockhouse tactics that surrounded and destroyed the Chinese Communist Party's Jiangxi Soviet base in central China (roughly lng 113, lat 29). Unable to hold their positions, the CCP abandoned the Soviet in October 1934 and began the Long March, eventually reaching Yan'an in Shaanxi in 1935–1936. By 1936, the Nationalists had effective control of the territories formerly held by the CCP in central and southern China. The dataset records this shift (Communist Party of China → Republic of China) as occurring between 1932 and 1936, capturing the full arc of Nationalist pressure and Communist withdrawal.

w4-900687.name: Nazi seizure of power (Machtergreifung) and Gleichschaltung
w4-900687.blurb: Adolf Hitler was appointed Chancellor on 30 January 1933; the Enabling Act of March 1933 granted dictatorial powers, ending the Weimar Republic and inaugurating the Third Reich. The subsequent Gleichschaltung (1933-35) abolished state governments and replaced them with Nazi Gaue under direct Reich control. The worklist window of 1932-1936 (Weimar Republic to Nazi Germany) reflects this full transition to consolidated Nazi rule, with the Rhineland remilitarized by 1936.

citations.label: States of the Weimar Republic – Wikipedia

w4-900688.name: Anglo-Egyptian Treaty of 1936
w4-900688.blurb: The Anglo-Egyptian Treaty of 1936 ended Britain's formal occupation of Egypt while maintaining British forces in the Suez Canal Zone and confirming the Anglo-Egyptian Condominium over Sudan. The coordinates (36 degrees E, 31 degrees N) point to Egypt/Sinai/Palestine. In the Cliopatria dataset 'British Africa' likely encompasses the Anglo-Egyptian administrative sphere; the treaty's partial sovereignty restoration shifted Egypt and adjacent territories from a 'British Africa' entity toward direct United Kingdom mandate and treaty-based administration. Britain retained Mandatory Palestine and Transjordan as League of Nations mandates under direct UK administration throughout this period.

w4-900689.name: Kondylis Coup and Abolition of the Second Hellenic Republic
w4-900689.blurb: On October 10, 1935, General Georgios Kondylis overthrew the Tsaldaris government, declared himself regent, and abolished the Second Hellenic Republic. A rigged plebiscite on November 3, 1935, restored King George II and the Kingdom of Greece. The dataset's 'First Hellenic Republic' label (coords 23.4E/38.3N, Athens) is a mislabeling for the restored Kingdom of Greece; the real event is the 1935 royalist counter-revolution captured in the [py=1932, y=1936] window.

w4-900691.name: End of US occupation of Haiti – withdrawal of Marines (1934)
w4-900691.blurb: Under FDR's Good Neighbor Policy, the US and Haiti signed a disengagement agreement in August 1933 and the last US Marines departed on 15 August 1934, restoring Haitian sovereignty. The coordinates are Haiti, matching the recorded United States → Republic of Haiti transfer for 1932–1936.

citations.label: United States occupation of Haiti – Wikipedia
The American Withdrawal from Haiti, 1929-1934 – Duke University Press

w4-900696.name: First Vienna Award
w4-900696.blurb: The First Vienna Award (2 November 1938), arbitrated by Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy, compelled Czechoslovakia to cede the predominantly Hungarian-populated southern strip of Slovakia and southern Carpathian Ruthenia to the Kingdom of Hungary - about 11,927 km2 (19.6E, 48.3N, southern Slovakia). Presented as ethnic revision following the Munich Agreement, it reversed part of the Trianon settlement; the territories were declared void by the Paris Peace Treaties (1947) and returned to Czechoslovakia.

w4-900701.name: Bunreacht na hÉireann — Irish Free State becomes Éire
w4-900701.blurb: De Valera's constitution (Bunreacht na hÉireann), approved by plebiscite on 1 July 1937, came into effect 29 December 1937, renaming the state Ireland/Éire. The coordinates (-8.2,53.4) are Ireland, matching the from→to (Irish Free State → Éire) in the 1936–1938 window.

w4-900702.name: Sheng Shicai aligns Xinjiang with Soviet Union and CCP (Second United Front period)
w4-900702.blurb: From 1934, warlord Sheng Shicai ruled Xinjiang as a de facto Soviet protectorate; he joined the CPSU in 1938 and invited Chinese Communist Party cadres to staff his administration during the Second United Front. Cliopatria codes Xinjiang (centroid lat 42.3, lng 92.4) as shifting from nominal 'Republic of China' to 'Communist Party of China' control in 1936-1938, reflecting the period when Soviet/CCP influence replaced nominal Nationalist authority. Sheng's purges (1937-1938) followed Soviet models and were supported by NKVD advisors.

w4-900705.name: Battle of Wuhan and Japanese occupation of central China (1938)
w4-900705.blurb: During the Second Sino-Japanese War, Japan captured Wuhan on 27 October 1938 after the Battle of Wuhan (June-October 1938), forcing the Nationalist government to retreat to Chongqing. By 1939 Japan occupied large portions of central and coastal China including the Yangtze valley near the dataset coordinates (114.4, 28.1, Jiangxi/Hubei region). Republic of China -> Empire of Japan in the 1938-1939 window matches this occupation.

w4-900706.name: First Vienna Award (1938); Hungary gains southern Slovakia
w4-900706.blurb: On 2 November 1938 the German-Italian First Vienna Award compelled Czechoslovakia to cede roughly 11,900 km2 of southern Slovakia and Carpathian Ruthenia to Hungary. The window (1938-1939) and Slovak-Hungarian border coordinates (20.9, 48.5) match this transfer.

w4-900708.name: Spanish Civil War — Nationalist Victory
w4-900708.blurb: The Spanish Civil War began on 17 July 1936 when generals Franco and Mola launched a Nationalist uprising against the elected Second Spanish Republic. German and Italian military support gave the Nationalists decisive advantages. Barcelona fell on 26 January 1939, France and Britain recognized Franco's government on 27 February 1939, and Franco declared final victory on 1 April 1939. This ended the Republic and established Francoist Spain. The coordinates reflect the Spanish Sahara region where Nationalist control was also established.

w4-900714.name: Rally of French Equatorial Africa and Cameroon to Free France
w4-900714.blurb: Following France's armistice with Germany in June 1940, Governor Félix Éboué of Chad declared for de Gaulle's Free France on 26 August 1940. Cameroon followed the same day under Philippe Leclerc, and French Congo and Ubangi-Shari joined within days, forming Free French Africa with Brazzaville as its capital (Cliopatria centroid lat 4, lng 17.9, in Ubangi-Shari/Central Africa). This matches the French Africa to Free French transfer in the 1939-1940 window.

w4-900716.name: Xinjiang's Soviet protectorate deepened under Sheng Shicai (1940 Treaty)
w4-900716.blurb: On 26 November 1940, Sheng Shicai signed a 50-year tin mining treaty with the USSR, granting Soviet economic and strategic control over Xinjiang. Cliopatria codes this as territory (centroid lat 42.3, lng 85, Tarim Basin region) shifting from 'Communist Party of China' to 'Union of Soviet Socialist Republics' in 1939-1940. This reflects the progressive Sovietization of Xinjiang under Sheng Shicai that made the province 'a part of China in name only,' with all major decisions cleared through the Soviet consulate.

w4-900717.name: Soviet occupation and annexation of Latvia
w4-900717.blurb: Under the secret protocol of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact (1939), Latvia fell within the Soviet sphere; the Red Army occupied it on 16–17 June 1940 after an ultimatum, and rigged elections led to formal annexation into the USSR on 5 August 1940. The coordinates (24.6,57) are Latvia, matching the from→to (Republic of Latvia → USSR) in the 1939–1940 window.

citations.label: Soviet occupation of Latvia in 1940 – Wikipedia

w4-900719.name: Soviet Occupation and Annexation of Lithuania (1940)
w4-900719.blurb: On 15 June 1940, the Soviet Union issued an ultimatum to Lithuania demanding unlimited troop access and a friendly government, then occupied the country the same day. Rigged elections in July produced a rubber-stamp parliament that requested admission to the USSR; Lithuania was formally incorporated on 3 August 1940. This Soviet action, enabled by the secret Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact (1939), was not recognised by most Western governments.

citations.label: Soviet occupation of the Baltic states (1940) – Wikipedia
Occupation of the Baltic states – Wikipedia

w4-900720.name: Soviet invasion of Poland (1939)
w4-900720.blurb: On 17 September 1939, sixteen days after the German invasion began, the Soviet Red Army crossed Poland's eastern border under the pretext of protecting Ukrainian and Belarusian minorities, in accordance with the secret protocol of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact. Soviet forces rapidly overran eastern Poland; by 6 October Germany and the Soviet Union divided the entire Second Polish Republic between themselves. The USSR annexed approximately 200,000 km2 of eastern Poland, incorporating it into the Ukrainian and Belarusian SSRs.

w4-900721.name: Soviet occupation of Estonia (1940)
w4-900721.blurb: Following the Molotov–Ribbentrop secret protocol, the USSR issued an ultimatum on 16-17 June 1940 and occupied Estonia, annexing it in August 1940. Estonia passed from Estonian to Soviet control within the 1939-1940 window. Well attested.

citations.label: Occupation of the Baltic states – Wikipedia

w4-900722.name: Italian invasion of British Somaliland (1940)
w4-900722.blurb: After Italy entered World War II on 10 June 1940, Italian East African forces under General Guglielmo Nasi invaded the British Somaliland Protectorate on 3 August 1940. Outnumbering the defenders roughly three to one, Italian and colonial troops defeated the garrison at the Battle of Tug Argan and the British evacuated to Aden on 19 August 1940, giving Italy temporary control over British Somaliland. Britain reconquered it in March 1941 during Operation Appearance.

citations.label: Italian invasion of British Somaliland - Wikipedia
East African campaign (World War II) - Wikipedia

w4-900723.name: Fall of France: Vichy regime takes over French colonial empire
w4-900723.blurb: Following the Franco-German Armistice of 22 June 1940, the Vichy regime under Marshal Pétain retained authority over the French colonial empire, including French West Africa, until Allied Operation Torch (November 1942) brought most French Africa over to the Free French. Matches the French Third Republic → Vichy France transfer in the 1939-1940 window.

citations.label: French West Africa in World War II – Wikipedia

w4-900724.name: British invasion and occupation of Iceland (Operation Fork)
w4-900724.blurb: On 10 May 1940, following Germany's occupation of Denmark (Iceland's royal suzerain), British Royal Marines landed at Reykjavík in Operation Fork and occupied Iceland without resistance despite the Icelandic government's formal protest. Britain feared Germany might seize the strategically vital island dominating North Atlantic convoy routes. The Icelandic government acquiesced to the occupation under protest and the British promised full withdrawal at war's end and compensation for any damages.

w4-900733.type: wartime defense agreement / de facto occupation
w4-900733.name: US–Denmark Defense of Greenland Agreement (1941)
w4-900733.blurb: With Denmark under German occupation, Danish Ambassador Henrik Kauffmann unilaterally signed the 'Agreement Relating to the Defense of Greenland' with the United States on 9 April 1941, authorizing the US to establish bases and occupy Greenland to prevent German use of it. US forces began arriving in 1941, establishing airfields and weather stations. Denmark retained nominal sovereignty but the US exercised effective administrative and military control, matching the window [1940,1941].

citations.label: Wikipedia: Greenland in World War II

w4-900737.name: Axis invasion of Yugoslavia and proclamation of the Independent State of Croatia
w4-900737.blurb: Germany and its Axis allies invaded Yugoslavia on 6 April 1941 (Operation Castigo/Marita), overrunning the country within eleven days; Yugoslavia surrendered on 17 April 1941. On 10 April, as German troops entered Zagreb, the Ustaše movement under Slavko Kvaternik proclaimed the Independent State of Croatia (Nezavisna Država Hrvatska, NDH), encompassing most of modern Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. Ante Pavelić returned from exile to lead the NDH as Poglavnik (leader), establishing a fascist puppet state under German and Italian sponsorship.

w4-900738.name: East African Campaign: British conquest of Italian East Africa
w4-900738.blurb: Following Italy's declaration of war in June 1940, British Commonwealth forces launched a three-pronged offensive against Italian East Africa (Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Italian Somaliland) in January 1941. By May 1941 the main Italian forces had surrendered at Amba Alagi, and the remnants capitulated at Gondar in November 1941. The campaign placed the former Italian East African territories (Cliopatria coordinates lat 15.2, lng 37.4, in the Eritrea/Ethiopia region) under British military administration,

citations.label: How Italy Was Defeated in East Africa 1941 – IWM

w4-900739.name: Axis Invasion of Yugoslavia — Italian Annexation of Dalmatia
w4-900739.blurb: On 6 April 1941 the Axis powers invaded Yugoslavia; eleven days later the kingdom surrendered. Italy immediately annexed large portions of the Dalmatian coast, the Bay of Kotor, Gorski Kotar, and most Adriatic islands as the Governorate of Dalmatia, formalized by the Treaty of Rome with the puppet Independent State of Croatia on 18 May 1941. This is the 'Yugoslavia → Kingdom of Italy' transfer in Dalmatia documented in the dataset.

citations.label: World War II in Yugoslavia – Wikipedia

w4-900741.name: Axis invasion of Yugoslavia — Operation 25 (April 1941)
w4-900741.blurb: After a Yugoslav coup on 27 March 1941 overturned accession to the Tripartite Pact, Hitler issued Directive No. 25 and the Axis invaded Yugoslavia on 6 April 1941. The Royal Yugoslav Army surrendered on 17 April; Yugoslavia was partitioned and the territory around lng 18.1, lat 43.9 (Bosnia-Herzegovina) was assigned to the German-controlled Axis order (Yugoslavia -> Nazi Germany), matching the [1940,1941] window.

citations.label: Axis invasion of Yugoslavia – Holocaust Encyclopedia

w4-900742.name: Axis invasion and occupation of Greece (Operation Marita)
w4-900742.blurb: Germany invaded Greece on 6 April 1941 (Operation Marita) following a failed Italian invasion. Within roughly three weeks the Greek army and British Expeditionary Force were overwhelmed; German troops entered Athens on 27 April 1941, and mainland Greece was divided into German, Italian, and Bulgarian occupation zones. Nazi Germany controlled key strategic areas including Athens, Thessaloniki, Central Macedonia, and most of Crete, while the Greek government went into exile. (The atlas 'First Hellenic Republic' label is anachronistic; the territory is Greece.)

citations.label: Military history of Greece during World War II – Wikipedia

w4-900743.name: German Afrika Korps Advance in North Africa (Operation Sonnenblume, 1941)
w4-900743.blurb: After Italy's 10th Army was destroyed by the British in Operation Compass (December 1940–February 1941), Hitler dispatched the Afrika Korps under General Erwin Rommel (Operation Sonnenblume, February 1941). Rommel launched an immediate offensive in March–April 1941, recapturing most of Cyrenaica (Libya) and driving the British back to the Egyptian frontier, placing the Italian-administered territory under German operational control by spring 1941.

w4-900745.name: Japanese occupation of French Indochina
w4-900745.blurb: Japan invaded northern French Indochina in September 1940 and extended occupation to southern Indochina on 28 July 1941 with about 140,000 troops; the Vichy administration agreed to Japanese military use of Indochinese territory. The from=French Indochina / to=Empire of Japan and 1940-1941 window match the Japanese occupation.

citations.label: Japanese invasion of French Indochina - Wikipedia
French Indochina in World War II - Wikipedia

w4-900746.name: Hungarian occupation of Yugoslav Bačka and Baranja (April 1941)
w4-900746.blurb: On 11 April 1941 Hungarian forces crossed into Yugoslavia alongside the German-led Axis invasion, occupying Bačka and Baranja — territories lost under the 1920 Treaty of Trianon. Yugoslav capitulation followed on 17–18 April, and Hungary annexed these regions. The coordinates (18°E, 46.1°N) place this in Vojvodina/Baranya, matching the Yugoslavia→Hungary transfer.

citations.label: Hungarian occupation of Yugoslav territories – Wikipedia

w4-900752.name: Japanese Invasion of Sarawak (1941–1942)
w4-900752.blurb: Japanese forces landed at Miri, Sarawak (coords 112.7E/3N), on December 16, 1941, seizing the oil fields; Kuching fell on Christmas Day 1941, and by February 1942 the entire territory was under Japanese occupation. Rajah Charles Vyner Brooke, abroad in Australia, could not return. The occupation lasted until Australian forces liberated Sarawak in September 1945.

citations.label: Japanese occupation of British Borneo – Wikipedia

w4-900756.name: Finnish advance in East Karelia during the Continuation War
w4-900756.blurb: After the USSR launched air raids on Finnish cities on 25 June 1941, Finland entered the Continuation War and launched a major offensive to recover territories lost in the 1940 Winter War and to occupy Soviet East Karelia. By autumn 1941 Finnish forces had retaken the Winter War cessions and advanced well beyond the old border into East Karelia, reaching the Svir River and capturing Petrozavodsk. Finland established a military administration over occupied East Karelia on 19 July 1941, holding these territories until the Soviet summer offensive of June 1944 forced a retreat.

citations.label: Finnish invasion of East Karelia (1941) – Wikipedia

w4-900757.name: Anglo-Soviet Invasion of Iran (Operation Countenance)
w4-900757.blurb: On August 25, 1941, British and Soviet forces jointly invaded neutral Iran (Operation Countenance) to secure its oil fields, the Trans-Iranian Railway supply route to the USSR, and to prevent German influence from exploiting Iranian territory. British forces advanced from the south and west, occupying the Khuzestan oil fields and southern/central Iran, while Soviet forces entered from the north. Reza Shah Pahlavi abdicated on September 16, 1941, in favor of his son Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, under Allied pressure. The 1941–1942 transition in the dataset (Pahlavi Dynasty → British Colonial Empire) reflects the establishment of the formal British occupation zone following the Tripartite Treaty of January 1942.

citations.label: The Anglo-Soviet Invasion of Iran – Brilliant Maps

w4-900758.name: East African Campaign (WWII) — British-led liberation of Ethiopia
w4-900758.blurb: British, Commonwealth, Free French, and Ethiopian Patriot forces defeated Italian East Africa in early 1941; Addis Ababa fell on 6 April 1941 and Haile Selassie returned on 5 May. The Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement of 31 January 1942 formalised the restoration of Ethiopian sovereignty under British advisory oversight, transferring effective control from British Africa military administration back to Ethiopia. The dataset window of 1941–1942 matches.

citations.label: East African campaign (World War II) — Wikipedia

w4-900759.name: Free French consolidation of Equatorial Africa (1940-1942)
w4-900759.blurb: After France's armistice with Germany in June 1940, the territories of French Equatorial Africa (including Chad, Cameroon, Congo, Ubangi-Shari, and Gabon) rallied to de Gaulle's Free France, forming 'Free French Africa' (Afrique française libre). The dataset records a transition from 'French Africa' to 'Free French' around 1941-1942 at coordinates near Chad (29.4E, 13.9N). Chad served as the primary base for Colonel Leclerc's campaigns into Italian Libya; Free French forces fought at Bir Hakeim in May-June 1942.

w4-900760.name: Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran (Operation Countenance) - Soviet occupation of northern Iran
w4-900760.blurb: On 25-26 August 1941 British and Soviet forces jointly invaded neutral Iran (Operation Countenance), citing the presence of German nationals and the need to keep open the Trans-Iranian supply corridor for Lend-Lease deliveries. Soviet forces rapidly occupied northern Iran; Reza Shah abdicated on 16 September 1941 in favor of his son Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. The northern zone (~49.7E, 37.8N = Azerbaijan/Alborz region) remained under Soviet occupation until May 1946.

w4-900762.name: Italian occupation of southeastern France — Case Anton (November 1942)
w4-900762.blurb: Following the Allied landings in North Africa (Operation Torch, 8 November 1942), Germany and Italy launched Case Anton, occupying all of Vichy France. The Italian 4th Army seized the French Riviera, Nice, and Provence up to the Rhone, formally occupying the zone from 11 November 1942. The occupation lasted until Italy's armistice in September 1943.

w4-900763.name: German Occupation of the Free Zone (Case Anton / Operation Attila)
w4-900763.blurb: On 11 November 1942, following the Allied landings in North Africa (Operation Torch), Nazi Germany launched Case Anton (planned as Operation Attila), occupying the previously unoccupied southern 'Free Zone' of Vichy France. Vichy lost its limited autonomy; the French fleet at Toulon scuttled itself on 27 November 1942. Transfer Vichy France -> Nazi Germany fits the 1942-1943 window.

w4-900764.name: German occupation of Tunisia — Tunisian campaign (November 1942)
w4-900764.blurb: Triggered by the Allied landings in North Africa (Operation Torch, 8 November 1942), Nazi Germany rushed troops into Tunisia from 9–10 November 1942, seizing El Aouina airfield and Tunis by 14 November. Germany occupied the French North African territory to deny Allied use of Tunisian ports and support Rommel's retreating Afrika Korps. Axis forces in Tunisia surrendered in May 1943.

w4-900769.name: Japanese invasion and occupation of the Dutch East Indies
w4-900769.blurb: Japan's invasion of the Dutch East Indies began on 10 January 1942 as part of its southward resource-driven strategy. Dutch forces surrendered unconditionally at Kalijati on 8 March 1942, ending 300 years of Dutch colonial presence in under three months. Japan occupied the entire archipelago (Cliopatria centroid lat -2.6, lng 118, central Indonesia) until its own surrender in August 1945,

citations.label: Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies – Wikipedia

w4-900773.name: WWII wartime administrative unification of Papua and New Guinea under Australia
w4-900773.blurb: Although Papua had been administered by Australia since 1906 (while remaining legally British), the Japanese invasion of New Guinea in early 1942 forced an emergency consolidation. In 1942 Australia formed the Australian New Guinea Administrative Unit (ANGAU) to provide unified civilian-military governance over both territories. This effectively completed the practical transfer of all administrative authority over the region from residual British to Commonwealth of Australia control for the remainder of the war.

w4-900778.name: Sheng Shicai breaks with Soviets and re-aligns with Nationalist China
w4-900778.blurb: After Germany's invasion of the Soviet Union in 1941 threatened Soviet power, Sheng Shicai judged the USSR weakened and expelled Soviet advisors, arrested CCP cadres (including Mao Zedong's brother Mao Zemin, later executed), and realigned Xinjiang (centroid lat 42.3, lng 85) with Chiang Kai-shek's Kuomintang government in 1942. Cliopatria codes this as Xinjiang returning from CCP/Soviet-aligned 'Communist Party of China' control to 'Republic of China' control in 1942-1943.

w4-900782.name: Yugoslav Partisan liberation of Dalmatia
w4-900782.blurb: After Italy's capitulation (September 1943) the Yugoslav Partisans expanded into Dalmatia; the Knin Operation (November–December 1944) cleared German and NDH forces from northern Dalmatia. The Dalmatian hinterland near lng 16.9 E / lat 43.9 N passed from the Independent State of Croatia / Axis control to the Yugoslav Partisans, matching the [1943,1944] window.

w4-900785.name: Operation Margarethe – Nazi Germany occupies Hungary (March 1944)
w4-900785.blurb: On 19 March 1944, German Wehrmacht forces occupied Hungary in Operation Margarethe, launched because Hitler feared Hungary was negotiating a separate peace with the Allies. Regent Miklós Horthy was coerced into appointing a pro-German government under Döme Sztójay, reducing Hungary to a German-controlled satellite. This marks the effective transfer of Hungarian territory to German military control.

w4-900786.name: Tunisia Campaign / Allied liberation of Tunisia from Axis
w4-900786.blurb: Axis forces under Rommel and von Arnim occupied Tunisia from November 1942. The Allied Tunisia Campaign concluded on 13 May 1943 with the surrender of some 260,000 Axis troops, restoring French colonial authority (here 'French Africa') over the protectorate (coordinates 10.7E, 34.8N). The worklist's y=1944 reflects a one-year lag in the Cliopatria political record.

w4-900787.name: Allied Conquest of Italian Libya and French Occupation of Fezzan
w4-900787.blurb: Following the North African campaign, Allied forces expelled Axis troops from Libya by February 1943. Italian Libya was placed under Allied Military Administration: the British controlled Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, while France administered the Fezzan-Ghadames territory from its base in Chad. This French military administration of Fezzan lasted until Libyan independence in 1951.

w4-900788.name: Allied reconquest of Libya from Axis forces and British Military Administration (1943)
w4-900788.blurb: By February 1943 Axis forces were expelled from Libya after El Alamein (1942) and the Allied advance; a British Military Administration was established over Tripolitania and Cyrenaica in 1943. The coordinates (23.7°E, 32.9°N) match Cyrenaica; from=Nazi Germany, to=British Africa matches the 1943-1944 window.

w4-900789.name: Allied North Africa Campaign — British forces defeat Italy and occupy Libya (1942–1943)
w4-900789.blurb: After the Second Battle of El Alamein (Oct–Nov 1942), the British Eighth Army pursued the Axis across Libya, taking Tripoli by January 1943; the final Axis surrender in Tunisia on 13 May 1943 ended Italian presence in North Africa. Libya came under British and French military administration, transferring territory from 'Italian Africa' to 'British Africa'. The dataset window of 1943–1944 matches.

w4-900790.name: New Guinea Campaign — Australian Liberation of Papua New Guinea
w4-900790.blurb: Australian and Allied forces launched major offensives in 1943–1944 to liberate New Guinea from Japanese occupation. The September 1943 capture of Lae by the 7th and 9th Australian Divisions was a turning point; by April 1944 Madang was liberated, restoring Australian administration. Coordinates (144.7, −5.2) place this in the Lae/Huon Gulf area, the epicenter of the 1943 campaign.

citations.label: New Guinea Offensive – Australian War Memorial

w4-900799.name: Yugoslav Partisan Liberation of Yugoslavia
w4-900799.blurb: Tito's Partisans, under AVNOJ, progressively liberated Yugoslav territory from Axis occupation in 1944–1945, aided by Soviet forces at Belgrade (October 1944). By May 1945 all Axis forces were expelled; the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia was proclaimed in November 1945. Territory (~17.7E/43.7N) moved from Partisan control to the Yugoslav state. Window [1944,1945], date 1945.

citations.label: Anti-Fascist Council for the National Liberation of Yugoslavia – Wikipedia

w4-900801.name: Liberation and dissolution of the Independent State of Croatia (NDH), 1945
w4-900801.blurb: The Independent State of Croatia (Nezavisna Država Hrvatska), a fascist Ustaše puppet state from April 1941, collapsed in May 1945 as Yugoslav Partisan forces captured Zagreb and the Axis surrendered. Its territory was reconstituted within Democratic Federal Yugoslavia. The coordinates correspond to central Bosnia, part of the NDH that reverted to Yugoslavia, matching Independent State of Croatia -> Yugoslavia in [1944,1945].

citations.label: World War II in Yugoslavia – Wikipedia

w4-900802.name: Belgrade Offensive — Bulgaria Switches Sides and Withdraws from Yugoslav Territory
w4-900802.blurb: Bulgaria had occupied Vardar Macedonia and parts of eastern Serbia as an Axis power since 1941. Following the pro-Soviet coup of 9 September 1944, Bulgaria declared war on Germany and three Bulgarian armies joined Soviet and Yugoslav Partisan forces in the Belgrade Offensive (September–November 1944). Under the armistice of 28 October 1944, Bulgaria was required to evacuate all Yugoslav territory; liberated Serbian and Macedonian lands (near lng 21.7, lat 42.5) passed back to Yugoslav authority by early 1945. The dataset records 'Bulgaria → Yugoslavia' for 1944–1945.

citations.label: World War II in Yugoslavia – Wikipedia

w4-900803.name: Liberation of Belgium from Nazi Germany (1944–1945)
w4-900803.blurb: The Liberation of Belgium began on 2 September 1944 when Allied forces (primarily British, Canadian, and American) crossed the Belgian border and liberated Brussels on 3 September and Antwerp on 4 September. Germany's Ardennes Offensive (Battle of the Bulge, December 1944–January 1945) temporarily reoccupied parts of eastern Belgium. The last Belgian territory was liberated on 4 February 1945.

citations.label: Belgium in World War II – Wikipedia

w4-900808.name: Liberation of Norway from German occupation (May 1945)
w4-900808.blurb: On 8 May 1945 German forces in Norway surrendered; Norwegian exile forces (trained in Sweden) entered the country and King Haakon VII returned on 7 June. The worklist's Kingdom of Sweden→Kingdom of Norway label is imprecise — Norway was under German, not Swedish, control 1940–1945 — and likely maps the Sweden-based exile forces or post-liberation restoration of sovereignty. The underlying event, the German capitulation of 8 May 1945, is real and restored Norwegian territory.

w4-900809.name: Liberation of Norway from Nazi Germany
w4-900809.blurb: Following Germany's unconditional surrender on 8 May 1945, the roughly 350,000 German troops in Norway capitulated. The Norwegian government-in-exile returned from London and the Kingdom of Norway was restored to full sovereignty, ending five years of occupation that had begun with Operation Weserübung in April 1940. From 'Nazi Germany' to 'Kingdom of Norway' fits; window py=1944, y=1945.

w4-900815.name: Papua New Guinea Provisional Administration Act
w4-900815.blurb: In 1945-46 Australia passed the Papua New Guinea Provisional Administration Act, combining the Territory of Papua and the Territory of New Guinea into a single Australian administration as the Japanese surrender allowed civil rule to resume. The coordinates (lat -5.4, lng 146.7) lie in the former Territory of New Guinea; the from-British attribution is loose (this area was German then a League mandate), but the consolidation under Australian administration in 1945 is well attested. Window 1944-1945.

citations.label: Territory of Papua and New Guinea – Wikipedia

w4-900817.name: German withdrawal from Greece — Liberation of Athens
w4-900817.blurb: As Soviet forces advanced through Romania and the Balkans in autumn 1944, German forces began withdrawing from Greece to avoid encirclement. Athens was liberated on 12 October 1944 when the last German troops departed; British forces under General Scobie arrived on 14 October, and the Greek government-in-exile returned. German garrisons on Crete and some Aegean islands remained until surrendering to the Allies in May-June 1945. Greece was thus restored to the Kingdom of Greece, though it immediately faced civil war between communist EAM/ELAS and royalist/British-backed forces.

citations.label: Liberation of Athens – Greek City Times

w4-900818.name: Bulgarian withdrawal from occupied Greek Thrace (Moscow Armistice 1944)
w4-900818.blurb: Bulgaria occupied Greek Western Thrace and Macedonia after joining the Axis in March 1941. Bulgaria switched sides on 8 September 1944; under Soviet/Allied pressure it ordered withdrawal from Greek and Yugoslav territory on 10 October 1944, codified by the Moscow Armistice (28 October 1944). Coord 24.4E/41N is in Greek Thrace. The 1947 Paris Peace Treaties confirmed the return. The dataset's donor label 'Principality of Bulgaria' is anachronistic but identifies Bulgaria; event real and correctly dated.

citations.label: Bulgaria during World War II – Wikipedia
Armistice Agreement with Bulgaria (1944) – Avalon Project

w4-900820.name: Liberation of France and the Provisional Government (GPRF)
w4-900820.blurb: After the liberation of Paris (25 August 1944), the Provisional Government of the French Republic (GPRF) succeeded the Free French movement and reasserted French sovereignty over the empire, including French Guiana (which had rallied from Vichy to Free France). The dataset labels the restored republican government 'French Fourth Republic'; in 1946 French Guiana was formally constituted as an overseas department under the new constitution. The transition from Free French to the restored French republic in 1944-45 is well attested.

w4-900821.name: Liberation of the Netherlands from Nazi Germany
w4-900821.blurb: Following the partial liberation of the southern Netherlands in Operation Market Garden (September 1944) and the Dutch Hunger Winter of 1944-1945, Canadian and Allied forces launched the final offensive in April 1945, fully liberating the country by May 1945. Central Netherlands (lat 52.1, lng 5.3) reverted to Dutch sovereignty. Window 1944-1945.

w4-900823.name: Moscow Armistice (1944): Finland cedes territory to USSR
w4-900823.blurb: The Moscow Armistice of 19 September 1944 ended the Continuation War; Finland restored the 1940 Moscow Peace Treaty borders, ceding parts of Karelia, Salla and Petsamo and leasing Porkkala to the USSR. Coord 30.1E/65.2N is in the ceded northern Karelia/Salla region. The 1947 Paris Peace Treaties confirmed these provisions. The dataset's 'Republic of Finland → USSR' shift matches; event real and correctly dated.

w4-900825.name: Soviet occupation of Bulgaria and Fatherland Front coup
w4-900825.blurb: On 8-9 September 1944 the Soviet Red Army crossed into Bulgaria unopposed after declaring war on 5 September, while the Fatherland Front (a coalition dominated by the Bulgarian Communist Party) simultaneously staged a coup in Sofia, overthrowing the Muraviev government. Bulgaria signed an armistice with the Allies on 28 October 1944 and its army was placed under Soviet operational command. The country then fought alongside the Soviets against Germany in Yugoslavia and Hungary until May 1945. In Cliopatria's model this Soviet-occupation period is represented as the USSR controlling Bulgarian territory.

citations.label: Bulgaria during World War II – Wikipedia

w4-900826.name: Soviet annexation of the Tuvan People's Republic (1944)
w4-900826.blurb: On 11 October 1944, the Soviet Union annexed the Tuvan People's Republic (Tannu-Tuva), framing it as a voluntary petition by Tuva's rubber-stamp parliament (Small People's Khural). The annexation occurred while Allied attention was focused on the final stages of World War II and was designed to secure Tuva's mineral resources and strategic position. Tuva became the Tuvan Autonomous Oblast of the Russian SFSR.

w4-900828.name: Ili Rebellion and establishment of the Second East Turkestan Republic (1944)
w4-900828.blurb: The Second East Turkestan Republic, proclaimed on 12 November 1944 amid the Soviet-backed Ili Rebellion, wrested the northern Xinjiang districts of Ili, Tarbagatay and Altay from Republic of China (Nationalist) control. This entry reflects the Nationalist ROC's loss; the ETR existed until incorporation into the PRC in late 1949.

w4-900829.name: Liberation of Denmark and southwestern Norway from Nazi Germany (May 1945)
w4-900829.blurb: Germany occupied Denmark from 9 April 1940. On 4 May 1945 German forces in the Netherlands, northwest Germany, and Denmark surrendered to Montgomery; British troops entered Denmark on 5 May 1945. The coordinates fall in the North Sea / southwestern Norwegian coast, reflecting the simultaneous end of German occupation of these sea and coastal areas at the same surrender.

citations.label: Denmark in World War II — Wikipedia
How Denmark was liberated — The Local

w4-900833.name: Romania switches sides in WWII - reversal of Second Vienna Award (1944-1945)
w4-900833.blurb: On 23 August 1944, King Michael I of Romania staged a coup deposing Ion Antonescu and immediately announced an armistice with the Allies. The subsequent Armistice Agreement (12 September 1944), Article 19, declared the Second Vienna Award (1940) null and void and committed to returning Northern Transylvania to Romania. Soviet and Romanian forces drove out German and Hungarian troops from Northern Transylvania by October 1944, and Romanian administration was restored by March 1945, representing territory reverting from Nazi German/Hungarian control back to Romania.

w4-900836.name: Japanese surrender (1945) — Republic of China restores sovereignty
w4-900836.blurb: Japan's unconditional surrender on 15 August 1945 ended eight years of occupation of large areas of China. The Republic of China, governing in exile from Chongqing, reasserted sovereignty over formerly occupied territories including Manchuria, coastal cities, and the Yangtze valley. The dataset records the Empire of Japan → Republic of China transfer in the 1945–1946 window.

w4-900837.name: Communist takeover and proclamation of People's Republic of Albania
w4-900837.blurb: After the Allied liberation of Albania in 1944 and the communist-dominated National Liberation Movement seizing power, a Constitutional Assembly on 11 January 1946 declared the People's Republic of Albania, deposing King Zog I; a new constitution followed on 14 March 1946. Enver Hoxha consolidated power. The from=Albania / to=People's Socialist Republic of Albania and 1945-1946 window match.

citations.label: People's Socialist Republic of Albania - Wikipedia

w4-900838.name: Japanese surrender in the Dutch East Indies (1945) and Acehnese independence declaration
w4-900838.blurb: Japan surrendered on 15 August 1945, ending the occupation of the Dutch East Indies including Aceh (Sumatra's northernmost province). Indonesian independence was proclaimed on 17 August 1945, and Japanese forces were evacuated from Aceh by mid-December 1945. The Sultanate of Aceh, which had never fully submitted to either the Dutch or the Japanese, reasserted itself in this power vacuum. The data entry (from Empire of Japan to Sultanate of Aceh, py=1945, y=1946) reflects the immediate post-surrender period before Indonesian state authority was consolidated.

citations.label: Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies - Wikipedia

w4-900845.name: Resumption of the Chinese Civil War and CCP territorial gains (1945–1946)
w4-900845.blurb: After Japan's surrender in September 1945 the CCP rapidly expanded its 'Liberated Zones' in northern China, receiving Japanese-captured weapons from Soviet forces in Manchuria. Despite a January 1946 Marshall-brokered ceasefire, full-scale civil war resumed in June 1946 when KMT forces assaulted CCP territory, transferring control of contested zones in the Shaanxi region in this initial phase.

citations.label: Chinese Civil War, 1946–1950 — Wilson Center Digital Archive

w4-900846.type: restoration of sovereignty / end of wartime occupation
w4-900846.name: Liberation of Denmark and restoration of Danish control over Greenland
w4-900846.blurb: Denmark was liberated from German occupation on 5 May 1945, restoring the Danish government's authority. The Danish parliament subsequently ratified the 1941 Kauffmann agreement, and Denmark reasserted sovereignty over Greenland while the US military presence wound down. This falls in the window [1945,1946]; the Truman administration's 1946 attempt to purchase Greenland for $100 million was declined, confirming the island's return to full Danish jurisdiction.

citations.label: Wikipedia: Greenland in World War II
Wikipedia: US attempts to purchase Greenland

w4-900847.name: Post-WWII Australian Administration of Papua New Guinea
w4-900847.blurb: Same administrative reorganization as change 900845: after Japan's 1945 surrender, Australia unified the Territory of Papua and the Territory of New Guinea under a single provisional civil administration, and the atlas reclassifies this territory from British Colonial Empire to the Papua New Guinea administrative entity.

w4-900850.name: French restoration of authority in Indochina after Japanese withdrawal
w4-900850.blurb: After Japan's March 1945 coup removed the Vichy administration and the August 1945 surrender, France reasserted colonial authority, seizing Cochinchina in late 1945 with British help; by April 1946 British and Chinese forces had withdrawn, leaving France in control. The from=Empire of Japan / to=French Indochina and 1945-1946 window match, leading to the First Indochina War.

citations.label: French Indochina in World War II - Wikipedia
Japanese coup d'état in French Indochina - Wikipedia

w4-900851.name: Abolition of the monarchy and proclamation of the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia (1945)
w4-900851.blurb: On 29 November 1945 the Communist-dominated Constituent Assembly deposed King Peter II and proclaimed the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia, abolishing the monarchy; the 1946 Constitution established six federated republics under Tito. The from->to (Yugoslavia -> Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia) at 18.2, 43.8 reflects this constitutional refoundation (the 'Socialist Federal' name was formally adopted in 1963, but the entity is treated as continuous).

citations.label: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia - Wikipedia

w4-900852.name: Italian institutional referendum – abolition of the monarchy
w4-900852.blurb: On 2 June 1946 Italians voted to abolish the monarchy and establish a republic, with about 54% choosing the republic over the Savoy monarchy. King Umberto II left Italy and the Italian Republic was proclaimed, superseding the Kingdom of Italy (1861, House of Savoy). From 'Kingdom of Italy' to 'Republic of Italy'; window py=1945, y=1946 fits.

w4-900854.name: Soviet invasion of Manchuria (Operation August Storm)
w4-900854.blurb: On 9 August 1945, Soviet forces launched a massive three-front offensive against Japanese-held Manchuria, fulfilling Yalta commitments. The Kwantung Army surrendered on 18 August 1945. The USSR occupied Manchuria and adjacent territories including the Pacific littoral (Cliopatria centroid lat 43.9, lng 135.7, the Primorsky/Vladivostok region), with much of Manchukuo's territory transitioning to Soviet/Chinese Communist control, matching the Empire of Japan to USSR transfer in 1945-1946.

w4-900855.name: Papua New Guinea Provisional Administration Act 1945-46
w4-900855.blurb: After the Japanese surrender in September 1945, the Australian Parliament passed the Papua New Guinea Provisional Administration Act (1945-46), abolishing the wartime ANGAU military administration and merging the Territory of Papua (a former British protectorate ceded to Australia in 1906) with the mandated Territory of New Guinea into a single civil administration restored in 1946 under Administrator Jack Keith Murray. The worklist source label 'British Colonial Empire' is a geo-label artifact reflecting Papua's British protectorate origin; the underlying administrative reorganization into the unified Australian-administered territory (with New Guinea a UN trust territory from 1946) is real and in-window (1945-1946).

citations.label: Australian New Guinea Administrative Unit – Wikipedia

w4-900856.name: End of Japanese Occupation of New Guinea; Australian Civil Administration restored
w4-900856.blurb: Japan occupied large parts of New Guinea (Rabaul and the northern coasts) from early 1942. Following Japan's surrender in August 1945, Australian forces completed liberation including the recapture of Rabaul in September 1945. Under the Papua New Guinea Provisional Administration Act 1945–46, Australia restored civil administration and merged its Territory of Papua with the former Mandated Territory of New Guinea into a single administrative union, with the New Guinea half becoming a UN Trust Territory from 1946.

citations.label: Territory of Papua and New Guinea – Wikipedia
Japanese occupation of New Guinea – Wikipedia

w4-900857.name: Papua New Guinea Provisional Administration Act and UN Trust Territory
w4-900857.blurb: Following Japan's surrender, Australia passed the Papua–New Guinea Provisional Administration Act (1945), combining the Territories of Papua and New Guinea under one administration; in December 1946 the UN General Assembly approved a trusteeship agreement for New Guinea under Australian governance. Matches the Commonwealth of Australia → Papua New Guinea relabeling in the 1945-1946 window.

citations.label: Territory of Papua and New Guinea – Wikipedia
Independence of Papua New Guinea – naa.gov.au

w4-900858.name: Japanese surrender (1945) — Dutch East Indies nominally restored
w4-900858.blurb: Japan occupied the Dutch East Indies from early 1942. Following Japan's surrender on 15 August 1945, the Dutch sought to re-establish control, leading to the Indonesian National Revolution (1945–1949). The dataset records the nominal restoration of 'Dutch East Indies' from 'Empire of Japan' in the 1945–1946 window, though Indonesian nationalists declared independence on 17 August 1945.

w4-900859.name: Transfer of western New Guinea from Australian to Dutch administration
w4-900859.blurb: During WWII, Australian forces had liberated and administered parts of Dutch New Guinea (western New Guinea, lng 136.4, lat -4.7) from Japanese occupation. After the Japanese surrender in 1945, the Dutch sought to re-establish their pre-war East Indies administration. By 1946, the Netherlands resumed direct administration of Netherlands New Guinea, while Australia retained the eastern half (Australian-mandated Territory of New Guinea).

w4-900861.name: British Withdrawal from Iran after WWII
w4-900861.blurb: The Anglo-Soviet Tripartite Treaty of January 1942 stipulated that Britain and the USSR would withdraw from Iran within six months of the end of hostilities. British (and US) forces began withdrawing from their southern and central zones in January 1946, completing the handover to Pahlavi-controlled Iran. The dataset records this as 'British Africa → Pahlavi Dynasty' (lng 49.3, lat 33.3, central Iran), where the 'British Africa' from-label is a Cliopatria labeling artifact, but the underlying event is the real British military withdrawal restoring Iranian sovereignty over the occupied zone. The Soviets only withdrew in May 1946 after US and UN pressure.

citations.label: Iran during World War II – Holocaust Encyclopedia (USHMM)

w4-900862.name: Keflavík Agreement — US troop withdrawal from Iceland
w4-900862.blurb: After Iceland declared a republic in June 1944 and World War II ended in 1945, US forces remained despite Icelandic demands for withdrawal. Iceland's Prime Minister Ólafur Thors rejected permanent basing requests and the parties concluded the Keflavík Agreement on 7 October 1946, under which the United States agreed to withdraw all troops within 180 days and return Keflavík Airport to Iceland while retaining operating rights. US forces completed their withdrawal by mid-1947.

citations.label: Iceland in the Cold War – Wikipedia

w4-900864.name: Allied Occupation of Austria and Restoration of the Second Republic
w4-900864.blurb: After the defeat of Nazi Germany, Austria was liberated and divided into four Allied occupation zones (US, UK, USSR, France) from April 1945. The British zone covered Styria, Carinthia, and East Tyrol. A provisional Austrian government was established on 27 April 1945 and internationally recognised in October 1945. Austria remained under Allied occupation until the Austrian State Treaty of 15 May 1955 restored full sovereignty.

w4-900865.name: Allied occupation of Austria - American zone administration
w4-900865.blurb: After Germany's defeat in May 1945, Austria was divided into four Allied occupation zones; the United States occupied Salzburg and Upper Austria south of the Danube (near 12.5E, 47.8N). The Second Control Agreement (28 June 1946) formalised the zonal framework. The dataset's transfer from 'United States of America' to 'Second Republic of Austria' in 1945-1946 reflects the US military occupation transitioning into support for the Austrian provisional government.

citations.label: The U.S. Occupation of Post-WWII Austria - Austria in USA

w4-900866.name: Allied Occupation of Austria - French Zone in Tyrol/Vorarlberg
w4-900866.blurb: After Germany's defeat in May 1945, Austria was divided into four Allied occupation zones; France received Vorarlberg and Tyrol (handed over by the Americans on 10 July 1945). The dataset transfer near lng 11, lat 47.2 (Tyrol/Inn valley) from 'French Fourth Republic' to 'Second Republic of Austria' reflects the co-existence of the restored Austrian state with Allied occupation. Final French withdrawal occurred in October 1955 after the Austrian State Treaty.

w4-900867.from: French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
w4-900867.name: French withdrawal from Syria - end of the French Mandate
w4-900867.blurb: Although Syria had been recognized as an independent republic in 1941 (when the Free French proclaimed it), French troops remained present and effective control was contested. Under sustained diplomatic pressure from Britain, the United States, and the nascent UN, France completed the evacuation of its forces from Syria in April 1946, transferring full territorial sovereignty to the Syrian Arab Republic (here labeled 'Second Syrian Republic').

citations.label: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon - Wikipedia

w4-900868.name: Soviet occupation and establishment of the Republic of Hungary (1946)
w4-900868.blurb: After Soviet forces occupied Hungary at the end of WWII (1944-1945), the Hungarian monarchy was abolished on 1 February 1946, creating the Second Hungarian Republic. This data entry reflects territory transitioning from Soviet (USSR) administrative control to the nominal sovereignty of the new Hungarian state - though Soviet occupation troops remained and the Communist Party steadily consolidated power through 'salami tactics' toward the 1949 People's Republic.

w4-900870.name: British-American Bizone reorganization in occupied Germany
w4-900870.blurb: The coordinates point to north-central Germany. The data entry shows the United Kingdom passing territory to the United States between 1946 and 1947 - this corresponds to the creation of the British-American 'Bizone' on 1 January 1947, when Britain merged its occupation zone in Germany with the American zone for economic administration. This represents a rearrangement of Allied occupation responsibilities rather than a true sovereignty transfer.

w4-900871.name: Treaty of Paris (1947) — Bulgaria
w4-900871.blurb: The Treaty of Paris signed on 10 February 1947 formally ended WWII hostilities with Bulgaria and restored formal Bulgarian sovereignty, confirming Southern Dobruja as Bulgarian territory. This ended the Allied (Soviet-led) occupation regime that had governed Bulgaria since September 1944; occupation forces were to withdraw upon the treaty's entry into force on 15 September 1947. The monarchy had been abolished by referendum in September 1946 and the People's Republic of Bulgaria was formally proclaimed, so this Cliopatria entry spanning 1946-1947 straddles the monarchy's abolition and the Paris peace settlement that recognised the new Bulgarian state.

w4-900873.name: Chinese Civil War — CCP Advances in Hebei
w4-900873.blurb: After the KMT-CCP truce broke down in June 1946, full-scale civil war resumed. By 1947 the Communist Party of China had built substantial control across northern China, including Hebei province (114.3E, 38.6N), through guerrilla operations, land reform mobilization, and exploiting Nationalist overextension, steadily consolidating territory throughout 1947.

w4-900875.name: Dutch First Police Action (Operation Product)
w4-900875.blurb: After Indonesia's August 1945 independence declaration, the Netherlands launched 'Operation Product' on 21 July 1947, a full-scale offensive of nearly 100,000 troops. Dutch forces retook much of Java and Sumatra (~106E 2S), reducing the Republic to a rump around Yogyakarta. UN pressure forced a ceasefire and the January 1948 Renville Agreement. Correctly dated within the 1946-1947 window.

w4-900876.name: Philippine Independence – Treaty of Manila (1946)
w4-900876.blurb: The United States formally recognized Philippine independence on July 4, 1946, when President Harry Truman issued a proclamation and both nations signed the Treaty of General Relations (Treaty of Manila). The treaty renounced all US claims to the Philippine Islands, transferring sovereignty from the United States to the Republic of the Philippines. The path to independence had been set by the Tydings-McDuffie Act of 1934, which established the Commonwealth of the Philippines with a ten-year transition period; WWII delayed but did not derail this process. The dataset window of 1946–1947 (United States of America → Republic of the Philippines) reflects the transfer of sovereignty and the subsequent establishment of full Philippine governmental functions.

citations.label: July 4, 1946: The Philippines Gained Independence – National WWII Museum

w4-900878.name: Statute of Westminster Adoption Act 1947 (New Zealand)
w4-900878.blurb: On 25 November 1947 New Zealand's Parliament received royal assent for the Statute of Westminster Adoption Act, formally adopting sections 2-6 of the British Statute of Westminster 1931 (which New Zealand had earlier declined to accept out of loyalty to Britain). This repealed the Colonial Laws Validity Act 1865 as it applied to New Zealand and barred the UK Parliament from legislating for New Zealand without its consent. New Zealand was already a self-governing Dominion, so this was a constitutional formalization of legislative autonomy rather than a transfer of territorial sovereignty; full constitutional independence was completed only by the Constitution Act 1986.

citations.label: Wikipedia: Statute of Westminster Adoption Act 1947
New Zealand History — Constitutional history: Statute of Westminster (NZ Ministry for Culture and Heritage)

w4-900885.name: Transjordan gains independence as the Hashemite Kingdom
w4-900885.blurb: The Treaty of London (22 March 1946) and the proclamation of Emir Abdullah as King (25 May 1946) ended the British Mandate, creating the Hashemite Kingdom of Transjordan. Matches the recorded British Colonial Empire→Kingdom of Jordan transfer at lng 37.1, lat 31.2 in the 1946–1947 window.

w4-900887.name: Indian Independence Act 1947 — Hyderabad State independent
w4-900887.blurb: Under the Indian Independence Act 1947 (effective 15 August 1947), British paramountcy lapsed and the Nizam of Hyderabad declared independence, refusing to accede to India or Pakistan. Hyderabad (78.1,18.2) thus briefly existed as an independent state before India annexed it in 1948, matching the from→to (British Raj → Hyderabad State) in the 1946–1947 window.

w4-900888.name: Constitution of the Kingdom of Laos (1947)
w4-900888.blurb: Following France's reassertion of control over Laos in 1946, a constituent assembly drafted a constitution promulgated by King Sisavang Vong on 11 May 1947, formally establishing the Kingdom of Laos as a constitutional monarchy and autonomous state within the French Union, replacing the direct structure of French Indochina over the ~238,285 km2 Laotian territory. Transfer French Indochina -> Kingdom of Laos fits the 1946-1947 window.

w4-900890.name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1947-1948 over Kashmir
w4-900890.blurb: After partition in August 1947, Pakistani-backed tribal lashkars invaded Jammu and Kashmir on 22 October 1947; Maharaja Hari Singh acceded to India on 26 October. The war ended with a UN ceasefire on 1 January 1949, leaving Pakistan in control of roughly one-third of the former princely state (Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan). The worklist transition is 'Kashmir and Jammu' -> 'Islamic Republic of Pakistan' [1947,1948] at lng 74.9, lat 34.7 (northern Kashmir / Gilgit region, the Pakistan-controlled portion), with 1947 inside the window.

w4-900891.name: Proclamation of the People's Republic of Bulgaria
w4-900891.blurb: After the monarchy was abolished by referendum in September 1946, the Grand National Assembly adopted the 'Dimitrov Constitution' on 4 December 1947, modelled on the Soviet constitution of 1936, formally establishing the People's Republic of Bulgaria under the Bulgarian Communist Party. Opposition leaders including Nikola Petkov were arrested and executed in 1947. By 1948 the communists had liquidated all rival political parties, nationalised industry, and established unchallenged one-party rule backed by Soviet occupation forces.

w4-900892.name: Proclamation of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea
w4-900892.blurb: Following the division of Korea at the 38th parallel, the Soviet-administered north developed separately, and on 9 September 1948 Kim Il-sung proclaimed the Democratic People's Republic of Korea in Pyongyang over the northern ~215,000 km2. The coordinates (127.6E, 38.6N) fit the peninsula. Transfer (Soviet zone/USSR) -> DPRK fits the 1947-1948 window.

w4-900893.name: Ceylon Independence Act — Dominion of Ceylon
w4-900893.blurb: The Ceylon Independence Act came into force on 4 February 1948, when the Dominion of Ceylon (modern Sri Lanka, 80.8,7.9) became self-governing within the Commonwealth, separate from British India. This matches the from→to (British Raj → Sri Lanka) in the 1947–1948 window.

w4-900894.name: Instrument of Accession of Jammu and Kashmir to India; First Kashmir War
w4-900894.blurb: Following the British partition of India in August 1947, Maharaja Hari Singh of Jammu and Kashmir sought independence but was forced to seek Indian military aid when Pakistan-backed Pashtun tribal militias invaded on 22 October 1947. Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession to India on 26 October 1947, and Indian troops airlifted to Srinagar repelled the invasion. The subsequent First Kashmir War (1947–1949) ended with a UN ceasefire, leaving India controlling roughly two-thirds of the territory.

citations.label: Instrument of Accession (Jammu and Kashmir) – Wikipedia

w4-900895.name: Indian Annexation of Hyderabad (Operation Polo)
w4-900895.blurb: The Nizam of Hyderabad, Mir Osman Ali Khan, refused to accede to India after 1947. On 13-18 September 1948 the Indian Army launched Operation Polo, defeating the Hyderabad State forces in five days and incorporating Hyderabad (~211,946 km2) into the Republic of India under Sardar Patel. Transfer Hyderabad State -> Republic of India fits the 1947-1948 window.

w4-900896.name: Romanian Communist Takeover and Abolition of the Monarchy
w4-900896.blurb: On 30 December 1947 King Michael I of Romania was forced to abdicate by the communist-controlled government under Petru Groza, backed by Soviet pressure. The Kingdom of Romania was abolished and replaced by the Romanian People's Republic (the dataset's 'Socialist Republic of Romania' label is the later name of the same communist state). Fits the 1947-1948 window over ~234,485 km2.

w4-900900.name: Burmese independence from the British Raj
w4-900900.blurb: The Burma Independence Act 1947 received royal assent on 10 December 1947, and Burma became a fully independent republic on 4 January 1948, with Sao Shwe Thaik as president and U Nu as prime minister. Matches worklist transition British Raj -> Burma (1947-1948); coords lng 96.6 lat 19.3 confirm Burma.

w4-900901.name: PLA entry into Xinjiang and incorporation of the East Turkestan Republic into the PRC
w4-900901.blurb: In August 1949 most ETR leaders died in a Soviet plane crash en route to attend the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference in Beijing; remaining ETR leaders accepted CCP authority and the PLA entered Xinjiang in October 1949, peacefully incorporating the ETR's territory into the newly proclaimed People's Republic of China.

w4-900902.name: Chinese Civil War: Communist Liaoshen Campaign in Manchuria
w4-900902.blurb: The Liaoshen Campaign (12 September – 2 November 1948) was the first of three decisive PLA offensives. Under Lin Biao, PLA forces captured Jinzhou (15 October), Changchun (20 October), and Shenyang (2 November), giving the Communists full control of Manchuria and its industries. Matches the Republic of China → Communist Party of China transfer in the 1947-1948 window.

w4-900906.name: Chinese Communist Revolution — Huaihai and Pingjin Campaigns
w4-900906.blurb: The decisive phase of the Chinese Civil War saw the People's Liberation Army (PLA) defeat Nationalist (KMT) forces in three major campaigns: the Liaoshen Campaign (September-November 1948), the Huaihai Campaign (November 1948-January 1949, east-central China), and the Pingjin Campaign (November 1948-January 1949, northern China including Beijing). The KMT government fell back to Taiwan, and Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China on 1 October 1949, completing the Communist takeover of mainland China.

w4-900907.name: Newfoundland joins Canada (31 March 1949)
w4-900907.blurb: On 8 August 1949 India and Bhutan signed the Treaty of Perpetual Peace and Friendship at Darjeeling, regularizing relations after the end of British paramountcy in India. Under the treaty India agreed to return about 32 square miles of territory in the Dewangiri area to Bhutan, while Bhutan agreed to be guided by India in its external relations in exchange for India's non-interference in Bhutan's internal administration. It was the first treaty Bhutan's Druk Gyalpo signed as a sovereign monarch.

w4-900908.name: Founding of the German Democratic Republic
w4-900908.blurb: On 7 October 1949 the Soviet occupation zone of Germany was converted into the German Democratic Republic, a separate East German state under the Socialist Unity Party (SED). The GDR was formally established in response to the founding of the Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany) in May 1949. Soviet military forces remained in East Germany until 1994, and the GDR was effectively a Soviet satellite state. West Germany considered it illegitimate until normalisation in the early 1970s through Ostpolitik.

citations.label: Soviet occupation zone in Germany – Wikipedia

w4-900909.name: Dutch transfer of the East Indies to Indonesia excluding Netherlands New Guinea
w4-900909.blurb: Under the 1949 Round Table Conference, the Netherlands transferred sovereignty over the Dutch East Indies to Indonesia on 27 December 1949, retaining Netherlands New Guinea as a separate territory. The Dutch East Indies-to-Netherlands New Guinea split (-4.5N) is within the window (1948-1949).

w4-900910.name: Chinese Communist Revolution — proclamation of the People's Republic of China
w4-900910.blurb: On 1 October 1949, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China from Tiananmen Square, following the Chinese Communist Party's decisive military victories over the Kuomintang in the Chinese Civil War. Chiang Kai-shek's Republic of China government retreated to Taiwan by the end of 1949. The PRC assumed administrative control over mainland China, with remaining KMT pockets on Hainan and other islands eliminated by mid-1950.

citations.label: Proclamation of the People's Republic of China – Wikipedia

w4-900911.name: Chinese Communist Revolution — CPC-held northeast territories incorporated into PRC
w4-900911.blurb: The territories in northeastern China (Manchuria) that the Chinese Communist Party had controlled since the Liaoshen Campaign of 1948 were formally incorporated into the People's Republic of China upon its proclamation on 1 October 1949. The CPC's Northeast Democratic Allied Army had seized Manchuria from Kuomintang forces with Soviet assistance after Japan's 1945 defeat; these areas were already governed by CPC organs and transitioned seamlessly into the new PRC administrative structure. The dataset records this as a distinct transfer from 'Communist Party of China' to the 'People's Republic of China' entity.

citations.label: History of the People's Republic of China – Wikipedia

w4-900912.name: PLA incorporation of the East Turkestan Republic into the PRC (1949)
w4-900912.blurb: Following the Communist victory in the Chinese Civil War, the PLA entered Xinjiang in October 1949. ETR leaders agreed to dissolve the republic, which was formally abolished on 22 December 1949 and its army merged into the PLA. The from->to (East Turkestan Republic -> People's Republic of China) in the 1949-1950 window matches this annexation.

w4-900913.name: Establishment of the Federal Republic of Germany
w4-900913.blurb: The Federal Republic of Germany was established on 23 May 1949 when the Basic Law came into force, converting the US, British, and French occupation zones into a semi-sovereign German state. US military governors were replaced by civilian high commissioners, marking the transfer of de facto governmental authority over western Germany from American occupation to the new FRG, though full sovereignty was not achieved until 1955. The coordinates (~9.9E, 51.2N = central West Germany) reflect the western occupation zone.

w4-900914.name: Saar Protectorate: transition from French administration toward the Federal Republic of Germany
w4-900914.blurb: After World War II, France established the Saar Protectorate (1947) as a de facto separate entity with a customs union with France. The formation of the Federal Republic of Germany in May 1949 created a framework in which the Saar's status was contested, leading to its formal reintegration into West Germany on 1 January 1957 after the 1955 referendum. The worklist transfer French Fourth Republic → Federal Republic of Germany at lng 8.1, lat 49.3 in the 1949–1950 window reflects the start of this transition.

w4-900915.name: Indonesian National Revolution: Dutch recognition of Indonesian sovereignty
w4-900915.blurb: After four years of armed struggle and diplomatic pressure, the Dutch signed the Round Table Conference agreements at The Hague. Queen Juliana transferred sovereignty on 27 December 1949, creating the Republic of the United States of Indonesia (Cliopatria centroid lat -3.2, lng 118.3, central Indonesia). On 17 August 1950 it was reorganized as the unitary Republic of Indonesia, matching the Dutch East Indies to Republic of Indonesia transfer in 1949-1950.

w4-900916.name: Indonesian Independence - West Timor Incorporated into Republic of Indonesia
w4-900916.blurb: The Netherlands formally recognised Indonesian independence in December 1949, dissolving the Dutch East Indies. West Timor became part of the new Republic of Indonesia, while Portugal continued to hold East Timor. The dataset's 'from' label 'Estado Novo' is a Cliopatria mislabel for the Dutch-controlled western half of Timor; the underlying transfer of West Timor to Indonesia in 1949-1950 is attested.

w4-900917.name: Indonesian independence and incorporation of Aceh (1949-1950)
w4-900917.blurb: The Netherlands recognised Indonesian sovereignty in December 1949 after the Indonesian National Revolution. Aceh was incorporated into the new Republic of Indonesia as part of North Sumatra Province, over the objections of Acehnese leaders who had expected special autonomous status. By early 1950 Republican administration had been extended across the province. The data entry (Sultanate of Aceh to Republic of Indonesia, py=1949, y=1950) represents this transition.

w4-900918.name: Indo-Bhutan Treaty of Friendship and return of Dewangiri
w4-900918.blurb: The Indo-Bhutan Treaty of Friendship signed on 8 August 1949 at Darjeeling committed India to return approximately 32 square miles of Dewangiri territory (lost to Britain in the 1865 Treaty of Sinchula) to Bhutan, formalised through India's Assam (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1951, with demarcation in the early 1950s. The from=Kingdom of Bhutan / to=Republic of India direction is inverted relative to the cession but the 1950-1953 window aligns with phased implementation of the handover.

citations.label: Treaty of Friendship between India and Bhutan - Refworld

w4-900919.name: UN Resolution 390A — Eritrea-Ethiopia Federation
w4-900919.blurb: UN General Assembly Resolution 390A (V) of December 2, 1950, ended British administration of Eritrea (coords 38.6E/13.2N) and created a federation with Ethiopia under Emperor Haile Selassie, effective September 15, 1952. Britain had administered Eritrea since 1941. The dataset's [py=1950, y=1953] window from 'British Africa' to 'Ethiopia' matches the resolution and federation's implementation.

citations.label: Federation of Ethiopia and Eritrea – Wikipedia

w4-900920.name: Darul Islam Rebellion in Aceh (1953)
w4-900920.blurb: Disappointed with Jakarta's failure to grant Aceh special autonomy and its merger into the North Sumatra province, Aceh's military governor Teungku Daud Beureueh pledged allegiance to the Negara Islam Indonesia on 21 September 1953, launching the Darul Islam insurgency. Rebels controlled large rural areas of Aceh beyond Indonesian government reach, effectively reasserting an autonomous or rebel-controlled zone associated with the Acehnese political identity. The data entry (Republic of Indonesia to Sultanate of Aceh, py=1950, y=1953) reflects this insurgent counter-claim over territory.

w4-900923.name: Egyptian Revolution of 1952 — Kingdom of Egypt becomes Republic of Egypt
w4-900923.blurb: On 23 July 1952 the Free Officers Movement under Naguib and Nasser overthrew King Farouk, who abdicated. The Revolutionary Command Council abolished the monarchy on 18 June 1953 and declared the Republic of Egypt with Naguib as first president. The dataset records this as a 1950–1953 transition.

w4-900924.name: Chinese Civil War Conclusion — PRC Consolidation of the Mainland
w4-900924.blurb: After the People's Republic of China was proclaimed on 1 October 1949, the PRC spent 1950–1953 consolidating control over remaining pockets of Republic of China (Nationalist) territory on the mainland.
